body:
## What this is

A DIAGNOSTIC probe, not the fix. It belongs to dashboard node `adhoc-afb0f800-78c` ("nominal type-application child edges carry declared-parameter labels on both sides"), the lowering fix that #15868's site-6 arm is pinned on.

`v2.std.exact_structural_equality_zip_fold_predicate`'s descent (the verdict arm #15868 adds) decides a child pair by its `Edge` label before its target. If the two producers of a nominal application -- the declared position's annotation and the produced position's inferred type -- disagree about those labels, every nominal mismatch decides at argument index `[0]` as `arguments_differ` and never descends into the argument types: a lowering mismatch reported as a type mismatch (DESIGN §5).

## Why CI is the instrument

No local compiler run is permitted for this node, so the measurement is the corpus: every cell is a whole module read through the real resolver and `infer`, and each asks exactly one question.

| cell | program | asks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nal_identical_concrete_nominal_application_is_accepted_holds` | `fn nal_take(p: Pair<Int, String>) -> Pair<Int, String>` | are the two sides of ONE application structurally identical at all, labels included? |
| `nal_differing_concrete_nominal_application_refuses_holds` | `Pair<Int, String>` vs `Pair<Int, Int>` | does a concrete mismatch refuse |
| `nal_identical_generic_nominal_application_is_accepted_holds` | `<K> Pair<K, String>` vs `Pair<K, String>` | the generic control |
| `nal_differing_generic_nominal_application_refuses_holds` | `<K> Pair<K, String>` vs `Pair<K, Int>` | the site-6 shape |
| `nal_identical_alias_application_is_accepted_holds` | `List<Int>` vs `List<Int>` (`List<e> = FreeMonoid<e>`, a body with NO member labels) | separates "alias unfolding" from "product member labels" |
| `nal_differing_alias_application_refuses_holds` | `List<Int>` vs `List<String>` | same, mismatching |
| `nal_nested_second_argument_disagreement_refuses_holds` | `<K> Pair<List<K>, String>` vs `Pair<List<K>, Int>` | the nested-ordinal cell |

`Pair` is `type Pair<A, B> = Mk { first: A, second: B }` -- its body members are exactly the `first`/`second` structural labels the site-6 measurement named; `List` is an alias whose body carries none. Pair-vs-List is the discriminator between "any alias unfolds with member labels" and "a product body's member labels are what split the sides".

## Reading the result

A cell RED where it is written ACCEPT means the two producers do not agree on the node (the mismatch, confirmed); a cell RED where it is written REFUSE means the judge refused for a reason other than the one named. The implementation PR replaces the reds with the truth and carries the RFM row; this PR may be closed once the measurement is read.
title: DO NOT MERGE (measurement): nominal application child Edge labels on the two sides

## NOT ACCEPTED

**Read this first, before the diff.**

- **NOT ACCEPTED.** This is a durable review head, not an acceptance event. Dashboard node `v2-emitter-direct-rust-door` stays **NOT ACCEPTED**.
- **The witnesses are unexecuted.** Nothing in this branch has been built, run, or dispatched — no claim batch, no host run, nothing through the build runner. Verification so far is source reading only, and no green is claimed here.
- **A v2-bootstrap green does NOT establish that the witnesses resolve.** Per DESIGN, section *"What a green v2-bootstrap does not say"*: the bootstrap suite exercises the compiler pipeline, not the witness claims and their realization pairing. If CI on this branch goes green, that says nothing about whether these witnesses resolve, whether their floor is satisfiable, or whether the capabilities they use are paired with a host realization. Do not read CI green as witness resolution.
- **(d) and the landed-head receipt are outstanding.** Witness (d), the generator-removal control, exists only as a design draft (comment [6709770916](https://github.com/gunb-ai/gunbc/pull/15969#issuecomment-6709770916)), its cost is over the granted booking and is stated as over, and its budget question is unchosen and with keen-otter. The GAP 2 receipt at a landed head is also outstanding (it needs a keen-otter grant; srv1 is suspended).

**Review material** — the full delta with its extraction rule and verification commands: comment [6709724150](https://github.com/gunb-ai/gunbc/pull/15969#issuecomment-6709724150). The (d) v3 design: comment [6709770916](https://github.com/gunb-ai/gunbc/pull/15969#issuecomment-6709770916).

## What this changes

GAP 1 of the `direct-rust-door` acceptance (recorder return msg_35851162, static reads at `34869d80`). The execution contract of roadmap node `v2-emitter-direct-rust-door` named `direct_rust_door_production_group_closing_expectation_holds` — the in-memory walk the operator's 2026-10-12 acceptance review refused — and named **none** of the written-route obligations. It now binds the written route.

**One authority.** The contract binds the five claims of `v2.test.claim.direct_rust_door_written_compile_wet` over **one** entry via `gunbc_claims_execution_contract`: the four obligations the 2026-10-12 review named, plus the control paired with the read-back leg. Chosen over making the closing function execute them, because a test may not call another test — that route can only mean *copying* their assertions into a second file, which mints a second authority in the one file whose own header allows a single test function (every function there pays the whole production walk), and it would hang `Filesystem.Write` plus a rustc subprocess on a row whose floor is hermetic.

**Demoted, not deleted.** `direct_rust_door_production_group_closing_expectation_holds` still exists and still executes, as regression evidence over the in-memory group. It closes nothing: the contract no longer names it. Deleting the function would have destroyed an executing integration receipt to remove an authority.

**Witness.** `witness_v2_emitter_direct_rust_door_has_discriminating_contract` is now a set identity over the bound set — every binding in the set, every member bound, nothing bound twice. The closing set is deliberately written in **two** files: the witness is an independent check, and a check that read the very list it verifies would verify nothing.

**Witness (c).** `written_compile_holds` now reads the file named by the write receipt back over `Filesystem.Read`, by the pattern `written_refusal_reason_receipt_read` uses, and requires the bytes on disk to equal `direct_rust_door_expected_source`. Its paired control re-spells one token class: the target still writes and still compiles, and the claim refuses it **for the bytes**. Both halves are asserted, so the control cannot pass on an inert plant. The plant goes through `rust_target_model_with_lex`, so it is the production target field-for-field except the lex, and the override is **prepended** because the first rule met for a token class wins — appended, it would be dead code and the control would measure nothing.

**Unchanged on purpose.** `dag/gunbc/rung_drop/transitional_admission_exception.dag` — its exception covers the in-memory row's admission cadence, that row still exists, and the written claims add no admission rows. `extra_capabilities` stays **empty**: these claims shell out to rustc and write under `target/`, and minting a capability with no observable host realization is the DESIGN §3 pairing violation, so it belongs with GAP 2 where the host is named.

## Files

`dag/gunbc/roadmap/roadmap_authority.dag`, `dag/test/claim/roadmap/roadmap_authority.dag`, `src/v2/compiler/self_host/direct_rust_door_fixture.dag`, `src/v2/compiler/self_host/direct_rust_door_written_compile.dag`, `src/v2/extdeps/languages/rust.dag`, `src/v2/test/claim/direct_rust_door_written_compile_wet.dag`, `src/v2/test/claim/long/direct_rust_door_production_group.dag` — 7 files, +265 / −41.

Identity: head `48c83343ddb16d67a470e43cb3cbaeeef52f2385`, parent `9b25e1c7ab121b3c181b23689fda473d253cc4f7`, tree `d5895ad9c86233d4713e4ef1093e2df13443b14a`.

## What was NOT verified

No build, no claim batch, no host run, nothing through the build runner — none was granted. Four things to read rather than trust:

1. The lex override is really the leg that spells the body's plus. The emission chain is source-checked: `target_value_expression_to_concrete_tokens` → `target_value_expression_primitive_apply_to_concrete_tokens` → `target_operator_realization_catalog_lookup` → `target_operator_shape_emit_primitive_apply_tokens`, whose `InfixToken` arm emits `FixedToken { token_class: ^rust_token_plus }`, spelled later by `token_text_from_decoded` through `lex_literal_indexed`. The **scanning** direction was not traced end-to-end; if that premise is wrong the new control fails at its first half rather than passing quietly.
2. The new fixture imports are the ones the plant needs.
3. The fifth member of the bound set appears in **both** `roadmap_authority` files.
4. `extra_capabilities` is empty deliberately, for the pairing reason above.

> **Stacked logically on #16040** (it contains #16040's commit `771aa83f`; once #16040 lands, the diff is this PR's own). It targets main. Source only; nothing was run.
>
> **BLOCKER, stated (tidy-ant-251 msg_870db9ee (2), caveat):** this adds a `std.primitive_projection` row (`primitive_substring`). Its stage0 mirror `src/v1/stage0/src/std_primitive_projection.rs` must be regenerated by heal and published by `gunbc.heal_publisher_workflow`, and main's publisher currently refuses its own entry (#15992; observed as run 42371786252 on #15892). Until that mirror lands, the seed's `rust_seam_primitive_name` has no row for `std.host_text substring`, so v2-bootstrap is expected to red with an "unrealized host seam" for it. That is the same one-regen-round state #15164 has for `map_keys`. This PR ships the declaration and the respell anyway, as the ruling directs.

## 1. `substring`'s home: `std.host_text` (ruling msg_870db9ee (2))

```
fn substring(text: HostText, start: Nat, end: Nat) -> HostText
```
It sits beside `string_length` and `char_at`: the host-text layer and the F5 family. The semantics are `src/v1/runtime_rust.dag` `v1_rt::substring`'s, stated EXACTLY and **not changed**:
- positions are Unicode-scalar (code-point) positions;
- `end <= start` gives the empty text;
- `start` at or past the scalar count gives the empty text;
- `end` past the count is clamped to the count;
- a negative position clamps to 0 in the realization, but that input has no spelling here because the positions are `Nat`, exactly as for `char_at`'s `pos`.

There is no absence arm: an empty window is a window. This follows the host-seam pattern of `string_length`:
- the `HostRealizedSeam` row `primitive_projection_row(primitive: primitive_substring, module_path: "std.host_text", decl_name: "substring", fidelity: HostRealizedSeam)`;
- a **dead fold body** until that row is on main (a self-call would emit as bare Rust recursion in heal round 1, the #15507 trap);
- the trigger, stated on the declaration: once the row is on main, the body becomes the self-call. The body's quadratic cost is stated on the declaration too; no call reaches it.

## 2. `LexWalkUntil.scalars` is a Nat count (ruling B, msg_0bfbd861)

A count cannot be negative, so `Int` was the earliest unjustified boundary (DESIGN §6b), and the `n < 0` arm existed only because the type permitted an impossible state (§5).

**`v2.compiler.tokenize`:**
- before: `| LexWalkUntil { scalars: Int }`; after: `| LexWalkUntil { scalars: Nat }`
- `lex_window` before (main plus #16040):
  ```
  if (string_length(text: substring(s: text, start: 0, end: n + 1)) as Int) > n {
    LexWindow { text: substring(s: text, start: 0, end: if n < 0 { 0 } else { n }), truncated: true }
  ```
- after:
  ```
  if string_length(text: substring(text: text, start: 0, end: nat_add(a: n, b: 1))) > n {
    LexWindow { text: substring(text: text, start: 0, end: n), truncated: true }
  ```
  The `n < 0` arm is deleted. `#16040`'s `as Int` is no longer needed: the comparison is Nat against Nat. The `+ 1` is `std.nat` `nat_add`, because `n + 1` would type as Int under #15610's both-operand rule. The imports are `std.host_text { string_length, substring }` and `std.nat { Nat, nat_add }`. `std.nat` is already in tokenize's closure, so **no module is added**.

**Producers, followed** (`v2.compiler.module_header`). Production never yields a negative window: it starts at `module_header_first_window` (256), `module_header_read_from` refuses `< 1`, and the window only doubles. tidy-ant-251 ruled that this is the evidence for Nat (msg_31998a49). Changes:
- `module_header_first_window() -> Int { 256 }` becomes `-> Nat { 256 }`;
- `module_header_read_from(..., window: Int)` becomes `window: Nat`, and its refusal `if window < 1` becomes `if window == 0`, with the same refusal text. 0 is the only Nat it ever refused;
- `module_header_read_window(..., window: Int)` becomes `window: Nat`;
- the doubling `window * 2` (two sites) becomes `nat_add(a: window, b: window)`.

## 3. The claim files: what changed in each, and the rung climb

The expectations change in **form, not meaning**.

**A rung climb (DESIGN §4b).** "A negative window" becomes STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE (rung 4). The lower-rung machinery is deleted (the `n < 0` arm, and module_header's `< 1` answering negatives). **The discriminating RED is moved, not deleted.** Each negative conjunct is replaced by a fixture SOURCE that writes the negative window where Nat is required, and is refused at the type boundary. The harness is the corpus's existing fixture-source refusal pattern, `v2.test.claim.compiler.literal_elaboration` `lel_reason`: it assembles fixture source against a `std.nat` peer and runs infer. The pinned reason `infer_reason_literal_outside_kernel_grounding_range` is the one `lel_negative_literal_at_nat_refuses` already pins for `-1` at Nat. Each RED carries a positive control: the same source with a non-negative count is `^accepted`.

- **`src/v2/test/claim/module_header.dag`:**
  - `header_from(..., window: Int)` becomes `Nat`; `sweep_last() -> Int { 40 }` becomes `-> Nat { 40 }`; `window + 1` becomes `nat_add(a: window, b: 1)` (2 sites); the import `std.nat { Nat, nat_add }` is added.
  - `a_first_window_that_holds_no_scalar_is_refused`: the conjunct `header_from(..., window: -4) == "refused"` is **removed**, and the `window: 0` conjunct stays as it is.
  - New `a_negative_first_window_is_refused_at_the_nat_boundary`: `read_from(window: -4)` at a `Nat` formal refuses with the range reason; `window: 4` is accepted.
- **`src/v2/test/claim/tokenize/lex_window_beyond.dag`:**
  - The `window: Int` params (7 helpers) become `Nat`; the import `std.nat` is added.
  - `a_window_is_the_whole_text_exactly_when_it_holds_all_of_it`: the conjunct `!dag_prefix_complete(text: "module a.b\n", window: -3)` is **removed**, and its comment clause "a negative window holds nothing" is replaced by a pointer to the RED. The `window: 0` and `window: 5` conjuncts are unchanged.
  - New `a_negative_window_is_refused_at_the_nat_boundary`: `Until { scalars: -3 }` in a record field of LexWalkUntil's shape refuses with the range reason; `scalars: 3` is accepted.
- **`src/v2/test/claim/tokenize/lex_prefix_door.dag`:**
  - `window: Int` params become `Nat`; `sweep_last() -> Int { 60 }` becomes `-> Nat { 60 }`; `window + 1` becomes `nat_add(a: window, b: 1)` (5 sites); the import is added.
  - No literal changed: its windows are 0 and positive (`window: 0` at 169 and 216-217 stays as is).
- The claims' own `cut_of` / `modal_cut_*` helpers still call the ambient `substring(s:, ..., end: window)`. A Nat reaching an Int formal is the declared implicit-safe injection. These sites are listed for the namespace wave and are not respelled here.

## 4. `any` at `lex_first_admits` (ruling msg_870db9ee (3))

No new name. It goes through the existing `std.algebra` `fold_list`, which tokenize already imports:
```
-    || any(xs: first.classes, predicate: fn(k) { char_in_class(c: c, class: k) })
+    || fold_list(xs: first.classes, empty: false, cons: fn(acc, k) { acc || char_in_class(c: c, class: k) })
```
The answer is the same disjunction. The fold visits every class, but `acc || …` skips `char_in_class` once one class has admitted, so after the first hit each step is one boolean read.

## Stated unknowns
- **Text identity** (ruling (5)): tokenize's `String` is `v2.std.text` (structural) while `std.host_text` `substring` and `string_length` take `HostText`. This stays **UNKNOWN** under `gunbc.rung_drop.text_boundary_identity_wall`, with no cast added.
- **The pinned reason is derived from source, not executed.** If the record-field position judges a literal through a different refusal, the RED fails visibly rather than greening.

## Controls (source-only, as #16040)
- **Resolve positive:** `lex_window`'s `string_length` and `substring` bind to `std.host_text`.
- **Inversion:** remove `substring` from `import std.host_text { string_length, substring }` and the `substring` occurrences refuse with `resolve_reason_unbound_symbol`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
title: std.host_text substring home; LexWalkUntil.scalars is a Nat count (negative-window RED moved to the type boundary); any via fold_list

## What
Moves one `CliDispatchHost` body (`invoke_bound_target_producer`, the `gunbc test` verb) behind an emitted boundary.

- `05_emit_rust.dag` renders the `CliInvokesBoundTargetProducer` arm itself: run the bound producer (`test_verb_checked`, still the host kernel), take the status from the emitted `gunbc.target_invocation` `invocation_exit_status`, then call one generic host method `end_process_with_verdict`.
- `gunbc.target_invocation_termination` (a new leaf holding the MOVED `InvocationTermination` and `invocation_exit_status`, plus `bound_target_producer_status_declaration`) is admitted into the seed's emitted closure by the emitter importing it. `gunbc.target_invocation` and its registry/extdeps.bazel imports stay out; it imports the names back from the leaf (move, not copy: one authority).
- Deleted: the Rust `Termination` enum, the Rust `invocation_exit_status` table, the `invoke_bound_target_producer` body and the `RetainedCommands::Test` arm. The producer outcome is now typed `InvocationTermination`.
- Divergence row `reason`, `bootstrap_operation_seed_growth` and `target_invocation_seed_growth` updated.

## Consumer and route
`gunbc test <label>` -> generated `dispatch` Test arm -> `test_verb_checked` -> `InvocationTermination` -> emitted `invocation_exit_status` -> `end_process_with_verdict` (main.rs, unchanged `Verdict::apply`).

## Control
`the_test_arms_status_is_the_emitted_table` (target_invocation_host tests) calls the emitted function for all four terminations (Refused and SubjectUnreached both 2). Altering the .dag table, then regenerating the mirror, turns it red. The existing .dag claims in `target_invocation_witness.dag` still pin the table itself.

## Generated mirrors
Not generated locally (no seed run, per limits). `gunbc_target_invocation.rs`, `lib.rs` module line, `v1_compiler_emit_rust.rs` and `gunbc_cli_dispatch_generated.rs` are expected from the PR's heal job. Until it converges, this branch does not compile. If heal fails, the first failing step is reported below.

## Still retained (a MOVE not applicable; nothing relocated)
`Verdict::apply`, `print_invocation_receipt`, `end_process_without_teardown` stay in main.rs, now reached via `end_process_with_verdict`. Not retired. **Missing fact: a modeled process-termination carrier ("print the receipt, then end without teardown").** Per tidy-ant-251 the homes to extend are `std.compiler_entry` `NativeClaimTerminal`/`NativeClaimReport`; next slice, citing tidy-ant-251 for a §3 naming review.

## Does `invocation_exit_status` fork `NativeClaimTerminal`'s mapping (§3)?
Same numbers, different domain. `NativeClaimTerminal` is three-valued (Held/NotHeld/NoObservation) and its 0/1/2 mapping is emitter text in the rendered main, not a `.dag` table. `InvocationTermination` is four-valued: `SubjectUnreached` and `Refused` are kept apart (different remedies) though both map to 2. A claim terminal maps into it without loss (NoObservation -> SubjectUnreached), so it is a refinement, not a rival table; the one status authority for `gunbc test` is this function. Unifying the two numeric mappings belongs with the next slice (realizing the verdict as a report value).

## Closure delta (gate widening)
Exactly one module newly enters: `gunbc.target_invocation_termination`. Its imports: `std.decl_ref {DeclarationRef, WholeDeclaration}`, `std.integer {Int}`. The emitter imports only this leaf (`import gunbc.target_invocation_termination { bound_target_producer_status_declaration }`). A wider first attempt (importing `gunbc.target_invocation`, 363 uncovered endpoints, heal run 42387964536) was refused and narrowed.

## Status
Heal run 42392174030 at df257b27 refuses `Stage0EmittedEdgesNotCovered` for this one module: the admission reads the host-shell roster from the pre-existing `lib.rs` (gap left by #12255). Routed as a separate admission defect; this PR holds until it lands. Step 2 (host switches to the emitted module, Rust enum/table/host method deleted) is not yet pushed. `Verdict::apply`/`_exit` stay retained in main.rs.


## Deviations from the brief, stated
No separate stage0 crate layout row was added: closure membership here is import-derived (as for `gunbc.cli_dispatch_surface`), the emitter import is the admission.

Draft. No host runs.

## Revision `ac94292c`, merged with main as `30c16ac0` (proposed; local; not pushed)

**Head for review:** `30c16ac0cc62c257f9838f07c985567c11faffcb`. Its first parent is `ac94292c` (the reviewed correction, unchanged) and its second parent is main `c188b49fc7b73e0e49f8272728dd384123058706`.

- Everything below about `ac94292c` applies unchanged to this head. Its evidence limits apply too: no claim has executed at either head.

Revised in response to disposition keen-otter msg_791e24a3, relayed by sleek-owl. Landing is held. The existing CI and approval apply to `e7867e6c` only.

**Changes in this revision** (4 files, +72/−30, on top of `e7867e6c`):
1. **Terminal is final on both routes.** In `gunbc.compute.attempt_lifecycle` `attempt_state_transition_admitted`, a Terminal prior now refuses another Terminal. Before, `AttemptTerminal => true` ignored the prior, so a settled verdict could be rewritten to a different verdict through the shared law. That held on the payload route as well, and the payload route's behaviour on main was the same. The comment now says Terminal is never reopened *and* never rewritten.
2. **The claim field is the hold.** `AttemptClaimAcquire` no longer calls `durable_hold_acquire_assess` over an invented `HoldSlotFree { generation: revision, released_by: <record bytes> }`. That input was always `Eligible`, so its refusal arm was dead. Now claim `Present` means held, refused as occupied; claim `Absent` means free; and the slot CAS makes acquisition exclusive. The unused hold imports are removed.
3. **`controller_receipt_admit` is removed.** It had no caller, so it was dangling under §3c. The three refusal variants only it produced (`WrongRequest`, `WrongWork`, `WorkUnreadable`) are removed with it. Receipt binding remains the PR 5 frontier recorded in `integration_concern::controller_executor_fence_handoff`, whose trigger is "PR 5's receipt binds WorkOutcome ...". `controller_receipt_for_attempt` is unchanged and still refuses with `ControllerReceiptBindingMissing`.
4. **One new discriminating claim per route:**
   - `durable_attempt_controller_witness::a_settled_attempt_refuses_a_second_terminal_on_the_fenced_route`: same owner, same still-valid lease, different verdict. Expected `AttemptFenceStateRefused`, with the first settle as the positive control.
   - `attempt_lifecycle_wet_witness::a_settled_attempt_refuses_a_second_terminal_on_the_payload_route`: a second terminate at the CURRENT generation, so it cannot be a lost race. Expected `AttemptTransitionRefused`; the record keeps the first verdict and the generation stays at 2.

**Disclosures:**
- **(a) Claim execution.**
  - **Both new claims have NEVER RUN.**
  - The payload-route claim (`attempt_lifecycle_wet_witness::a_settled_attempt_refuses_a_second_terminal_on_the_payload_route`) shares the known-blocked `attempt_lifecycle_wet_witness` closure. At this head it is **predicted** to refuse at resolve, on the `host_effect.dag` equality admission for `CreateCause`, before any evaluation. That prediction is not an observed result for the new claim. Until a prerequisite repair is present in the final head, the payload-route finality has no executable discriminator.
  - The fenced-route claim (`durable_attempt_controller_witness::a_settled_attempt_refuses_a_second_terminal_on_the_fenced_route`) is only **potentially runnable**. It has not been validated.
  - **CI green does not execute these claims.** The required check (`v2-bootstrap`) evaluates no claims, so a green check at any head is not evidence for them.
  - A prerequisite repair (#15992 or an accepted stopgap) requires re-deriving the closure, the claims and the receipts at the **final head**. No named PR's merge is assumed to resolve the closure.
- **(b) `controller_receipt_admit`:** removed (change 3), not deferred.
- **(c) `fabric_terminal_contract_witness`:** this PR adds two missing imports (`unstated_envelope`, `shared_kernel_sandbox_profile`). So that witness did **not resolve on main before this PR**, and its claims were unexercised there.
- **(d) Not built or typechecked locally** for this revision. The legacy-pair qualification below is still outstanding.

**Reviewer minors:**
- **Release-refusal cause collapsed to `WrongEpoch`: left as is.** The observation passed to `durable_hold_release_assess` is built from the claim with `owner: c.holder`, so `HoldReleaseHeldByAnotherOwner` cannot occur. Only a generation mismatch is reachable, and `WrongEpoch` names it. `attempt_fence_owner_refusal` has already distinguished owner, subject and epoch before this point.
- **Follow-ups, not in this revision:**
  - `ControllerCapacityWaiting`/`Cancel` overwriting silently;
  - `DurableHoldSubject` having two wire forms;
  - the witness `lease()` helper constructing `LeaseRunningExpected` without observing it, so it bypasses `LeaseNotObserved`.

---

*The original description follows. Its validation section refers to head `670264ab`.*

An accepted request now commits a stable attempt link before opening its attempt. Restart follows that link; competing delegators recover the committed candidate. The active controller claim and attempt state share the existing reservation-reference CAS slot, so a stale owner cannot borrow a new owner's revision or commit a prepared write after transfer.

The admitted extension lives in `attempt_lifecycle`, reusing its writer. Authorization checks the HeldLease subject, owner and acquisition epoch; the conditional write checks the observed slot revision. Acquisition epoch stays stable across ordinary transitions. Capacity waiting records the exact wake subject, cancellation races on the same slot, and a committed launch survives transfer as an obligation to reconcile the same executor attempt.

## What this change is

Emitter-maintenance slice admitted by keen-otter's purpose ruling (msg_b08055f2, via sleek-owl-397), coordinated and direction-approved by clever-crane-830 (sleek-owl msg_a79be72e): the v1 emitter stops emitting a redundant clone of an owned fold accumulator at its **last use**, for exactly ONE frozen pattern — a literal lambda's owned by-value parameter whose sole use is a by-value call argument. **Structural evidence about emitted code only; no performance claims.**

The repair is PLACEMENT. The same grantor that already existed (#15041) — `v1.compiler.ownership` `build_moved_argument_occurrences` over the lambda's own params and body, `locals_admitted: false` — is now invoked **once, AT THE LAMBDA**, when its body render begins (the new `ExprLambda` arm of `emit_typed_expr`, via `lambda_body_grant_emit_info`), and the caller-side gate is retired in the same change: the grant used to be asked for at whatever call happened to be rendering, under `callee != none && !is_rt` — the kind of a subject the grant never spoke about. One grantor, one consumer (`emit_rust_expr_var`, occurrence-keyed insert into `movable`), one clone producer (`emit_var_ref`). No second registry, no post-pass string rewrite, no new decision site; `ownership.dag` is untouched. Collection lambdas and method folds keep their own renderers and their own grants and do not reach the new arm.

## Stated plainly (required honesty)

- **The loss link is UNLOCATED from source.** A static read of the retired gate's two branch inputs (`typed_emit_info` built only from the render's own `emit_info` via `emit_info_with_expected_type`, which field-copies `moved_argument_occurrences`; the grantor's `_ => emit_info` arm returning its input unchanged) predicted **BOTH** probe cells bare. The v5 packet falsified that: the String cell FAILed (clone stayed), the vec cell PASSed (already bare). I earlier theorized the gate itself dropped the grant at nested runtime-primitive renders — **retracted**: the branches provably carry the same set. The only mid-render replacement found in the path is the per-function-item rebuild (`moved_argument_occurrences := map_get(moved_argument_index, qualified_name)`); which descent link carried a set that never included the lambda-body occurrence, source does not say at this head. The claim is placement + behavior, never a located cause (DESIGN §4d). The class is filed as a durable follow-up: `dag/gunbc/recurring_failure_mode/a_grant_keyed_on_the_rendered_call_drops_the_grant_silently.dag`, whose trigger names the two capabilities that close it: (1) an executed v6 packet receipt of the 14 cells at the exact pin; (2) a located source cause of the retired placement's loss.
- **The 19-site census counted the consumer's name, not the use count.** My earlier working claim that "all 19 become bare" was WRONG and is corrected here before any heal: of the 19 `v1_rt::concat(acc.clone(), ...)` sites, **exactly one is a true last use** — the motivating `std_algebra` `string_concat_join` combine lambda. The other 18 use the accumulator again on some path; their clones are correct and stay. A wrong move would be a loud E0382 (build coverage below).

## The 19 sites (module :: function; mirror file:line at this head; verdict + deciding clause)

| # | module :: function | mirror:line | verdict — deciding clause |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | std.algebra :: string_concat_join | std_algebra.rs:2462 | **MOVE** — closure params `acc`, `field`, each used exactly once as a by-value arg: `fn(acc, field) { concat(acc, field) }` (dag/std/algebra.dag) → expected `v1_rt::concat(acc, field)` |
| 2 | extdeps.uri_path :: render_path_template | extdeps_uri_path.rs:116 | RETAIN — two match arms each use `acc` in tail position (2 edges); per-arm admission requires reusing `fold_body_branch_ends_move_acc`, not wired on this route (frozen pattern) |
| 3 | extdeps.uri_path :: render_path_template | extdeps_uri_path.rs:118 | RETAIN — same closure, second arm |
| 4 | extdeps.version.semver :: semver_split_on | extdeps_version_semver.rs:497 | RETAIN — `acc` is a FUNCTION parameter threaded through the TCO loop (deferred family D, outside the closure-param pattern) |
| 5 | extdeps.version.semver :: semver_identifier_list_parse | extdeps_version_semver.rs:650 | RETAIN — `acc` is a MATCH BINDER (`Some(acc)`), not a closure parameter |
| 6 | gunbc.cli_dispatch_surface :: cli_shipped_dispatch_gap_of | gunbc_cli_dispatch_surface.rs:763 | RETAIN — `acc` used in a match arm AND as the inner folds' `init:` (≥2 edges) |
| 7 | gunbc.cli_dispatch_surface :: gunbc_cli_shipped_dispatch_gap_rendered | gunbc_cli_dispatch_surface.rs:807 | RETAIN — condition `acc == ""` plus `concat(acc, ...)` (2 edges) |
| 8 | gunbc.stage0.stage0_emitted_edge_admission :: stage0_package_reachable | gunbc_stage0_stage0_emitted_edge_admission.rs:191 | RETAIN — condition (any-receiver) + both arms (3 edges) |
| 9 | v1.compiler.coercion :: unique_inhabitants_for_template_tests | v1_compiler_coercion.rs:694 | RETAIN — condition + both arms |
| 10 | v1.compiler.complexity :: analyze_structural_bounds | v1_compiler_complexity.rs:10474 | RETAIN — early-return arm `acc` + tail `concat(acc, param_results)` (2 edges; per-path single use, per-arm admission not wired) |
| 11-12 | v1.compiler.emit :: escape_emoji_codepoints_inner ×2 | v1_compiler_emit.rs:5345,5351 | RETAIN — loop-carried accumulator (`break acc.clone()` + both branches) |
| 13 | v1.compiler.emit_rust :: native_effect_bindings | v1_compiler_emit_rust.rs:47457 | RETAIN — condition receiver + both arms |
| 14 | v1.compiler.infer :: kernel_variant_owner_candidates | v1_compiler_infer.rs:30451 | RETAIN — condition + two arms |
| 15 | v1.compiler.infer_env :: qualified_all_but_last | v1_compiler_infer_env.rs:1915 | RETAIN — condition `acc == ""` + else-arm concat |
| 16 | v1.compiler.trait_bound_witness :: v1_union_bound_param_names | v1_compiler_trait_bound_witness.rs:66 | RETAIN — condition + both arms |
| 17-18 | v1.gunbc.occurrence_binding_parser_walk :: references_named, declarations_named | v1_gunbc_occurrence_binding_parser_walk.rs:158,176 | RETAIN — absent arm `acc` + miss-path `acc` + concat arm |
| 19 | extdeps.languages.rust.capabilities :: derive_traits_union | extdeps_languages_rust_capabilities.rs:577 | RETAIN — condition `derive_traits_contain(traits: acc, ...)` + both arms |

**Build coverage (the loud guard):** the 19 sites live in six stage0 crates — `stage0`, `stage0_std_core`, `stage0_std_surface`, `stage0_extdeps_languages`, `stage0_v1_infer` (mod declarations verified in each lib.rs) — all in the workspace the heal and CI build; a moved multi-use accumulator fails E0382 there. **Heal per-site review (the quiet one):** the heal mirror diff is reviewed site by site against this table; any site that moved bare outside row 1 is an over-application defect and blocks landing.

## Controls: 14 cells, one frozen expectation table

`dag/test/claim/emit_last_use_acc_clone_fixtures.dag` (seven data strings; every module `module probe.lastuse` → read path `src/probe_lastuse.rs`, derivation cited in the control header) + `dag/test/claim/emit_last_use_acc_clone_control.dag` (14 cells; every behaviour cell paired with a marker-only cell so a red can never collapse a refusal). FROZEN expectations, pre-registered in the control header before any run: 7 markers Pass; `the_last_use_by_value_parameter_emits_bare_holds` Pass (v5 receipt: FAIL at the pre-repair emitter); `the_last_use_vec_accumulator_emits_bare_holds` Pass as **regression floor** (v5 receipt PASS — `rc_list_push(acc, x)` already bare, must stay bare); `the_by_ref_primitive_takes_the_borrow_form_holds` Pass — the grant drops the clone but the borrow form holds: `v1_rt::string_contains(&acc,` present, `v1_rt::string_contains(acc,` and `&acc.clone()` absent (the `&` is prefixed after the argument render by `rust_by_ref_bridge_argument`, independent of the move); the four RETAIN cells Pass (v5 receipts PASS ×4). The claim pool is executed only through an authorized frozen packet (manager-owned hardened frame); no lane under `.github/workflows` evaluates the claim pool.

## Floors

`std_graph.rs:267` and `extdeps_external_authority.rs:258` (method-form folds, separate grantor `analyze_single_fold`/`whole_acc_single_use`) stay byte-identical — that renderer is not touched; the corpus bare movers (`hash_combine`, `rc_map_insert`, `canonical_content_cmp`) keep their bare forms; the vec floor above pins the List shape.

## Provenance and landing

`.dag` only; the stage0 mirrors land **only from a real heal at the exact head**, committed verbatim with run id + blob sha256 in the commit record; the final heal must report `changed_paths=0 []`. Precedents cited in-file: String `.length()` spelling (std.types `string_non_empty`, dag/std/types.dag; oci reference fixture), by-ref registry rows (`passes_by_ref: true`, dag/extdeps/languages/rust/emit.dag). v2-bootstrap at the current branch head fails the DOCUMENTED main-red (E0425 `equality_derived_evaluation_environment`, class documented in #15992 — "Every PR's v2-bootstrap on current main fails until this lands"); the repair push carries the sanctioned merge-of-main so v2-bootstrap runs against the fixed base when #15992 lands.

## Heal round provenance and authorization record (keen-otter protocol; ruling msg_2c5a1865 via sleek-owl-397)

**Round 1** — artifact `13532607825`, digest `sha256:47088bcec715d6a322aac2e0db4c48bb5c01d45e8efb891dbba481ee5d0c8a97`, size 523134; producer run 42263722957 (heal-generated-artifacts job 128050204993); producer head `684f12ee13f60121ec94d67bbe46da92a36fa668`, tree `132e2ee5d0c73d676721d6b5c02fcfd48ad0450d`. Manifest declared paths == applied paths (2), entries verbatim:
- `src/v1/stage0/src/v1_compiler_emit_rust.rs` base `6a7f7754e28b523244c9896b4221e2d79a7fa4c9` -> proposed `67d80f92b5bc0ecc0a6d004232018c4123ef93fc` (sha256 `bca76c64c4bb7bfe23064a07d1d792801156b514207e48d6b4c2f22a92bc516d`) — this slice's emitter change; no `concat(acc` text moves in this file.
- `src/v1/stage0/src/v1_compiler_infer.rs` base `3db621b52900a1d54527025dc2633a41a7c88960` -> proposed `073a43c944f95b60522087488c7f6c759843abe4` (sha256 `55c97815a1568a2f67a3e8ee70650e72b5337eedb5a99bb70ea2f4ca7bb190a3`) — NOT this slice's rule (zero last-use-move lines; verified by grep).
Independently byte-reviewed by clever-crane-830: applied == declared, blobs equal the proposed blobs, base blobs equal 684f12ee.

**AUTHORIZATION RECORD.** The push that carried the round-1 commit (`e15db175ee86825ce9f86738b34fb44b4d79cf0c`, tree `1c33f0e79e0e75a7b6270266cca55af9b96b52ab`) was LANE-DIRECTED — made under manager instruction without the required operator grant. That attribution sits with the lane, not the implementing session.

**SEMANTIC IMPACT of the `v1_compiler_infer.rs` convergence (the infer file) — findings from an INDEPENDENT SOURCE REVIEW outside the lane (via sleek-owl-397, msg_5756b6e1); cited as theirs.**
- OLD gate (the committed mirror): `equality_body_helpers_visible`, checked ONLY at the definition door; the call door does no helper check — that asymmetry is the E0425 mechanism.
- NEW gate (the `.dag` seed, and `073a43c9`): `equality_derived_body_emitted`, checked at BOTH doors; it accepts a helper that is either declared in the declaring module or named-imported from its own module.
- FLIPS: NEW ACCEPTS a type in `std.algebra`/`std.optional` whose derived body needs that module's OWN helper; NEW REFUSES at infer a type whose module lacks a foreign helper's import (e.g. `v2.std.diagnostic` `NonEmptyDiagnostics`), which previously died at rustc E0425. UNVERIFIED: modules relying only on `import all` may flip to refused. Plausibly affected: ~25 modules importing `map_values_eq`, `zip_eq`, or `optional_eq` (a grep candidate set).
- `073a43c9` LACKS #15992's two conjuncts, so it still admits `DemandEngine<NativeDemandValue>` (#15992's E0369 reproducer).

Observed in CI at this head: the v2-bootstrap rung moved from `EmittedCompilerBuildFailed` (`E0425 equality_derived_evaluation_environment`) to `EmissionRefused` at demand-acquire (family-2 interim, fail-closed at use). THE LANE'S INTERPRETATION — NOT ESTABLISHED — is that this is `#15972`'s intended semantics (its seed named the new signatures; its committed mirror never converged to them). The lane's recommendation, recorded here: **#15988 does NOT land before #15992.**

**DISTINCT PREDICATES, NEVER INTERCHANGEABLE.** `073a43c944f9...` (this branch's converged `v1_compiler_infer.rs`) and `87b00a4b` (#15992's version of the same file, which ADDS the hotfix conjunct) are DIFFERENT predicates. They must never be swapped, substituted, or described as interchangeable; whichever lands second re-merges main and re-heals. No hand-resolution of that file.

**COVERAGE LIMIT.** The v5 packet receipt (12/12 outcome lines, exit 1) is of the PRE-repair emitter at an earlier head. It does NOT cover `e15db175`; no executed receipt exists at this head (no run is authorized).

**Round 2** — push-triggered workflow run 42275962349 (heal-generated-artifacts job 128092226852) at `e15db175ee86...`: `changed_paths=0 []`, no heal-repair-candidate artifact produced (the committed mirrors ARE the seed's fixed point). MATERIAL FACT: the expected `std_algebra.rs` move (string_concat_join's `v1_rt::concat(acc, field)`) did NOT occur at this head. Static lead, explicitly unconfirmed: `string_concat_join`'s `combine` closure may be rendered by a fold/lowering path that does not pass through `emit_typed_expr`'s ExprLambda arm — the attach point — so the grant may never have been requested for that emission; which renderer produced the `|acc, field|` text at std_algebra.rs:2462 is NOT established from source at this head. Until an executed packet receipt shows the moved spelling, the frozen-pattern claim of this PR is UNEXECUTED, and the land condition (`std_algebra.rs` change) is NOT met — this PR is NOT landable on current evidence.

body:
## What
The heal convergence round rebuilds only `claim_executor`; the overlap refusal, seed-build regen and produce steps then run a `target/release/gunbc` built from the committed (pre-repair) mirrors. #15612's heal (run 42150981431 at 8b763d26e07) failed with no candidate for exactly this reason.

This PR adds `gunbc.heal_workflow heal_round_two_seed_step`, between "Converge the stage0 mirrors" and the overlap refusal. Order is unchanged otherwise: convergence, overlap refusal, seed-build writer, produce. The step refuses (no fallback to the old binary) when:
- the convergence receipt is absent or not newer than the old `gunbc` (ReceiptStaleOrAbsent), has no `changed_paths=` line, or has no execution-identity line;
- the rebuilt binary is absent;
- the converged diff (`git diff HEAD --binary | sha256sum`) moved during the build (TreeMovedDuringBuild);
- `gunbc --version` names neither HEAD nor `HEAD^{tree}` (WrongIdentity).
It prints head, base mirror commit, converged diff sha256, version and the binary sha256. No new manifest field.

Also adds integration_concern row `round_two_seed_identity_not_carried_by_candidate` (SuspectedCapabilityGap, Open): the candidate does not carry the seed identity.

## NOT DONE: heal.yml is not regenerated
`.github/workflows/heal.yml` still has main's bytes (sha256 `489bd88f464ee1aca759fd42bef4e8fcc6a0d298989bbf2b806aab8249fcaf29`), so this PR does not yet match its authority. The one granted remote regen failed:
- BuildBuddy invocation `28cbef5b-c01a-4c15-ba78-52162a348ca5`, runner at EstimatedMemory=32GB (the org cap; 64GB and 48GB were refused).
- `gunbc` built (6m07s). `gunbc run ... generated_artifact_gate.dag --function main_wet_one --arg path=.github/workflows/heal.yml` died in resolve after ~1030 s with three errors: `fleet/fleet_physical_inventory.dag:367:12`, `host/host_effect.dag:248:12`, `compute/compute_seat_ensure.dag:154:41` ("equality admission ... cannot be judged"). None is in this diff; read as a main-base resolve defect.
- The cgroup memory.max write was refused (Permission denied) and the run went uncapped (max_rss 17.5 GB), so that dispatch gives no memory verdict.
- Consequence: the `.dag` changes were not parse-checked past resolve, and none of the controls has run.
- Next: wait for the main resolve fix, merge main, one new regen dispatch (granted separately), commit the bytes verbatim, confirm sha256 locally.

## Controls still owed
1. A real stage0 write to a seed-build-owned path still refuses and publishes no sealed candidate.
2. A paired source+mirror repair needing the new seed (#15612's shape) reaches the check and yields a correctly bound candidate.
3. A failed, non-converged or wrong-identity seed cannot pass.
All need a real heal run (not granted).

Draft; no merge, no landing, no #15612 push.

body:
### v9 — R4, R5 re-frozen; R6 carries the same fixes and stays **HELD**. Prepared only: **nothing here has been run.**

Execution grants come only from keen-otter via sleek-owl-397. No ssh, no claim execution, no partition or
operator writes were made in preparing this. R4 and R5 **discriminate nothing** — presence observations,
no mutation leg, and none is proposed here.

### What v9 changes (manager msg_6ad94d81, as extended by keen-otter msg_baaf8712; budgets per keen-otter msg_42c3c192)

**M1 — `cs_check` now binds each claim to its own leg.** v8 compared claim names as a flat set, so with leg
A booking `a1 b1` and leg B booking `b1`, classes files `A: a1,b1` and `B: b1` produced `AS_EXPECTED`: `b1`
was booked, `b1` appeared exactly once in *some* file, and nothing joined a claim to the leg that produced
it. v9 requires, per classes file `<stem>.classes`, **exactly the names the registration registers under
that same stem, each exactly once** — a name registered under another leg is `claim-wrong-leg:<stem>:<name>`,
a name the registration does not name at all is `claim-unregistered:<name>`, a name registered for the stem
that its own file does not carry once is `claim-count:<stem>`, a name appearing in two leg files is
`claim-duplicated-across-files`, and a registration that names legs this packet never booked (even with a
matching count) is `registration-leg-count`. Every comparison is a **literal awk field comparison**
(`$1==stem && $2==name`); no claim name is ever interpolated into a regex, so a name that happened to look
like a pattern could not widen its own match. The comment now states what is enforced, not what was
intended. Fixtures drive the **shipped** `cs_check` through `final_verdict` on synthetic booked sets:
duplicate-across-legs (`cs-claim-from-another-leg-exits-2`), the moved-claim case (`cs-claims-moved-between-legs-exit-2`,
both directions named), a substituted name (`cs-substituted-name-exits-2`), an unbooked leg in the
registration, and malformed registration/classes lines — each asserting the reason token, not just exit 2.
`cs_check` also **snapshots** what it validated into `$OUT/cs-snapshot` with digests, and `final_verdict`
counts only that snapshot, so the bytes the gate saw are the bytes the verdict counts.

**M2 — the fixture git is hermetic.** The post-leg fixtures' `git init` carried `-c user.name/-c user.email`
but the **commit** did not, so on a machine with no global git identity the commit fails, two fixtures fail,
and a real run-path self-check under the same conditions reports `NO_OBSERVATION`. Every git call in the
fixture scope now goes through one wrapper: identity passed on **every** invocation (init, add, commit),
`HOME` pointed at an empty directory, `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`, `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null`,
`core.hooksPath` set to an empty dir, `env -i` with only `PATH`/`TMPDIR`. Nothing reads or changes an srv1
git identity. The self-check now runs each packet's full fixture suite **twice**, once normally and once
under `env -i HOME=$(mktemp -d) PATH=/usr/bin:/bin`, and runs **itself** under `env -i` as well; and a
control reintroducing the v8 git shape is required to **fail**, so the fix is proven to bite rather than to
be stylistic.

**Wall accounting now admits every timeout.** v8's "capped sum" omitted the bounded `--classifier-fixtures`
self-run and omitted the kill grace: `timeout(1)` without `-k` sends `TERM` and waits for a child that
ignores it, so the sum was not a ceiling. v9 adds `timeout -k 20` at every one of the **six** run-path
`timeout` call sites (clone, fetch, checkout, build, self-run, leg) and counts each grace in `WALL_SUM`
alongside the self-run, with a fixture that counts the `timeout` call sites in the shipped file and refuses
any that lacks a grace. **No booked number moved** — the budget rule is explicit that 7200 is a capability,
not an authorization, and that re-splitting, aggregating, retrying or retuning a per-phase limit may not be
used to fit: R4 stays `RUNTIME_S=5400`, R5 `4500`, R6 `4800`, and every per-step limit is byte for byte what
v8 froze.

| row | booked `RUNTIME_S` | capped sum in v9 | margin | driver row |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| R4 | 5400 | 300+300+120+2400+2×900+**300 self-run**+**7×20 kill graces** = **5360** | 40 | 5700 |
| R5 | 4500 | 300+300+120+2400+900+**300**+**6×20** = **4440** | 60 | 4800 |
| R6 | 4800 | 300+300+120+2400+900+**300**+**6×20** = **4440** | 360 | 5100 |

Nothing was shortened, so no new `NO_OBSERVATION` risk was introduced. The residual risk of the reserve is
stated in each packet header next to the number: work left after the last timeout must fit the reserve, or
the scope's `RuntimeMaxSec` (`TERM`) and the driver row's (`RUNTIME_S`+300, `SIGKILL`) cut the row short and
the row is incomplete, which is `NO_OBSERVATION` (2) for its claims. R4's reserve is 40 s, the tightest.

**Minor items from the same review:** the `PY28` control is replaced by `grepctl()`, which greps the shipped
packet **and** the mutated copy, so both directions can fail (the old pair could only pass); the self-run's
300 s is in the wall sum (above); `final_verdict` counts the snapshot `cs_check` validated instead of
re-reading the files.

### Evidence, as measured

* embedded fixture suites (each packet, in this container): **R4 292 pass / 0 fail, R5 290 / 0, R6 294 / 0**, `rc=0`;
* the same suites under `env -i HOME=$(mktemp -d) PATH=/usr/bin:/bin`: **R4 292 / 0, R5 290 / 0, R6 294 / 0**, `rc=0`
  — where **v8** under the same environment failed **2 fixtures each** (`pg-ok-exits-0`, `pg-short-log-refuses-nonzero`),
  which is M2 reproduced rather than asserted;
* self-check (this PR's harness, with the repo argument): ****1003 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped → `VERDICT=COMPLETE`, rc 0** with the repo argument; the same harness launched whole-sale under `env -i HOME=$(mktemp -d) PATH=/usr/bin:/bin` gives 1003/0/0 again, and its nested empty-HOME re-run 1002/0/0. 92 negative-control rows (v8: 74)**;
* `--predict-only` diff v8 → v9: **only** the manifest file name in the header line and the
  `wall_capped_sum_s=` line (R4 4920→5360, R5/R6 4020→4440). **Every command string and every command digest is
  unchanged** (R4 `f256a1da 4a0ac69f fdb0ba19 b9eb7b3c 453568e5 98211ed7`, R5 `1c90e944 1b03a85f 220bd6bb
  b9eb7b3c c5f7fe87`, R6 `995b533e 4500968d 85a78469 b9eb7b3c 0053be34`) — the command inventory is
  byte-identical to v8;
* end-to-end gate refusals re-measured on v9: bounds-mismatch → exit 2 (R4, R5), the R6 hold → exit 2 naming
  keen-otter msg_3407a188, a relative `OUT` → 2, a nonexistent `OUT` → 2, an `OUT` whose job directory does
  not match the booked job name → 2; nothing is written in any of them;
* the self-check's negative controls run **92 rows across the three packets (v8: 74)** — v8's 27 mutations
  plus **mut28** (the per-leg claim binding removed), **mut29** (the cross-file duplicate scan removed),
  **mut30** (the registration's leg set relaxed to a count), **mut31** (`cs_check` validates but records no
  snapshot), **mut32** (the self-run and the kill graces dropped from `WALL_SUM`), **mut33** (every `-k`
  grace stripped from the run-path timeouts). Each of the six bites all three packets, and the failing
  fixture is named in the log: mut28 → `cs-crossleg-names-the-claim-cause`, mut29 →
  `cs-crossleg-names-the-cross-file-cause`, mut30 → `cs-legset-names-the-leg-cause`, mut31 →
  `cs-shipped-set-registers-and-is-countable`, mut32 → `wall-sum-arithmetic`, mut33 →
  `no-run-timeout-lacks-a-kill-grace`. The wall controls additionally carry hand inversions that must go red
  (removing the `+ T_SELFRUN` term, removing the graces term).

### Honesty state of the self-check

The harness now compares **pinned blob to pinned blob** (`git rev-parse <pin>:<path>`, then re-hashed with
`hash-object`) rather than pinned blob to working copy, so a branch checkout can no longer turn a real
comparison into a skip; a blob this object store cannot produce offline is reported **UNRESOLVED**, and
`report_state` makes the summary read `VERDICT=INCOMPLETE` and exit **2** whenever any check was skipped.
Ancestry is proved, not assumed: a found chain is reported with its `rev-list --ancestry-path` count, and a
miss in a shallow clone is a skip (UNRESOLVED), never a pass. The attestation line prints this repo's shape
(`is-shallow`, `partial-clone-filter`, `has-origin-main`) so a reader can tell what the ancestry evidence is
worth. In this measuring repo the chains resolve: `dff57af7..db56530f` is a chain of **8** commits - the same number calm-eagle-670 measured in their full clone - `db56530f..origin/main` 43 and `dff57af7..origin/main` 51 with `origin/main` reading `7d062bda1b6d…`; the harness prints the clone shape next to the claim (`is-shallow=true partial-clone-filter=blob:none has-origin-main=yes`), reads pinned bytes with `git rev-parse <pin>:<path>` re-hashed by `hash-object` (23 materializations, 0 skips), and where an object or a chain is unavailable it reports UNRESOLVED: any skip makes the summary read INCOMPLETE and exit non-zero.

v8's self-check run is reported as it was measured — **903 passed, 1 failed, 19 skipped, `VERDICT=INCOMPLETE`**

**STATUS: prepared for review only (keen-otter msg_e50888d8). Implementation and LAND are not pre-approved; keen-otter rules on the credential change before LAND. NOTHING in this PR has been compiled or executed.** Basis: ruling msg_52ee1c1b, grant msg_0d7b6ccb.

## Problem
heal-publish minted a 300 s Google token in a workflow step, then `heal_publication_publish_for` re-admitted (~8 min) before its first use: 401 `ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRED`. Run 41951971617: federate 16:53:29, 401 at 17:01:23.

## The one material delta
Federation moves from a workflow step into the binary: a new in-process OIDC -> STS -> iamcredentials exchange, `heal_publisher_cloud_credential` in `gunbc.heal_publication`, called immediately above `mint_publisher_installation_token` (the Secret Manager read). Ported from crisp-bee-97's patch; its extra `GetRef` re-read and `ReferencePreconditionUnreadable` were dropped (outside the grant). The fast-forward-only write, 422 -> `ReferenceNotFastForward`, and `readback_wet` are untouched.

## Checklist (by symbol)
- **Provider:** `gunbc.auth.heal_publisher_federation` `heal_publisher_wif_provider_resource` (unchanged). **SA:** `heal_publisher_service_account` (unchanged, `heal-publisher@gunbai-secrets...`).
- **Audiences** (new accessors, same provider resource): `heal_publisher_assertion_audience` = `https://iam.googleapis.com/<provider>` (OIDC request); `heal_publisher_exchange_audience` = `//iam.googleapis.com/<provider>` (STS). Both spellings are what the pinned google-github-actions/auth 7c6bc770 sends (src/main.ts, src/client/workload_identity_federation.ts).
- **Scopes:** STS `scope` and GenerateAccessToken `scope` are both `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform` (the action's defaults; `gcp.IAM.GenerateAccessToken` default unchanged).
- **Lifetime:** `heal_publisher_cloud_token_lifetime` = `300s`, same value the Federate step carried; a witness pins it.
- **Chain:** `github.OIDC.GetToken` -> `gcp.STS.Exchange` (`extdeps.cloud.gcp.sts`: body clause added, camelCase request per the STS v1 discovery schema; RFC 8693 type mappers) -> `gcp.IAM.GenerateAccessToken`.
- **Impersonation stage:** `gcp.IAM.GenerateAccessToken` ALREADY EXISTED in `extdeps.cloud.gcp.iam` and is reused unchanged (consumer elsewhere: `gcp_iam_bootstrap`). It did NOT previously run in the publisher: the Federate action did that stage. Retained, now in-process.
- **Removal of the early mint:** `heal_publisher_wif_auth_step` and `heal_publisher_wif_step_id` deleted; `WIF_ACCESS_TOKEN` env row and `heal_publisher_wif_access_token_env_name` deleted. The publish step's env now carries only `GITHUB_TOKEN`.
- **Unchanged:** `id-token: write` permission, the pool's attribute condition (trust checks), the App key read (not fetched early), no retry.
- **Credential hygiene:** the token is held in process memory only: not in env, argv, file or receipt. Errors name the stage and `rest_refusal_text`, never a token. Witness fixtures contain no token material.

## Points for the reviewer (honest risks)
1. **Endpoint:** `github.OIDC` now takes its endpoint from an operation parameter (`request_url`, fed from `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL` via `extdeps.github.actions` `github_actions_runtime`), because the sidecar URL arrives per run. That is an input-chosen endpoint, not a constant, and the Bearer request token is sent to it. The pinned action does the same, but this is what "no arbitrary endpoint override" must be judged against; no host allowlist is added here.
2. The provider's live admission of the in-process exchange is unverified.
3. Depends on #15896 (endpoint naming an operation parameter); without it `sts.dag` fails `undefined variable request_url`.

## Controls (required: all three executed; NONE executed yet)
1. Acquisition only after a successful re-admission (failed re-admission -> no exchange). By construction in `heal_publication_publish_for` (credential call sits inside the admitted + open-check arm); no executing witness yet.
2. Still fresh after a corpus interval > 300 s: needs a real run via calm-crab.
3. Fails closed on missing/malformed/denied OIDC, STS or impersonation response without attempting publish: each stage returns `PublisherCloudCredentialNotMinted` -> `exit_failure`; no executing witness yet.
Plus unchanged target/head binding. The only witnesses in the diff (`repository_ci_profile_witness`) check SHAPE (no credential env row, no google-auth action step, audiences, 300 s), not these three behaviours.

## Not done
`.github/workflows/heal-publish.yml` NOT regenerated (waits on #15896 and the #15175 revert); the committed YAML still has the Federate step. Never hand-edited.

## Affected cases (timing join, NOT proof of one root cause)
Open PRs: #15624, #15876, #15779 (draft), #15540, #15903, #15509, #15574, #15894. 401 ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRED runs (12): 42048639519 42047032000 42041335263 42041038610 42036628247 42026788283 42018479344 42005319750 42005266712 41998102997 41996679548 41987672669. Unreadable cause, separate: 42046895767, 42007967761. A separate Admit-step failure (`CreateCause` equality refusal) is not addressed.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)



## Residual (recorded before merge, per the shared Secret migration review at 7d3878a4)

This is the immediate ordering repair, not the first migrated consumer of the shared constraint-aware Secret model. Not a merge or execution grant.

- `PublisherCloudCredentialMinted { cloud: Secret }` DISCARDS `issued.expire_time` (and STS `expires_in`), and carries no point-of-use expiry or scope judgment and no renewal. The shared migration absorbs this provider acquisition into the existing acquisition authority, carries issued expiry/identity/scope, and removes the publisher-specific raw-Secret outcome.
- `token_lifetime_within_maximum` reads the 43200 s ceiling (`default_token_lifetime.max_seconds`), which depends on GCP org policy and is not universal. The ruled 300 s value is unaffected.

# v2 equality: a lookup miss on the equality route is a counted site, never an admit

Work item: node://adhoc-8dcf4dc9-260.

**Question.** Does any v2 equality path read a lookup miss as an admit? (`lookup_miss_read_as_positive_classification`, the equality instance.)

**Answer, as executed at f38a00cb75d:** no equality path admits on a miss — but the one path where a miss
is *accepted* was unpinned, which is how the failure mode returns with a green tree. This PR pins it and
shows the pin can fail.

## The scope swept, and what it is not

At revision `f38a00cb75d85e3a7879c27f7288c2a8bba993ae`:

```
# the population swept: equality-named definitions in the v2 corpus, tests excluded
grep -rIn --include=*.dag -E "^[[:space:]]*(fn|test fn) [A-Za-z0-9_]*(equal|_eq|equality|isomorph|equiv)[A-Za-z0-9_]*\(" \
  src/v2 --exclude-dir=test | sed 's/ *->.*//;s/ *(.*//' | sort -u | wc -l
# => 207

# the site this PR pins, before this PR
git grep -c "ComparisonNotDerived" f38a00cb75d -- src/v2/test | wc -l   # => 0 files
git grep -n "ComparisonNotDerived" f38a00cb75d -- src/v2                 # => 3 lines, all production
```

Every one of the 207 was inspected for a miss arm (`Absent`/`Missing`/`NotFound`/`NotCarried`/`Unknown`/
`Empty`/`Unavailable`) yielding a positive verdict, and for the asymmetric shape — one side's keys walked
with a lookup into the other side and no cardinality guard. Cleared, with the reason:

- `v2.std.node` structural equality (`node_equal_ignoring_provenance`, `node_same_occurrence`,
  `node_edge_equal_ignoring_provenance`): no lookup at all; children compare through `zip_eq`
  (`dag/std/algebra.dag`), which refuses on `b` empty while `a` has members *and* on `a` empty while `b`
  has members — both length mismatches, not one.
- `v2.std.runtime` `runtime_value_equality` and `runtime_value_projected_equality`: three verdicts, and the
  third is real. Two values that both project to a `Node` compare structurally; two that are both
  `RuntimeValueNodeUnrepresentable` answer `RuntimeValueEqualityUnavailable` (reason
  `runtime_value_structural_projection_unavailable`) and are never collapsed to `Equal`; two closures answer
  `Unavailable` (reason `runtime_closure_equality_unavailable`). A projectable value against an
  unrepresentable one answers `Differ` — a definite verdict about two different shapes, not a claim about
  their contents. Field selection answers `RuntimeFieldFound` or `RuntimeFieldMissing`, and `eval.dag`
  rejects the step on `Missing` (`eval_rejected_projected_field_absent_from_value`) rather than binding a
  stand-in, so an absent field is never read as equal to something.
- `std.algebra` `map_values_eq` (`dag/std/algebra.dag`): guards `count(map_keys(a)) == count(map_keys(b))` before walking one side's
  keys, so the one-sided walk cannot admit an index with extra entries.
- `v2.compiler.trait_derive_completeness`: a row miss yields `Unknown`, and `Unknown` is refused at the
  gate — already pinned by `tdc_unknown_capability_refuses_rather_than_defaulting`, whose own header
  records that the defaulting shape is the one that had to be kept out.
- `v2.compiler.dependency_demand` `demand_tables_equal`: the one genuinely one-sided comparison found
  (it walks `functions` and looks each path up in both tables). It is closed by its producer, not by
  luck: `demand_round` builds each table by folding over the same `functions` list, inserting exactly
  `f.path`, so no entry can exist outside the domain the comparison enumerates.
- `v2.compiler.infer` `infer_branch_type_atoms_equal` and `infer_unify_transform_operand_types`: an atom
  against a non-atom answers `false`, and the structural route is entered only when `a` carries no atom
  identity at all — a miss there goes to the *stricter* judgment (`node_equal_ignoring_provenance`), never
  to an accept. In `infer_unify_transform_operand_types`, every path on which an operand type does not
  resolve yields `OperandsNotJudged` or `OperandsDisagree`, each carrying its diagnostic; nothing resolves
  to `OperandsOneType` except a structural match of two resolved types.

**A negative grep is scope, not proof.** What the sweep buys is the ranking: it says where to look and
that nothing else looked wrong to the question asked. The proof is the executed pair below.

## What is pinned

`v2/compiler/infer.dag` `infer_operation_value_type`, the `EqualityComparison` arm, asks the operand
carrier for its Equivalence row through `infer_algebra_field_result_type`. Carried, the comparison's type
is the field's declared codomain, read from the structure. Not carried, the arm does not refuse and does
not answer `Bool` by assumption: it accepts the program and leaves the node on the grounding frontier
with site `ComparisonNotDerived` — *unmodelled, not incomparable*, the counted mechanism that keeps
`Bool == Bool` legal while the carrier is unmodelled. The accounting is not free either:
`infer_comparison_not_derived` first requires a descent witness (`infer_descent_witness_for_node`) and
**rejects** without one, so the site is recorded only for a node the checker can show it descended into.
That is an accounted miss, not a silent admit; but
nothing under `src/v2/test` named the site, so nothing separated "the arm records the miss" from "the arm
admits".

The two fixtures are not new programs: `src/v2/test/claim/compiler/equality_judged.dag` already exercises
both shapes over the operator route — `fn k(a: Int, b: Int) -> Bool { a == b }` accepted with **nothing**
left underived, `fn k(a: Bool, b: Bool) -> Bool { a == b }` accepted **and** carrying the grounding
not-derived advisory. That split is exactly the row census in
`src/v2/extdeps/languages/dag.dag` `dag_algebra_inhabitance_decls`: Equivalence inhabitance rows exist
only for `Int` and `Symbol`, while `Bool` carries only `BooleanAlgebra` (`and_`, `or_`, `not_`, `top_`,
`bottom_`) — no `eq` field for the comparison to consult. What was never asserted anywhere is the *site
name* behind that advisory, which is precisely the difference between recording the miss and admitting it.

`src/v2/test/claim/infer_not_derived_site.dag` gains six claims (the file declares 15 in total, and the
witness run requires all 15 to report PASS). **The pair varies only the row:** both
fixtures are the same `fn k(a: T, b: T) -> Bool { a == b }` shape, and Int carries its Equivalence row in
`v2.extdeps.languages.dag` `dag_algebra_inhabitance_decls` while Bool does not — so no claim here can
pass on anything but the row's presence.

| claim | what would break it |
| --- | --- |
| `nds_eq_row_carried_comparison_is_accepted_without_the_comparison_site` | the arm stops consulting the row and marks every comparison not-derived |
| `nds_eq_row_absent_comparison_carries_the_comparison_site_exactly_once` | the arm admits silently (no fact), or marks the node twice |
| `nds_eq_row_absent_comparison_moves_the_frontier_total_by_exactly_one` | the miss admits without being counted (delta 0), or drags an unaccounted node with it (delta 2) |
| `nds_eq_row_carried_comparison_leaves_the_frontier_total_where_the_no_comparison_fixture_has_it` | a derived comparison starts leaving residue |
| `nds_eq_no_comparison_fixture_carries_no_comparison_site` | the site belongs to the fixture shape rather than to the comparison (the cheap weaker control) |
| `nds_eq_row_absent_comparison_row_count_is_its_occurrence_count` | the per-site census disagrees with the facts on the tree |

The frontier assertion is a **delta**, not a number read off the tree: the comparison fixture's
`grounding_not_derived` total minus the no-comparison fixture's must be exactly 1. A count copied from
the current tree is a change detector; a delta between two fixtures that differ in one construct is a
claim. Every absence arm answers `false` rather than a vacuous truth, so a fixture the route refuses
cannot read as "no site".

## Receipt — executed green and red

> **STATUS: PENDING — nothing has been executed.** The claims are static-verified only (grammar shapes
> taken from this file's own forms, helper signatures, claim census, no duplicate names, ASCII) and their
> expected values are corroborated by the pre-existing green claims in `compiler/equality_judged.dag` over
> the same two programs. Corroboration is not execution: this PR is not evidence until the row has run and
> its raw per-claim lines are pasted below. Opened as a draft so the v2-bootstrap and heal gates run on
> this revision in parallel — v2-bootstrap runs no claims, so the row stays the only evidence here.

Run on srv2 by calm-crab-645 (row `witty-deer-788-nds-eq`), script
`nds_equality_row_miss_keeper_run.sh` sha256 `b3e4f5794d1644be4ff1a4068548426d0041f44d18aa6e4427e62fb8304953ff`,
which clones the repo itself and refuses unless HEAD is `9ba6d6fa538f1574203596a9eefa6c2f24e6d2f6` and
`HEAD^{tree}` is `d91b1cefc40a27994b4f6be922ae677ab8d9b283`.

**HOW THE RECEIPT IS READ (keen-heron's ruling, and a known defect in the script).** The script's own
`GREEN=`/`RED=` labels are not the verdict; the verdict is read from the harness's raw per-claim lines,
which the run prints in full: `PASS <fn>` on stdout per claim and `FAIL <fn>` on stderr
(`src/v1/stage0/src/main.rs`, `run_one_function`). A `FAIL` line in the GREEN leg is an **observed red**
whatever label the script prints — in `b3e4f579` a green claim that runs and prints FAIL is labelled
`NO_OBSERVATION` (calm-crab found it: the FAIL test sits in the NO_OBSERVATION branch, which makes the
`GREEN=FAIL` branch unreachable). The label is a mislabel, not a verdict, and the direction of the defect
is safe: it can under-claim a green, never invent one. `NO_OBSERVATION` is legitimately produced only by
a timeout, a signal (rc ≥ 124), OOM-counter movement, an `error:` line, or a claim set that does not match
the file's declarations.

<!-- filled from calm-crab's END: head/tree lines, every claim name with its PASS/FAIL, GREEN_EXIT, RED_EXIT, oom_kill, memory.peak -->

## Branch provenance

`session/witty-deer-788` carries two commits over `f38a00cb75d`, touching one file:

1. the six claims and their helpers;
2. a formatting-only change: the three fixture `data X: String = …` declarations collapsed onto one line.
   Nothing in `dag/` or `src/v2` breaks a `data` declaration after the `=` — every string constant in the
   corpus puts its value on the declaration line — and a load error there would have spent the row's single
   attempt. **That commit's message cites "DESIGN 11.3", which does not exist**; the reason is the one
   given here. Noted so the stale citation is not inherited silently.

## Not claimed

- **The sweep is over equality-*named* definitions.** Two heuristics were also run over **all 15,559**
  non-test `fn`s in `src/v2` — (i) a body that walks one collection (`all`/`any`/`fold`/`filter`) while
  looking into a second (`map_get`/`*_lookup`/`*_at`/`find`) with no cardinality guard anywhere in the
  body, and (ii) a miss arm (`Absent`/`Missing`/`NotFound`/`NotCarried`/`Unknown`/`Empty`/`Unavailable`)
  whose expression yields a positive verdict (`true`, `*Equal*`, `*Admit*`, `*Accept*`, `Pass`, `Holds`,
  `Complete`) with no negation in it. They flag 190 and 72 sites respectively. Every one reachable from an
  equality verdict was read and is in the cleared list above; the remainder are lens compile gates that
  accept because they found nothing, `Option` equality arms, and resolve-walk arms — outside this question,
  and **not** vetted by this PR. A miss read as an admit behind a name that does not mention equality is
  not excluded by anything here.
- No v1/seed equality path is audited here: `equality_route_for`, the folded plan and the residual rule
  are the seed checker's, and `src/v2/std/node.dag` records that the seed is their only consumer. They
  need the same question asked of them, separately.
- `ComparisonNotDerived` remaining on the frontier for `Bool == Bool` is not asserted to be *correct*,
  only to be *counted*: the arm's comment says the carrier is unmodelled, and until `Bool` carries an
  Equivalence row or a derivation, that hole is honest rather than closed.
title: v2 equality: a lookup miss on the equality route is a counted site, never an admit
