Only one path is in both sides' change sets, and the one line that appears to vanish from the
previous tip is the trailing comma as main's four controls append to the list — not content loss.

**NO VERDICT claimed**: still no compile and no `.dag` typecheck at any head of this branch.

The push was authorized by clever-crane-830 for this one merge commit (mergeability is a real
reason); **no other pushes until the operator rules the provenance route**. Runs at this head —
heal `41749948230`, witnesses `41749948041` — are **expected red with the recorded structural
`E0425`** (the regenerator cannot build until A exists) and are **not** to be rerun: that failure
is a property of the rename's provenance, already recorded above, and not a verdict on the merge.


---

## Generated-artifact drift: origin of the stale mirror (recorded 2026-11-05, at tidy-ant-251's direction)

- **The drift originates in `afb26935114`** — "gunbc(v1): generalize the collection-primitive grounding to cover
  the set cluster", Tue Nov 3 18:33:58 2026 +0000. It is the only commit in this branch's history whose diff touches
  `try_v2_std_collection_primitive_grounding`, and it renames the family on **both** sides of one boundary in a
  single commit: the authority `dag/gunbc/v1/v1_interpreter_primitive_surface.dag` (16 occurrences of
  `collection_primitive_grounding`) and the hand-written consumer `src/v1/stage0/src/v1_interpreter.rs:11373` and
  `:11375`, while `src/v1/stage0/src/v1_interpreter_dispatch_generated.rs` continues to define only the
  `..._map_...` names (2 map-family, 0 primitive-family).
- **`8a08d10d205` is NOT the origin.** It lands 23 minutes later (18:56:32) and its diff touches three lines of
  `src/v1/stage0/src/v1_interpreter.rs` only — neither the authority nor the mirror. It is named here so that a
  reviewer does not mistake it for the origin: it is the last commit to touch the area, and it carries the hand-Rust
  justification that makes the area look freshly opened.
- **Not inherited drift.** `main` is self-consistent at the same boundary — 4 map-family references in the consumer,
  2 map-family / 0 primitive-family in the mirror — so the mismatch is introduced wholly by `afb26935114`.
- **Base for the eventual regenerated bytes: `4c1a940c0be`** (the authorized merge of `main`, the #15621 resolution
  and the three fixes), per tidy-ant-251: the producer runs against the authority **as it stands at that head**, so
  dropping those commits would only mean redoing them. The declared producer for the mirror is
  `gunbc.v1.v1_interpreter_dispatch_emit` / `expected_v1_interpreter_dispatch_generated_rs`, bound at
  `dag/gunbc/generated_artifact.dag:179` (location) and `:489` (producer decl), and the file's own banner forbids
  hand editing — the bytes must be generator-produced and only that mirror committed.
- **Landing gate.** Any land ask for this PR must quote this PR's own heal `changed_paths` line verbatim and show
  `changed_paths=0` at the head being landed; inherited drift on paths this PR does not touch is disclosed, not
  blocking. There is currently **no** `changed_paths` line to quote at the CI head `eba95e400da`, because heal exits
  `floor_class=structural exit=101` before reaching the regen phase — that is a NO VERDICT under the rule, not a pass.


## Route A mechanism — base-built regenerator (recorded 2026-11-05, at tidy-ant-251's direction)

Correction recorded first, in tidy-ant-251's own words as his error: clever-crane-830 **never ruled "option B"** for
this PR. Their "B" was the heal-publish **token** fix, which he conflated with this branch's option B. Their only
ruling is that #15743 waits for the operator on **ROUTE A**, and the route-B retraction above stands. For the record,
neither "option A/B" nor token wording appears anywhere in this PR's comment thread — the conflation lived in session
traffic, not in the PR record.

Route A is precisely the mechanism that answers the bootstrap cycle recorded in the previous section: the regenerator
is taken from a tree where the mirror and the host still agree, so it can be built at all.

1. Check out this PR's **merge-base with `main`** — the tree where the mirror and the host agree. Build `gunbc` and
   `claim_executor` there, and record the binary `sha256`.
2. In a **separate tree at the PR head**, run that base-built binary's `--required-regen` over the **head's** `.dag`
   (head source roots) to produce `src/v1/stage0/src/v1_interpreter_dispatch_generated.rs`.
3. The receipt carries **both tree shas** (merge-base and head), the **binary sha256**, the **produced blob sha**, and

4. Commit **that one file, verbatim** — generator-produced, never hand-edited. heal at the new head must build with
   `changed_paths=0`, and that is the line any land ask for this PR quotes verbatim.

Status: **no ruling yet, and nothing prepared.** Route A requires its **own per-attempt operator ruling**; it is not
covered by any standing grant. The generic fix — heal building round 1 from base — is clever-crane-830's escalation
`msg_a1f3b7aa` and is tracked there, not here.

DRAFT. Repairs `type X = X { .. }` (arm spelled like its type) being unimportable on the native route (resolve_reason_unbound_symbol at the type reference; e.g. gunbc.site.gunb_ai_layout importing TokenSwatch).

**Mechanism (code reading + two executed refusals; Disj-vs-Conj of the one-arm record is UNMEASURED):** the Disj arm files an alias at `module.X`, equal to the type's own path, so `module.X` has claimants [module.X, module.X.X]; `symbol_index_lookup` answers Absent for >1 claimants, so the import row in `symbol_index_bind_pending_round` is deferred forever and binds nothing.

**Changes (symbol_index_fill.dag only):**
1. `symbol_index_bind_pending_round`: a Contested import target binds every claimant under its own declaring path (new `symbol_index_bind_claimants`); the reference's required kind then filters candidates before none/one/many. Two same-kind claimants stay two candidates and refuse as ambiguous (no pick).
2. New `symbol_index_mark_alias_payload`: the alias VariantArmPayload mark is skipped when it would land on the declaring path of the owning type. `symbol_index_mark_declared_payload` is `map_insert` (last write wins), so that write was a SILENT kind loss on a map keyed by declaring path; the arm's own kind is already marked at `<type>.<arm>`.

**Conforming refinement of ruling (B) (accepted by tidy-ant-251, no set and no new kind):** with the map keyed by declaring path the type (`module.X`) and arm (`module.X.X`) already have distinct entries; the defect was the alias mark writing a binding-path fact onto the type's entry. Skipping it plus kind filtering at the reference gives (B)'s semantics. Stands or falls on the construction row: if `resolve_sole_declared_payload_path` refuses on 2 candidates, it gets the required-kind filter before counting, in this PR.

Rationale as originally stated: the root violation is a binding-path fact written into a declaring-path-keyed map, not the map's cardinality; a set would keep a stale conflated fact and force changes in infer 1485/1601/4845/8649 and resolve 3131/3595. Readers changed: none beyond the import binder; the last-write-wins overwrite in `symbol_index_mark_declared_payload` remains and is the follow-up if the set model is still wanted. Needs tidy-ant-251's call.

**Evidence owed (not yet executed):** /tmp/sar/sar3.sh (sha256 dd3a5e70...): RED/positive entries sar_self (type position + construction), gunb_ai_layout; controls sar_dist (DistArm imported), sar_dupuse (genuine duplicate, must still refuse). Run main vs this head via calm-crab-645. Corpus census is regex-scoped (6 sites). Overlap with valiant-deer-27's head: none in these functions.

Per tidy-ant-251's condition (downstream consumers read the resolved-reference form `symbol_index_declaring_path_of_bound`; the mention form's callers are only inside resolve). Source: `git grep -n "symbol_index_declaring_path_of" -- '*.dag'` at cc31a90c9996 (a grep, not a semantic proof).

**Citation rule (tidy-ant-251 ruling, 2026-11-04):** a documentary citation (`v2.std.decl_ref_resolution` `resolve_declaration_ref`) names a declaring PATH, not an occurrence. module + `X` resolves to the module-level declaration X (the type); the arm of a self-spelled record is cited by its own path `X.X`; the two have distinct declaring paths and are not contested. Two distinct module-level declarations spelled X (a type X and a fn X) make a kind-less citation refuse as ambiguous, never a pick. Whether `resolve_declaration_ref` behaves so today is UNMEASURED; if not, it is a separate follow-up with a RED and is not folded into this PR.

**Draft, operator-authorized hardening (keen-otter-392 msg_8199c418, relayed by sleek-owl-397).** No live credentials, publish, re-run or IAM change. Not B1.

## What
1. **Refusal text on the heal publisher's credential operations carries no body.** `gunbc.github_effect_perform` `publisher_refusal_text` is used by `publisher_key_unreadable` (the Secret Manager read of the App key) and `publisher_installation_token_refused` (the installation-token mint). It used to print `HTTP <status>: <body>` into the cause that `heal_publication_publish_for`'s `exit_failure` writes to stderr. It now prints:
   - the HTTP status;
   - plus the **closed-vocabulary** codes of a Google error body: `extdeps.cloud.gcp.error_info` `gcp_safe_error_codes`, i.e. a `google.rpc.Code` name (googleapis `google/rpc/code.proto`) and a `google.rpc.ErrorInfo` reason in the `error_details.proto` shape `[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]+[A-Z0-9]`, at most 63 chars.

   Anything else, including `error.message`, metadata, non-JSON bodies and forged fields, is dropped. Transport causes and undecodable causes are withheld.
2. **`--record` refuses credential-bearing operations.** The v1 interpreter adds `InterpError::RecordRefusedCredentialOperation`. It is raised **before** the inputs are hashed or serialized and **before any request is built**, for an operation whose service declares auth (`auth` / `auth_input` / `auth_source`, the same properties `resolve_auth` reads) or that takes a `Secret` input. This is read off the declaration, with no operation-name list.

## Evidence
- `dag/test/claim/github_effect_perform_witness.dag` adds 6 fake-secret witnesses. They plant `FAKE-SECRET-MARKER` in:
  - a Google error message and metadata;
  - a 2xx-undecodable cause;
  - a transport cause;
  - a non-JSON body;
  - forged status and reason fields (out-of-vocabulary, lowercase, over 63 chars, trailing `_`);
  - a GitHub error body.

  Each witness asserts the exact refusal text and that the marker is absent. The existing prefix witnesses (`HTTP 403`, `HTTP 422`, `transport`) still hold by construction.
- Interpreter tests:
  - `record_refuses_a_credential_bearing_operation_before_any_request`: endpoint `192.0.2.1` (TEST-NET-1, unroutable), so a late refusal would surface as a transport error, not the typed one.
  - Control: `an_operation_with_no_auth_and_no_secret_input_is_not_credential_bearing`.
- **Not executed yet.** BuildBuddy refuses remote runs and the srv1 host is closed, so a srv2 run is requested from calm-crab-645. Results will be posted here; nothing is claimed green before then.

## Every output sink on the publish path (sleek-owl-397 scope check)
| Sink | Covered how |
|---|---|
| `gunbc.github_effect_perform` `publisher_refusal_text` (Secret Manager key read, installation-token mint) | **Changed.** Status plus Google closed codes only. Marker witnesses in `test.claim.github_effect_perform_witness`. |
| `gunbc.heal_publication` `rest_refusal_text` (writes, readbacks, PR-state read, receipt comment) | **Changed.** Status only; transport and undecodable causes withheld. Marker witnesses in `test.claim.heal_publication_refusal_redaction_witness`. |
| The not-fast-forward arm (`ReferenceNotFastForward { detail: body }`) | **Changed.** It printed the raw body directly; it now goes through `rest_refusal_text`. |
| `exit_failure` / stderr (`cli_run.rs`, `ExitClass::Failure { code, reason }`) | Prints `reason` **verbatim**. Every REST-derived reason on this path is now built only from fixed prefixes and the two functions above (`heal_publication` callers: `refused_exit`, the four `HealPublicationUnverified` readbacks, `HealReceiptUnposted`, `PublishPrStateUnreadable`; `publisher_*`). So the marker tests on those functions are tests of exactly what this sink prints. |
| v1 `decide_rest_exchange` | Builds `RestStatusRefused { status, body }` and the other arms **as values**, and prints nothing (no `eprintln`/`trace_emit` in its body). A body reaches output only through the text functions above. |
| `RestTransportRefused { cause: error.to_string() }` | Also a value only. Both text functions now withhold `cause`. |
| v1 `dispatch_rest` `[rest] {METHOD} {url}` trace | `url` = `base_url` + `substitute_template(path)`, with no headers and no body. The bearer goes on the request header via `resolve_auth`, never into the URL. The path parameters on this route are not credentials: the Secret Manager project, secret and version; GitHub owner, repo, ref and sha. No credential sits in a path or query here. |
| `--record` fixture file | **Refused** for credential-bearing operations, before serialization (`RecordRefusedCredentialOperation`). |
| Non-REST sinks on this path (`git write-tree` stderr in `classify_write_tree_completion`, the candidate manifest read error) | Local, credential-free git and file operations (the fetch is a credential-free public `ls-remote`/`fetch`), so they carry no token. |

## Not in this PR (declared census, for a follow-up)
Other sites that put a raw response body into printed text:
- `gunbc.auth.heal_publisher_provision` `rest_refusal_text`.
- `gunbc.cloudflare.r2_token_mint_run`.
- `gunbc.fleet.printer_credential_migration`.

Narrowing those is the same move with a body-free refusal function per site. They are listed, not changed here, to keep this draft bounded to the identified credential operations.

## v1 maintenance purpose
Under `gunbc.v1.v1_maintenance_standing`: the heal publisher runs on the v1 interpreter, and this closes a credential-exposure path on that live route.

Reviewers: crisp-ibex-490 (authority, DESIGN 3b), clever-crane-830 (code).

## Purpose (DESIGN §3 maintenance — serves the v2 self-host)
An else-less `if c { i }` followed by any sibling statement **refuses at PARSE on BOTH executors** — the interpreted route and the emitted gen-1 route agree (cc2-pp6 @ `32dfa37d`, srv2 run.log sha `dc759c24`). The text is a production the grammar declares reachable (`dag_grammar_if_block_form` = block + OPTIONAL else tail), yet it is unreachable in a statement sequence: the condition reads `c { i }` as a single-pun record and the if is starved of its block. This PR realizes the seed's condition-position separation as ONE grammar production both executors read (DESIGN §4). Ownership: `keen-heron-809` reviewed the rule (sign-off chain in the session receipts); the seed's `02_parse.dag` is NOT edited.

## EVIDENCE (separate from cause, per review condition 2)
- **Both-route agreement** (the earlier emitted-vs-interpreted divergence premise was WITHDRAWN in #15648 — cc2-pp6 completed the interpreted halves and the executors agree on every text): elseless + sameline + blockfinal REFUSE at PARSE with `parse_g0_tokens_remain`; interpreted loci (no binder-capture bug there) put the leftover AFTER the if-block — tail `i` at 151..152, fn closing `}` at 149..150 — while if-WITH-else and two-plain-statements PARSE on both. Receipts: srv2 `cc2-pp6` out/ + the pp7 twelve-row discriminator table (link pending).
- **What is established vs hypothesis**: the both-route refusal is ESTABLISHED; the punned-record mechanism is the leading reading (the only anti-record device keyed on a one-name brace run FOLLOWED BY ELSE, so it fires exactly when an else follows — matching which texts parse on both routes), and the pp7 discriminator rows (nonpun `if c { 1 }`, paren `if (c)`, call head, else-tail, dot head) pin it. If the discriminators refuse as the alternative reading predicts, the condition productions still land (seed parity, below) and the residual continuation defect gets its own RFM row.

## CAUSE and fix
v1 (the SEED) separates the readings in the condition parser only: `parse_if` and `parse_match` share `parse_expr_no_brace` — an uppercase-head gate (`02_parse.dag:5774/5899`) plus a retry that abandons a record ending at neither `{` nor an operator (`:6139`). v2's grammar cannot read a head's case, so the fix realizes the same separation declaratively rather than as a parser retry (DESIGN §7: the seed is the oracle of what v2 must not lose, not the mechanism spec):
- `grammar_expr_and_predicate`: named positive peek (`!!e`, Ford's `e / e` dual of not_predicate — exactly the derived form the not_predicate comment prescribes), zero-width on both arms, FIRST-gated by the probed element. One added helper in `v2/std/grammar.dag`, no new algebra node.
- Condition productions (`condition_expr` / `condition_binary` / `condition_unary` / `condition_postfix` / `condition_primary` + condition ident/dot suffix): the record arm of the ident suffix is admitted only when its residue continues with `{` or an infix class — the continuation set derived from ONE authority (`dag_infix_operators()` + the block brace), postfix heads excluded, matching the seed's set exactly (the `if r { x } .f { i }` datum is reported rather than widened silently).
- `if_expr` condition and `match_expr` scrutinee slots switch to the condition productions (the seed shares one no-brace parser across exactly these two). Emitted identities mirror the ordinary productions, so lowering dispatch is untouched.
- `dag_grammar_block_of_one_name_before_else_expr` is DELETED (DESIGN §6b root generalization): the peek subsumes its language at conditions, and its only firing OUTSIDE conditions was a misfire — `if c then R { s } else d` REFUSED although the then-branch has no block slot and the record is the only reading that fits. Reaching-site enumeration: the guard fires only where an expression can be immediately followed by kw_else — the then-branch (where it was wrong) and conditions (now peek-gated). Corpus: ZERO real then-form uses in `dag/` + `src/v2/` (all "then" hits are prose); the seed has no then-form. The declared then-branch limitation ("spell `s: s`") is retired with it, stated as a correction.

## RED / controls (claims on the live grammar, both executors)
`src/v2/test/claim/parse/condition_position_record_parse.dag` (exemplar: `block_expr_as_binary_operand_parse.dag`): RED pair — `elseless_if_with_tail_parses` (the verbatim rtp_probe shape; refused before, parses after) and `then_branch_record_parses` (refused under the guard, parses now); Branch-shape twin — the else-less body's arrow body lowers to `ComputationNode { behavior: Branch }`, red if the record reading ever returns. Controls, green before and after: record in let head, record call argument, parenthesised record condition, record right-operand of an infix in condition position (`if x == Present { value: y } { ... }` keeps the record), record-headed match scrutinee, record-LHS operator chain in condition position, else-if chain. Same-byte BEFORE/AFTER on both routes per condition 4: the claim halves run interpreted; the emitted half rides the existing claim-executing rows + pp7/post-fix receipts (pending rows listed in the session).

## Status
Draft pending the pp7 discriminator table (which names the fork). Controls from `namespace_xl0/return_tail_position.dag` stay green (the guard claims use return-bodied blocks — unaffected either way). RFM row for this class ships with the table-pinned wording.

## Dropped: the normalize-accepted Branch twin
The first draft carried a Branch-shape twin asserting normalize ACCEPTS the else-less body. It was
removed before push: namespace_xl0's `return_tail_position` control (the verbatim member source,
line 62) asserts that text PARSES and normalize REFUSES with `else_less_if_unlowered` — so a
normalize-Accepted twin is unsatisfiable by design. The parse-accept REDs here plus namespace_xl0's
lowering controls are the full chain (the rtp controls, which cc2-pp6 shows failing on both routes
at main, are expected to flip GREEN by this fix — reported as side evidence at land).

## Warm enrollment (exemplar rule)
Per the exemplar `block_expr_as_binary_operand_parse` (its in-file note: a claim that parses its own
source is over the new-witness eval-step budget), all twelve claim producers are enrolled in
`v2.workflow.floor_pure_producer_share` (ActiveFillDebt, alphabetical), mirroring the exemplar entry
(`8a255ba6564`).

## Corpus-fixed widening: the head set equals the ordinary postfix chain's heads (fb23ea37a38)
The earlier "postfix heads excluded, seed parity" design was WRONG and this PR fixes it:
`match R { ... }.totalUpdatedCells { ... }` (test/claim/review_sheet_converge_witness.dag:1745,
green on main) refused under the `{`-or-infix head set — the scrutinee record was rejected, the
bare name swallowed the match body's brace, parse refused with a token remainder (keen-koi-376,
#15639 v2-bootstrap run 41546355118; same hole = the 62 hard diagnostics in this PR's heal run
41551484349). The peek's head set is now exactly what the ordinary postfix repeat admits: `{`,
the infix rows (minus newline-guarded), and the postfix suffix heads `.` / `as` / `is` /
newline-guarded `[`. Call `(` is not a head (the call suffix sits inside the ident suffix before
the record arm, not in the repeat). The seed's retry set is the narrower hole keen-heron flagged,
not a behavior to copy. Control `record_scrutinee_dot_still_parses_holds` pins the corpus shape.
Comments at all four sites state the real set (review 38602, artifact 90178).

## Executed discriminator pair (cc2-15695c-5279 vs cc2-15695c-acb4, srv2, host claim runs)
At the peek-consumption regression head `52790408085`: 8 PASS / 4 FAIL — `infix_record_condition_still_parses_holds`,
`record_chain_condition_still_parses_holds`, `record_match_scrutinee_still_parses_holds` RED as
pre-registered (record skipped -> leftover braces have nowhere to go), GREEN again at `acb4c89c`.
The controls discriminate record-consumed from record-skipped by EXECUTION, not by construction.
`then_branch_record_parses_holds` PASSED at the regression head: the then-branch is an ordinary
expression production (dag_grammar_if_then_form_expr reads the ordinary expr chain), so the record
there was consumed by the never-regressed ordinary arm — this claim discriminates the GUARD
DELETION (RED at main), not the condition-arm consumption; stated in the module comment.

## Tree-shape witnesses (review 38602, artifact 90174; rewritten at 31dc346f90a)

Three claims assert the tree, not just acceptance: the else-less if owns exactly one
`fn_body` production holding exactly one statement, and the module holds three statements
total (the tail is a sibling, not part of the if); the then-form's if has zero `fn_body`
productions below it (its branches are records); the dot-condition if has one `postfix_expr`
(the `.d` consumed by the condition) and one `fn_body`. They read the MODULE tree
(`parse_module_prepared`) and locate the if node by production identity (`g_find_production`);
a production-rooted parse of the full module text refuses on leftover tokens and measures
nothing (that was the first version's defect, caught by cc's battery at 4f04dd31).


## Emitted-route AFTER, executed (cc2-15695e-09ad, srv2, gen-1 at 09ad199b, peak 12.8G)
The five member fixtures through the native CLI (ce-probe7): elseless 0f785394, sameline 26f4ca0a,
blockfinal fce23fc1 now refuse at LOWERING with body_lowering_reason_else_less_if_unlowered (was
parse_g0_tokens_remain at cc2-pp3/cc2-pp6); twostat adba7f47 and elseelse 68012d82 refuse with
statement_precedes_without_binding, unchanged. Same verdicts the interpreter gives (Path A) — the
parse-path unity defect is closed on BOTH routes, and the lowering refusals are exactly what the
namespace_xl0 rtp claims assert (the fix moved the CLI route to Path A's verdict, not to acceptance).

## Heal investigation (base-context artifact, resolved by rebase)

Heal failed at every pre-rebase head of this branch with 62 v1 self-compile diagnostics (type/effect cascade, no parse refusal). Bisect arms: two probe PRs (#15725 slots-reverted, #15726 peek-removed) reproduced the same 60-position cascade — and so does #15639's context NOT: keen-koi-376's #15639 carries this grammar and these claims through 4f04dd313c7 with heal AND v2-bootstrap green. ATTRIBUTION (confirmed): at the branch base 397ef748ca5, adding ONLY the claim module and its rows — no grammar change — reproduces the identical cascade (63 hard diagnostics, the same 60 src/v1 positions: 04_infer 5943, 05_emit_rust 3012, 04_resolve 897, ...; probe #15731, closed). The grammar never triggered the heal cascade; the claims enrollment at that base does. After rebase onto current main, heal AND v2-bootstrap are GREEN at head 4a3e8dd0960 (heal run 41648371154, witnesses run 41648371028). Probe #15730 (guard deletion only at base) was RED as designed — at that base the slots read the ordinary productions, so the guard is load-bearing there; this PR's condition-position rule replaces it.

## Review 90186: the site battery and the newline claim are DELETED (31dc346f90a)

Probes D1-D3 (`nl_minus_if_block_form_parses_holds`, `nl_minus_condition_is_bare_c_holds`,
`unary_minus_statement_parses_holds`), the newline-minus claim, and their fill-debt rows are
removed. The dual-role newline-minus behavior is not part of this contract; it is pinned by
the existing `newline_dual_role_operator_parse.dag` module (refusal at the line-break minus,
same-line subtraction). Bool arms cannot report a refusal reason, so the battery could not
settle its own conflict; landing scaffold that asserts behavior this PR does not change is
DESIGN §6 scaffold. The claim module now holds 15 claims, all registered, balance 0.


## Seed hole the declarative peek closes (keen-heron-809's datum, msg_7563c6e8)
The seed's condition handling retries the bare reading only when the record-literal attempt ENDS
WITHOUT ERROR (`src/v1/02_parse.dag` retry ~6139). A block starting with a labeled call —
`if a == CardOptional && b == CardOptional {\n    with_required_cardinality(n: actual)` — ERRORS the
attempt inside the braces ('expected RParen, found Colon' at `n:`), so the seed never retries and the
site fails; keen-heron parenthesized theirs in #15643. The v2 peek is declarative: the record arm is
admitted by the RESIDUE after the braces, independent of the attempt's internal error state, so this
hole does not exist here. Control `labeled_call_block_condition_still_parses_holds` pins it (green
before AND after this fix, both routes). This is a stated, deliberate divergence from the seed
(seed = oracle, not spec, DESIGN §7): the peek is strictly more permissive than the retry at exactly
these sites.

## pp7 discriminator table (pre-fix grammar, interpreted route; head a282af71d25, srv2, admitted 21:17:49Z, done 22:29:54Z, peak 4.8G, run.log `~/runs/jcp/jolly-carp-900-pp7/log.txt`)
| probe | text (cond + block + tail unless noted) | verdict pre-fix | stage |
|---|---|---|---|
| nonpun | `if c { 1 }` + tail | PARSES | refuses at lowering (`else_less_if_unlowered`) |
| paren | `if (c) { i }` + tail | PARSES | lowering (`else_less_if_unlowered`) |
| callcond | `if f(x) { i }` + tail | PARSES | lowering (`else_less_if_unlowered`) |
| elsetail | `if c { i } else { i }` | PARSES | lowering (`statement_precedes`) |
| dotcond | `if c.d { i }` + tail | **REFUSES** | PARSE (`parse_g0_tokens_remain` @153..154) |
| returnblk | `if c { return i }` + tail | PARSES | resolve-stage JSON (harness parse-ok signal) |
| blockfin_return | rtp verbatim `if c { i } then i` | PARSES | lowering (`else_less_if_unlowered`) — exactly the namespace_xl0 control's asserted pair |
| paren_record_cond | `if (p { x: 1 }) { i }` | PARSES | lowering |
| let_record | `let p = R { x }` + tail | PARSES | resolve-stage |
| arg_record | `g(R { x })` | PARSES | lowering |
| thenform_record | `if c then R { s } else 0` | **REFUSES** | PARSE (@150..151) — the guard's misfire |
| thenform_contrast | then-form control | PARSES | resolve-stage |

**Fork pinned: the punned-record reading (H-A) holds; the continuation-leak hypothesis is refuted.** Every text whose record reading is impossible (`{ 1 }`, parenthesised condition, call head, `{ return i }`) parses fine pre-fix and refuses only at lowering; the two PARSE refusals are exactly where the record arm fires (lowercase pun `c { i }`; and after a dot-suffix, `d { i }`) with no ELSE to trip the guard, plus the guard's then-form misfire. The condition production's residue peek covers the dot-suffix reach too (the gate sits on the record suffix of the condition chain, wherever it is reached). Post-fix verdicts for the RED and controls run as claims on this PR's CI (interpreted route); the emitted route reads the same grammar files (one authority, DESIGN 4) and heal regen proves the mirrors converge.

## Review responses (CI review pass + grammar-owner review, head 7d5d0d0225f)
- **Production bindings**: the five condition productions were named in the root list and referenced
  by the chain but never bound in the root `let` block — bound now, emitted identities mirroring the
  ordinary productions (lowering dispatch unchanged). The if-condition slot and the match-scrutinee
  slot are rewired to `condition_expr` / `condition_binary_expr` in the same commit; the earlier head
  left both reading the ordinary productions, which the review correctly flagged as making the guard
  deletion strictly worse. The condition chain now mirrors the ordinary `expr` arms exactly
  (fn_literal, guarded block_expr, arrow_lambda, guarded binary leaf).
- **Seed-parse form**: `Cons(head, rest)` positional multi-field payloads are not in the .dag pattern
  grammar (seed parse error at dag.dag:2022, also blocked keen-koi-376's #15639 merge); the fold is
  replaced by the std `list_head`/`list_tail` recursion idiom (`grammar_infix_operator_choice` shape).
- **Newline-aware minus (grammar-owner item 1)**: the peek now applies the SAME continuation guard
  the infix table applies (`dag_grammar_additive_newline_minus_guard`, #12817): a `-` beginning a
  line after a complete operand never continues the expression, so it must not admit a record. The
  `-` row enters the head set only as `not(after_line_break(minus))` then `minus`. No other infix row
  has a newline guard (the dual-role set is exactly `-`; the `[` index rule is separate and `[` is
  not in the head set). Claim: `newline_minus_after_if_refuses_with_guard_reason` — note the review's
  suggested expectation ("parses as if-block plus statement") contradicts the guard itself: a
  line-initial `-` after ANY complete operand, including a block-headed statement, refuses by design
  (#12817, guard comment). The claim therefore pins WHICH refusal: the guard's reason
  (`NewlineBeforeDualRoleOperator`), which is a reason-level RED against the peek fix (pre-fix the
  record swallowed `c { x }` and the refusal carried a different reason).
- **Stale comment (item 2)**: `dag_grammar_condition_record_expr` -> `dag_grammar_condition_ident_suffix_expr`.
- **Fill debt (item 3)**: the roster is the debt ledger itself — every non-retired row is
  `ActiveFillDebt` (405 rows; retirements are `RetiredFillDebt`), and its header states the
  membership rule: claims that run over the new-witness eval-step budget parsing their own source
  enter as cost debt. A new claim module that re-parses its fixture source follows the exemplar
  (`block_expr_as_binary_operand_parse`) exactly: enrolled `ActiveFillDebt`, retirement is a later
  measured transition. Cited rather than dropped.
- **dotcond as an executed RED**: added — `dotcond_with_tail_parses_holds` (the T9 text; pp7 shows
  the pre-fix parse refusal at 153..154). Twelve claims, twelve floor rows.

- **Hand-copied chain (review 38602, artifact 90169)**: fixed at 52790408085 — one builder family
  (`*_builder` fns) now produces both the ordinary and condition productions; the wrappers pass the
  threaded production and the record-arm guard. The infix-row filter answers the minus test once.
  No behavior change; peek placement unchanged.


## Review responses (artifacts 90174, 90178; head 09ad199be5a)
- 90174 (claims check acceptance, not reading): fixed by the three tree-shape witnesses above.
- 90178 (comments contradict the widened head set): all four stale comments rewritten to state
  the implemented set and the rule behind it (peek set == ordinary postfix repeat heads; corpus
  datum cited; `(` exclusion explained). DESIGN 4c: annotations now record rationale, not a
  shape the declaration does not have.

## Scope and brief (reconciled)
This PR is **R1, group D emitter slice: nested nullary-arm values**, assigned by clever-crane-830 in messages dated 2026-11-02. It is NOT the act0 baseline deletion (that work item, "Delete NamespaceBaselineObservationComplete (deletion-only)", completed as #15529/#15637; the session title is stale). Files changed: `src/v2/std/compilers/target_model.dag`, `src/v2/compiler/infer.dag`, `src/v2/compiler/target_serialize.dag`, claims under `src/v2/test/claim/{self_host,emit}`, and two RFM rows.
**Consumer rows:** the 6 `scheme: Https` rows that refuse `transform_shape_invalid` today (currency, iec_80000_13, iso8601, dimensionless, communication.medium, languages.c.emit).
**Does NOT cover:** Rust production match emission (lex tokens unwired; pinned, RFM row filed); the hard-coded `"::"` qualifier (RFM row filed, not fixed); facts-less callers (program_partition etc., unchanged, still refuse); other targets' arm spelling.
**Claim receipts by head** (srv2, run by clever-crane-830): cc2-15687g-1fa8 at 1fa80a14: closure_emission 14 PASS / 2 FAIL, the failing pair being the known main-red `ce_refusing` claims (fixed separately in #15639, pending #15695); cc2-15687h-1fa8: nested_arm_pattern_position 2/2.
**Status:** on operator HOLD; needs exact-head review and qualifying evidence including heal once the slot issue is resolved.

R1: a marked declaration reference nested in a record field or match arm reuses the facts-aware nullary-arm rule.

Root (chain re-derivation): `target_value_expr_project_body_subexpression` is facts-less. Nullary-ness is an inferred fact, so a record-construct field value or a match-arm pattern/body holding a marked declaration reference (`scheme: Https`) refused `transform_shape_invalid`, while the same reference as an arrow body took the facts-aware route and emitted `CeTsiScheme::Https`.

Change:
- `target_model.dag`: the Conj arm hands a marked declaration reference to the caller-supplied `handle_transform` (all nested positions already carry it; no signature change).
- `target_serialize.dag`: `project_nested_node_with_facts` is the callback serialize supplies; it sends Conj nodes through `project_value_node_from_inferred_facts` and everything else through the unchanged transform projection. Facts-less callers (program_partition, other claims) keep the old behavior and still refuse.
- Controls (`self_host/closure_emission`, closure route): nested record field emits `CeTsiScheme::Https`; the match claim is a declared pin of production refusal (see the update below), not a positive emission; RED: a reference to a nullary Arrow constant is not spelled as an arm.
- RFM row `target_agnostic_stage_hard_codes_one_targets_qualifier_syntax`: `nullary_coproduct_arm_binding_spelling` hard-codes Rust's `::` in a target-agnostic stage (DESIGN section 3), and this PR widens its reach to nested positions. Not fixed here; next-rung trigger is reading `scope_separator_text` from the target's `DeclarationReferenceForm`.

Consumers: the six `scheme: Https` rows (currency, iec_80000_13, iso8601, dimensionless, communication.medium, languages.c.emit). Executed on srv2; receipts above.

Update after the first srv2 run:
- Match-arm PATTERNS carry no inferred facts (inference types values, not patterns). `infer_nullary_zero_param_coproduct_arm_declared` (infer.dag) asks the declaration directly; the facts version delegates to it. `project_nested_node_with_facts` uses it only when facts are absent AND `node_is_match_arm_pattern` holds, so `facts_absent` stays the refusal at every other position.
- Value-position RED (a marked reference with missing facts still refuses `facts_absent`) is NOT authorable: the real route infers facts at every value position, so no source produces a missing fact there (DESIGN 4b). Substitute control: `v2.test.claim.emit.nested_arm_pattern_position` asserts the guard is true for an arm pattern and false for the same-spelling arm body.

## Update: match claim re-shaped as a declared pin (head 1fa80a14)
The srv2 probe showed the match member refuses `target_lex_rule_literal_not_found` AFTER projection succeeds: the production Rust lex has no rule for `rust_token_unwired_match` / `rust_token_unwired_fat_arrow` (they exist only in `rust_staging_match_additional_lex_rules`). So production Rust match emission is a separate unwired gap, not R1. The match claim now pins TODAY's behaviour (refuses with that reason); the trigger is the production match-emission wiring PR (rustc-validated rules), which flips it to the positive `CeTsiScheme::Https =>` assertion. New RFM row `production_rust_lex_leaves_match_tokens_unwired`. R1 claims exactly: record-field emission, the structural pattern-position controls (`nested_arm_pattern_position`), and the arrow-constant RED.

# Cross-tree import model lane: an authored construct tag is read from the EXPECTED TYPE's declared constructor set

Design note (read and ruled first): `docs/plans/native-construct-tag-expected-type-arm.md` on
`scratch/t4-a2a4`. Ruling: tidy-ant-251, 2026-11-02 — "Where the expected type is resolved, its
declared constructor set is the AUTHORITY. Exactly one matching arm binds, recorded as
BoundByExpectedType. No match refuses with the new typed cause
`resolve_construct_tag_not_in_expected_type`, never falling back to the name door. Two matching arms,
or an expected type without a unique declaration, refuses as ambiguous. The name door applies only
where no expected type is carried."

## What lands

Two producers, one rule each, plus the enrollment. Folded in per tidy-ant-251's rulings of 2026-11-02:
the expectation carry (scrutinee and record-field) belongs to this PR because a PR whose executed diff
moves nothing in its own bounded set has no consumer (DESIGN section 3c), and the bare-atom leg belongs
here because the same rule owns both readings of an arm pattern. A third leg (inference reading resolve's
record) was ruled in, landed, and is WITHDRAWN on executed evidence -- recorded below rather than deleted.

1. **An authored construct tag in a term position** is read from the expected type's declared constructor
   set -- the door order ruled above, described in full below.
2. **A bare atom in a PATTERN position** is read by the same rule, with the joint precedence jolly-cat-271
   and I agreed and tidy-ant-251 ruled: the visible-value gate first, then the constructor reading by the
   expected set, then the binder; and where the expected type is NOT readable while the spelling names a
   nullary constructor visible in scope, it REFUSES with `resolve_reason_pattern_atom_constructor_type_unresolved`
   rather than silently binding a catch-all.
3. A third leg -- inference classifying an arm from resolve's recorded binding (option (i), ruled by
   tidy-ant-251 after jolly-cat-271's report, shape approved by keen-heron-809) -- **landed and came back
   out**, claim-for-claim identical to main with the hunk removed. The finding is stated below; no repair
   and no recurring-failure-mode row are claimed for it.

In `v2.compiler.resolve`, an AUTHORED construct tag (`ConstructTagAuthored`, i.e. a tag the source
spelled — not an elided head, which the elided door already reads from the expected type) is now
resolved against the constructor set of the type the position expects:

* **exactly one arm of that set carries the spelling** → it binds, and the binding is recorded as
  `BoundByExpectedType` through a new `ModuleBindingRoute.ExpectedTypeConstructorRoute`, so the
  occurrence census labels it `expected_type` rather than `ambient_name`
  (`v2.compiler.occurrence_resolution_census occurrence_resolution_source` already maps that binding
  to `SourceExpectedType` — this is what makes an before/after join readable per occurrence);
* **no arm of the set carries it** → refused with the new typed cause
  `resolve_construct_tag_not_in_expected_type`, located at the tag, and **no other door is consulted**;
* **the expected type declares the spelling twice**, or the lookup is ambiguous → refused as
  ambiguous, with a new `AmbiguousLookupClass` arm (`AmbiguousInExpectedConstructorSet`) whose
  competing declarations are the ARM PATHS, carried in the same order as every other ambiguity here
  (class row, competing declarations, fatal last). The set never picks one;
* **a name-door hit is admitted BY the set, not by the hit alone.** Today's hit path is reproduced
  bit-for-bit, so no already-bound site changes identity; a hit the set does not declare is the
  mismatch the ruling named, and it refuses;
* **the gate that decides whether an expectation reaches a construct at all**
  (`resolve_node_consumes_expectation`, called only from `resolve_arrow_body_or_named_edge`) now admits
  an authored tag. It used to answer `false` for one — the comment read "only a headless literal or a
  list literal consumes the expectation" — so an authored construct standing in a **declared-return or
  data-initializer position** was walked with NO expectation at all, and the set authority above could
  only reach a tag nested under an expectation that was already flowing (a record field under a resolved
  record, the children of an elided head, a map-literal value). Most of the A2 sites stand at that
  gate, so without this arm the rule would have been unreachable where it is needed. What the gate
  changes is which set the tag is read from and which rule walks its fields; the scope a construct is
  walked in does not move, because `resolve_expected_authored_construct_edge` reads the plain door's own
  context pipeline and a `Positional` edge still pushes nothing.

* **no expectation, or an expectation whose head has no readable constructor set** (a type parameter,
  a non-pure alias — `type Char = Int where unicode_scalar, brand("Char")` — an opaque or primitive
  head, a contested head) → the name door answers exactly as it does today, with exactly today's cause.
  `type_decl_view` answers `TypeAlias` for an alias, so an alias head is never treated as a
  constructor set. Pure renamings (`type List<element> = FreeMonoid<element>`) are already followed by
  `resolve_expected_head_path`, so their arm sets ARE readable.

## Producers changed, one rule each

* One door, not two (this is the shape keen-heron-809's review produced). `resolve_node_walk` is now a
  thin wrapper over `resolve_node_walk_in(ctx, n, expected)`; `resolve_node_walk_entered`,
  `resolve_child_edge_in` and `resolve_labeled_child_edge_in` thread `Optional<ResolveExpectation>`
  through the existing pipeline, the authored-head arm reads the threaded expectation directly, and the
  elided-head arm keeps routing to `resolve_elided_construct_walk` (the producer `resolve_expected_edge`
  already reached). `resolve_labeled_child_edge` keeps its two-parameter signature for its existing
  caller in `v2.compiler.name_resolve` and delegates to the `_in` form, whose body is the same context
  pipeline in place — no extracted helper, no copied pipeline. A `Positional` edge still pushes nothing,
  and the module-root preservation arm keeps `resolve_child_edge`'s answer.
  The first shape of this PR copied the pipeline into a second door
  (`resolve_expected_authored_construct_edge` plus a parallel pattern edge) and that was wrong: the copy
  skipped `resolve_node_walk`, so `resolve_declaring_entering` (the spine-body declaring transition) and
  the generated-reference and where-refinement arms of `resolve_node_walk_entered` never ran at exactly
  the data-initializer and declared-return bodies the flip routes there. All three copied helpers are
  deleted and have no callers.
* `resolve_pattern_node_walk` → `resolve_pattern_node_walk_in(ctx, pat, expected)` plus new
  `resolve_pattern_field_edge` (pattern position). This is the one place a NEW expectation starts flowing where none flowed before:
  today the pattern walk dropped the tag's resolved declaration path, so a pattern field's contents
  had no expected type to be read against, and a nested pattern tag could only ever use the name door.
  With the path kept, the field's declared type becomes the expectation. A pattern target that is not
  a construct, and any field whose tag did not resolve to a declaration, keep `resolve_pattern_node_walk`
  unchanged.
* `resolve_construct_walk` / `resolve_construct_walk_with_tag` / `resolve_construct_tag_walk` /
  `resolve_construct_tag_reference` carry `Optional<ResolveExpectation>` down to the tag door; the
  projection door and the no-expectation sites pass `optional_absent()`.
* The arm-set fold `coproduct_variant_paths_of` is shared with `resolve_kind_variant_paths_optional`
  (the fold was inlined there; it is now read from one place, not duplicated).

### A bare atom in a pattern position (folded in, ruling 2)

The A2 population lives mostly HERE, not in term position: of the 38 unbound A2 constructor-name sites in
the 30-module bounded set (from clever-crane-830's `cc2-15637t2` rows), **18 sit at match-arm heads** and
**16 are payload-absent**, and the dominant corpus shape is `ComputationNode { behavior: Value }` -- a
nullary arm spelling inside a FIELD pattern under an `OperationBehavior`-typed field. Reading the rule from
`resolve_match_arm_walk`, `resolve_pattern_atom_names_frame_value` / `_module_value`,
`resolve_catch_all_binder_read_gate` and `resolve_pattern_atom_names_constructor`:

* the visible-value gate runs FIRST, as jolly-cat-271 required: a spelling that also names a frame value or
  a module-level value stays the loud refusal it is today (`resolve_reason_pattern_atom_names_visible_value`).
  Constructor-first would hide exactly the shadowing that gate exists to make loud;
* then `resolve_pattern_atom_constructor_reading`: if the expected type's declared constructor set carries
  the spelling and the arm declares no payload fields, the atom IS that constructor, bound
  `ExpectedTypeConstructorRoute`; the field's declared type is threaded in, so a nullary arm nested in a
  field pattern reaches the same door;
* **no default rank, no silent binder**: if the expected type is not readable and the spelling names a
  nullary constructor visible in scope, refuse with `resolve_reason_pattern_atom_constructor_type_unresolved`,
  located at the pattern node, with the correction row `CorrectionNotModeled` -- one text must not change
  meaning depending on whether a type happened to be reachable (DESIGN section 5, the same shape as the
  acquirer-entry ruling);
* otherwise the atom is whatever it is today: a binder, under jolly-cat-271's bare-atom-binds-its-arm lane
  (`#15380`), whose readers I do not touch -- it edits `infer_match_coproduct_rows`' call and the catch-all
  widening only, and does not change `InferCoproductArmRow`, so this PR builds on main and rebases over a
  type rename in that one function if #15380 lands first;
* the exclusion from BINDERS happens at the ONE collection point, `v2.compiler.lexical_scope
  pattern_binder_candidates`, keyed by the atom's OCCURRENCE (`NodeOccurrenceIdentity`), not by spelling or
  position -- `pattern_binders`, `resolve_pattern_atom_naming_a_frame_value`, `resolve_pattern_binders`,
  `resolve_catch_all_binder_read_gate` and the binder-frame readers all read that one list, and the misspelling
  guard survives, though not as first claimed: `Boxed { behavior: Absnet }` names nothing in the set, so the
  reading answers "not a constructor" and the spelling falls through to jolly-cat-271's atom rule: it stays a
  BINDER and the module is Accepted. The first version of this bullet predicted
  `resolve_reason_unbound_symbol` there; the claim asserting that read RED at row `cc2-15671-ctag10`
  (2026-11-03) and tidy-ant-251 ruled that the fall-through is the behavior to keep -- the code does not
  invent a refusal at a position whose rule it did not change (DESIGN 5). The claim is now
  `an_atom_outside_the_expected_set_binds_as_a_catch_all_binder`, it asserts the binder reading, and it
  cites the ledger row that carries the residual. The unread-binder gate's own refusal
  (`resolve_reason_catch_all_binder_unread`) stays claimed elsewhere.

### The asymmetry this PR creates, stated plainly (rule KEPT by tidy-ant-251, 2026-11-03)

One bare uppercase name now has two readings, and they are not symmetric:

| position | an arm of the expected type | NOT an arm of a readable expected set |
| --- | --- | --- |
| construct **tag** (value position, or a pattern head with a payload) | binds that arm, recorded as bound by expected type | **refuses**: `resolve_construct_tag_not_in_expected_type` |
| pattern **atom** (a nullary arm spelling) | binds that arm | **stays a catch-all binder: Accepted, silently** |

Why they differ: the tag rule is this PR's, and it is allowed to refuse because the expected set is in hand
and the spelling names a *constructor-shaped* thing in a position that only ever holds constructors. The atom
rule is #15125's precedence (an atom is a binder unless the symbol index names it a declared payload;
case-blind; last, even when a readable set lacks the spelling); refusing the atom spelling was considered
there and **not adopted**. This PR does not change binder precedence -- that is jolly-cat-271's design area
and a ruling for tidy-ant-251 -- so the asymmetry is shipped, and shipping an asymmetry silently is the
failure mode DESIGN 5 names. So it is recorded, not buried:

* `gunbc.recurring_failure_mode a_misspelled_nullary_variant_in_the_last_arm_reads_as_a_catch_all_binder`
  carries it, with the review tell widened and two evidence references (the claim and the shipped reading);
* the compensating refusal is `resolve_catch_all_binder_read_gate`, and it covers only a **top-level arm**
  binder its arm body never reads (remedy `_`). A field-position binder the body *does* read --
  `Boxed { behavior: Absnet } => 0`, where `behavior: Behavior = Value | Call` -- is uncovered: the binder
  takes the whole field domain, a two-alternative remainder that includes the nullary `Value`, which is the
  case the ladder refuses at a top-level arm position and does not reach one level down. Whether the
  widening gate catches it at a sub-pattern is the datum the ledger row marks PENDING; the claim above is
  that measurement;
* the next trigger is written in that row: making a sub-pattern atom outside the readable set refuse, as the
  tag rule already does, is a precedence ruling by tidy-ant-251 with jolly-cat-271 owning the design, and
  the claim flips when it lands.

### Carrying the expectation to a nested position: the located cause of the first four red arms

The rule above is useless at a nested site unless the expected type ARRIVES there. At the first claim row
(cc2-ctag8-897d, 16 PASS / 19 FAIL) every nested position failed the same way -- a value under a record
field, a field pattern, a projected scrutinee, a rename-headed expectation -- and the elimination probes said

cause is one line of index shape: `v2.compiler.symbol_index_fill` sites a coproduct arm at
`<type path>.<arm>` with the **payload record as the entry** (`kind: VariantArmPayload`), and
`resolve_record_field_type_optional` asked `type_decl_view` for a type declaration. A payload site is not a
type declaration, so the read answered Absent, every field of such an arm walked as an ordinary child, and an
arm alias -- sited only in its declaring module's scope -- has no name-door answer for an importer.

`TypeNode { connective: Conj }`, the entry IS the payload record, so the field is read there. Nothing else in
the function changes, the field-name lookup reuses the existing `v2.std.node_query declared_field_named`
authority that resolve already uses elsewhere, and a path that holds no such entry still answers Absent.

## Frontiers this PR states rather than closes

* **Argument position stays as today.** An expectation is not carried into call arguments, so an A2 tag in an
  argument keeps `resolve_reason_unbound_symbol`. Accepted as out of reach by tidy-ant-251; the trigger that
  brings it in is "expectation into call arguments".
* **The two-module pair arm is the discriminating RED for the resolve leg, executed on the real path.** At
  the base leg -- main's compiler plus this claim file only, `e9e4ad1f`, row cc2-mbtred-e9e4ad1f -- the arm is
  RED and its reading is `[resolve_reason_unbound_symbol]`: resolve refuses the site, because the name door
  cannot see an arm that lives only in its declaring module's scope. At this head (row cc2-mbt-897d) the same
  arm PASSES with neither arm-shape diagnostic. The resolve-only ref (`f68c6763`, this head with `infer.dag`
  restored to main, row cc2-mbtres-f68c) is claim-for-claim identical to the head -- that is the executed
  reason the inference leg came out. The question this section used to leave open, whether
  `assemble_program_from_ingest` resolves `import q { C }` across two ingested witnesses with no admission
  import, is settled by those rows: it does, and no fixture changed.

* **The residual hole, stated.** An atom with no recorded declaration and no visible nullary constructor
  keeps today's binder reading, so one text still has two readings depending on whether an expected type
  resolved -- the hole is narrowed to "a spelling that names no constructor in scope", not closed. Whether
  unresolved-plus-matching-a-visible-nullary-constructor should refuse rather than bind was decided by
  tidy-ant-251 as REFUSE (fail-closed), and it is what the code does; the remaining case is one that names
  nothing at all.
* **Payload-bearing arms in pattern position bind by the same door only where the arm is reached**; the
  nullary-versus-payload question clever-crane-830 raised was measured, not argued: 16 of the 38 A2 sites are
  payload-absent and 18 sit at match-arm heads, which is why the scrutinee carry is inside this PR.

### Red at the base of this module, not regressed and not claimed

`v2.test.claim.match_binder.match_binder_typing` carries four arms that FAIL at every head measured here,
including the base leg where the compiler has none of this PR's hunks:

* `mbt_the_binder_is_typed_from_its_variant_field_holds`
* `mbt_the_match_is_typed_by_its_binder_arm_holds`
* `mbt_the_sevens_call_scrutinee_is_typed_and_its_constructor_bodies_are_counted_holds`
* `mbt_an_underived_arm_body_is_a_counted_frontier_holds`

Executed: cc2-mbt-897d (this head) 20 PASS / 4 FAIL and cc2-mbtred-e9e4ad1f (main + this file only) 19 PASS /
5 FAIL -- the failing set is these four in both, the fifth at the base being this PR's pair arm. So they are
that module's rows, not a regression of this PR; nothing here touches them. The cause is UNATTRIBUTED: Bool
claims carry no cause line, and jolly-cat-271 (the module's author) has no executed reading either, so they
are recorded as "red at base per clever-crane-830, cause unattributed" rather than as a known state. They are
the first item of the follow-up work item on my node that tidy-ant-251 assigned after #15656 lands, together
with the ten `char_at` not-held pairs and `account_controls_route_witness`.

## Not in this PR, as ruled

* Map type-name sites (`v2.std.compilation_unit`, `v2.std.syntax`) — already inside valiant-fox-335's
  first Map unit. PartialFunction type-name sites — zesty-badger-599's type-position reader (with
  `Disposition`, `TargetEffectApplyShape`); the two sites were sent there.
* The 17 spellings that have contract rows and still refuse — routed to the wave lane.
* A tag whose expected type is a type parameter (R8) stays a refusal with its own rung_drop row; the
  arm does not give it a constructor set it does not have.

### The static screen over the whole corpus: what it supports, and what it does not

A Python reader of the `.dag` trees (not the compiler) walked every module under `dag/` and `src/v2` at this
head -- **298,447** authored construct sites: 280,532 carry no readable expectation, 10,527 carry a readable
expectation whose bound declaration is already the expected type's arm (`SAME`), and the rest keep the name
door for a named reason (alias 3,817; imported name that is not a type 1,878; record head 1,138; head is not
a declared type 246; declaring module not loaded 173). Its change classes: **78 bound-site-now-refused** (all
in expression position; ZERO in pattern position), 52 unbound-site-refused-by-the-new-cause, 6
unbound-site-now-bound, and **0 different-declaration** -- the stop class is empty corpus-wide, which is the
number this PR leans on.

That 78 is an UPPER BOUND with three named inflation modes -- `Sha256Hash` under a `ContentHash` coproduct
whose arms the screen mis-derives (16), a record constructor under a record or alias head, which
`constructor_set_of_type_member` answers with its own head (12), and `Present` under an `Optional<...>` head,
whose arm set `dag/std/optional.dag` does declare (7); all three are read out in the bounded-identity section
above -- and with one named UNDER-count: the screen reads a record field's type the way main's compiler does,
so it cannot see the sites my payload-entry branch makes expectation-carrying inside a coproduct arm's payload.
So 78 is an upper bound for the positions the screen models and a lower bound for the ones it does not.


What the screen cannot do is stamp a verdict on a site, and no executed before/after census pair exists to do
it either -- the census is retired process and clever-crane-830 has ruled this PR's evidence as the three claim
rows. So the bound-to-refused class is claimed by SHAPE, one fixture per shape, in the claim module: a
coinciding label whose expected set holds an arm of that name (refuses with the new cause); an arm-pattern tag
the scrutinee's type does not declare while the name door holds another module's declaration (refuses with the
new cause); a tag inside a record field under a readable expectation (binds). The stop condition -- a
name-door binding replaced by a DIFFERENT declaration at a position whose expected type declares the arm -- is
empty in both static passes (0 of 298,447 corpus-wide, 0 of 7,754 in the A2 set) and is claimed in the
affirmative by the first two of those shapes, which is what makes the zero mean something rather than nothing.

## Review asks

`v2.compiler.resolve` is load-bearing, so the bar here is the one the manager set: a RED per arm plus
controls, the bounded identity diff, and required CI. The hunks that deserve a second pair of eyes:
`resolve_node_walk_in` / `resolve_node_walk_entered` / `resolve_child_edge_in` /
`resolve_labeled_child_edge_in` (one door threading the expectation — the equivalence question is that
every arm of the plain door still runs, including the declaring-transition, generated-reference and
where-refinement arms keen-heron-809 named, and that the `Positional` case pushes nothing);
`resolve_construct_tag_under_expected_constructor_set` (the door order, including the LexicalHit branch
that refuses a hit the set does not declare); and `resolve_pattern_field_edge` (the one place a NEW
expectation starts flowing where none flowed before); `resolve_scrutinee_declared_type` and
`resolve_match_child_step` (the scrutinee carry, ruling 1 -- the declared type of a match scrutinee, through
a field projection or an atom type node, into the arm patterns through the SAME shared door);
`resolve_pattern_atom_constructor_reading` with `resolve_pattern_visible_nullary_constructor_path` (the
precedence jolly-cat-271 and I agreed, and the fail-closed refusal when the set is unreadable);
`pattern_binders` plus `pattern_atom_is_bound_by_the_expected_set` (the exclusion at the one collection
point, keyed by `NodeOccurrenceIdentity` -- a local filter would leave the other three binder readers and the
infer-side check seeing a binder); and `infer_coproduct_arm_pattern(pat, resolved)` with
`pattern_atom_bound_declaration` (one classifier, keyed on what the atom is bound to rather than which route
bound it). keen-heron-809 reviewed the resolve hunks and the shape of the infer hunk; jolly-cat-271 reviewed
the atom precedence and the collection-point exclusion.

## Purpose (DESIGN §3 maintenance — serves the v2 self-host)
This PR carries the **emitter binder-capture fix only** (`05_emit_rust.dag` rc-ref pattern/prelude pair rule), its RFM row, and the `//gunbc/instruments:pattern-binder-capture` sentinel. The emitted gen-1 realization is what executes the v2 self-host, so pattern-emission fidelity serves the self-host directly. The v1 seed is maintenance-active; admitted because it serves the v2 self-host. Ownership: `clever-crane-830` owns and reviews the emitter side (condition 1).

---
## Attribution correction (condition 3) — the parse-divergence premise is WITHDRAWN
This PR opened on the claim that the emitted CLI refuses at PARSE (`parse_g0_tokens_remain`) what the interpreted route accepts (refusing only later at lowering with `else_less_if_unlowered`) on the else-less-if member text (`if c { i }` + tail `i`). That claim is **refuted**: **cc2-pp6 @ `32dfa37d`** (srv2, run.log `dc759c24`) ran the identical texts on **BOTH** executors and they **AGREE** — the interpreted route also refuses at PARSE with `parse_g0_tokens_remain` (leftover at the tail `i` 151..152; sameline 149..150; blockfinal at the fn closing `}` 149..150), while if-with-else and two-plain-statement texts parse on both. The earlier divergence attribution came from pre-pp6 runs whose interpreted halves had not completed (the `spans` call-shape defect at `7d2215af`). There is **no emitted-vs-interpreted parse divergence** on this input; the RFM row `emitted_parse_refuses_a_grammatical_input_the_interpreter_accepts` is withdrawn in this PR (it described a class that does not exist).

The real defect — else-less `if c { i }` followed by a statement refuses at PARSE **on both routes** — is a **grammar/parser** defect (punned-record condition vs post-block continuation; the fork is a HYPOTHESIS until the discriminating probe row lands), tracked and fixed in its own PR under grammar-owner review (`keen-heron-809`), not here. Reading-complete artifacts (fragments1–13) established no executor difference; all read-faithful combinator/analysis code remains a useful negative result for that PR.

---
## SECOND FIX (independent, already true regardless of the CAUSE above): emitter binder capture
`emit_pattern_rc_aware`'s `field_needs_rc_ref` branch (src/v1/05_emit_rust.dag) emitted `ref <field_name>` for Rc-shared payload fields, binding the pattern field under its FIELD name and discarding the arm's declared binding variable. When the `.dag` arm renames the binding (`Accepted { table: table1 }`) and the body also reads a same-named OUTER variable (the `table` parameter), Rust resolves the body reference to the shadowing pattern binding. Confirmed instance: both arms of `parse_expr_not_predicate_attempt` (emitted v2_compiler_parse.rs `188439f2` lines 3754/3758 vs parse.dag:4403-4416): emitted `table.furthest` reads the INNER table; the `.dag` reads the parameter's. Crate-wide grep over the seed emission: sole instance. Impact: `furthest` feeds only the `tokens_remain` diagnostic locus — no accept/reject change — so this is fidelity of the error position, not today's verdict cause. Fixed by the general rule (commits 33a7deec3 + ee4970b34): the rc-ref **pattern and its prelude are one pair** — renaming only the pattern severs it (the prelude head `let bound_str = <fb_name>.as_ref()` would read the outer: type error, or silent inversion when the outer type also has `as_ref`). The binder and every consumer derive ONE emitter-owned name via `rc_field_binder_name` (`__rc_<field>`, no `.dag` identifier can collide): pattern renders `field: ref __rc_field`; `rc_pattern_preludes` head reads `__rc_field.as_ref()`; `rc_field_selection_test` matches! source and the two-stage plan second match (both twins) read the same binder. The arm body never names the binder — it reads the declared variable or the nested destructuring — so no same-named outer can be captured anywhere in the pair. RFM row: `dag/gunbc/recurring_failure_mode/emitted_pattern_field_bound_under_its_own_name_captures_an_outer_binding.dag`.

**Breadth (DESIGN 6b) — the arms inventory**: in `emit_pattern_rc_aware`/`emit_resolved_variant_pattern_rc_aware` the arms binding by the matched field name are the `field_needs_rc_ref` **named arm and its single-field fast path** (the fast path was missed on the first head; the heal regen caught the pair mismatch as E0425 `__rc_view` in the `type_head_exposure` mirror — fixed in ddf083b23df; the pair rule now holds at every rc-field render site). Every sibling binds under the declared variable: Bind leaf (`emit_ident(declaration.name)`); non-rc sibling (shorthand -> the field name IS the declared name; rename -> `field: <recursive pattern>`); tuple/positional payloads (`qualified(inner_pat)` recursion); string-literal field patterns (fresh `pattern_string_binding_name(path)` name); the non-rc twin `emit_pattern` has no `field_needs_rc_ref` branch at all (its only `ref` arm is the string-literal one). So the crate-wide instance grep is also an arm-level proof.

**Sibling sites served by the same lowering (cond1)**: the mis-emitted arm lives in the lowering of `parse_expr_not_predicate_attempt` (parse.dag), which is the single lowering for the `grammar_expr_not_predicate(...)` node — every such grammar site reaches it, and under RC every such arm took the field-name-binding branch. The complete site list in `src/v2/extdeps/languages/dag.dag` (19 call sites, enclosing fn in parentheses): declared_path_expr 1002; value_name_guard 1102; stmt_expr 1568; let_in_refusal_expr 1582; expr_expr 1733 and 1739; additive_newline_minus_guard 1793; record_field_init_list_helper 1859; postfix_index_suffix_expr 1956; primary_ident_suffix_expr 2006 (the guard named in the parse-verdict class: `block_of_one_name_before_else`); primary_expr_core 2103; arg_expr 2191; match_arm_stmt_body_statement 2272; match_arm_expr 2315; arrow_lambda_body_expr 2549; status_pattern_expr 2934; op_requires_expr 3035; module_expr 3450 and 3453. All 19 share the one lowering and are covered by the one pair fix; the sentinel fixture mirrors site 2006's node shape. The `optional(...)` inventory (51 sites) is carried into the parser-lane PR; its affected set is the statement-continuation subset.

**RED for this fix (review B2)**: new instrument `//gunbc/instruments:pattern-binder-capture` (`NativeClaimProgramProducer` entry `dag/gunbc/instruments/pattern_binder_capture_native.dag`, sibling of last-use-move / exit-return-ownership / cons-tail-recursion). Fixtures executed on the EMITTED route: `renamed_bind_capture` — the `parse_expr_not_predicate_attempt` shape itself: arm `AcceptedProbe { ..., table: table1 }` renames the field, body reads the outer parameter `table` AND `table1`; holds only reading the OUTER value (77135; the capture class observes 13135). `shorthand_bind` and `nested_variant_rename` hold on both legs and fence the fix from over-reaching. **RED: the entry built at the pre-fix seed (v2_compiler_parse.rs sha 188439f2) must exit NOT-HELD (1); built at the fix it must exit HELD (0).** Both legs are run by host runs — this label is executed by host runs, NOT by the required job; the class rung is mechanical-by-label, not gate-enrolled.



---
## Verification status
- **CI**: GREEN on head ddf083b23df — `v2-bootstrap` (the required witness, run 41427515521) and `heal` (run 41427515534) both pass. On the prior head 85e77f9cb9f the witness passed but heal failed with rustc E0425 (`__rc_view` readers vs the `ref view` fast-path pattern) — the fast-path pair mismatch above, fixed in ddf083b23df. (An earlier heal failure at 6ed6849d was fleet contention: the heal-pr workflow's `cancel-in-progress` concurrency group cancelled each other across branches; the re-run produced the real failure.)
- **Sentinel two-legs** (clever-crane-830, Butch `cc-15648lp`): LEG A restores base `src/v1/05_emit_rust.dag` (label must exit 1), LEG B the head (exit 0). Heads moved during review; legs to be pinned on the final green-CI head.
- **CI does not execute arbitrary claims**: the equality/claim rows on the parse-verdict side would be judged by nothing on the required path; the sentinel (executed by host runs) and the heal/bootstrap witnesses are the enforcement here, per the fleet's v2-bootstrap design (clever-crane-830 correction, adopted).

**A match arm that applies one generic template to a disagreeing concrete argument no longer joins**

Assignment routed by keen-otter-392 (from quick-newt-573): frontend acceptance admitted a distinct-record return. At main 70f502743c4c, `wla_inferred_with` is declared `-> Outcome<InferredTree>` but its `Accepted` arm returns `infer()`, an `Outcome<ObligatedInferredTree>`.

**Located by execution, not by reading** (srv2, seed acceptance route via `compile_dag_diagnostic_census`):
- `kh-recprobe`: a bare distinct record **refuses**, and so does a user-generic **product** (`Wrap<RB>` as `Wrap<RA>`). A user-generic **coproduct** returned from a match arm was **accepted**.
- `kh-recprobe2`: the coproduct **refuses** when returned directly, through a call, and from a match whose arms all agree. It is **accepted** only for `match r { Lost => Lost  Got {..} => s | mk(b) }`, a bare nullary sibling arm.
- Mechanism: `infer_expr` passes the declared `Res<RA>` as the expected type, so `Lost` types as `Res<RA>` and becomes the elected arm type. `v1.compiler.infer` `match_arm_join_diagnostics` judged a disagreeing arm only for bare/optional mixing and proven-disjoint heads, so `Res<RA>` vs `Res<RB>` (same head) passed, and the elected type then satisfied the declared return.

**Fix: the least general rule (parent ruling, §6b).** This is the arm-level twin of Q2's "an unsolved K does not license a wrong V", so ONE rule serves both:
- `application_pair` widens from collections to **two applications of one resolved declaration**, decided by identity (`type_reference_declaration_ref` + `declaration_ref_eq`), never spelling. The collection arm keeps its algebra-keyed test. `a.Foo<Int>` vs `b.Foo<Int>` is not a pair.
- The arm join consumes Q2's `application_arguments_inhabitance` through `arm_application_argument_refused`. A concrete per-argument refusal refuses the arm (`DeclaredTypeNotInhabited` at "match arm"). An argument still holding an unsolved variable is Undecidable, so the under-determined arm still joins.

**Evidence (executed)**: srv2 `kh-arm2` at 5ececb024048, ledger-admitted, memory.peak 13.09 GB. `--required-regen` named only `v1_compiler_infer.rs` (installed sha256 `db977634…72db`, committed in ddcce7e5ef37); the second regen reported `first_generation_equal=true`. gunbc `dc0cd15f…ddb5`, built 2026-11-02T04:02:32Z.
- `test.claim.match_arm_application_witness` **6/6**: both REDs (the probe shapes) refuse; agreeing arms and an under-determined arm beside a lawful rebuild join; a direct mismatch and a bare record still refuse.
- Q2 `declared_container_argument_witness` 13/13 (the widening regressed nothing); Q1d 3/3; anonymous-record roster 7/7.
- `gunbc test //gunbc/instruments:self-host` RC=0.

RFM: `gunbc.recurring_failure_mode` `an_under_determined_match_arm_licenses_a_wrong_sibling_application`, read AtCeiling with this receipt.

**Pending before the LAND ask** (scope per sleek-owl's 2026-11-05 ruling): ONE private roster row over gunbc-private main 9db4c41fb199, placed through calm-crab-645 under a keen-otter execution grant (job k15643-p2, srv1; execution currently on HOLD). Acceptance per sleek-owl msg_01ac5c25: VERDICT=OBSERVED (private_roster_main ran to its own exit; no TIMEOUT, signal, OOM rise or UNKNOWN oom read); head and tree checks pass for both repos; resolve_phase_line_present >= 1 and resolve_failed_lines = 0; does_not_inhabit_lines = 0, or each quoted line accounted for. The v1 driver's outer status is UNRESOLVED by construction and is disclosed here; the side-chat LAND at the exact head closes the gate. TIMEOUT or NO_OBSERVATION is not a pass. The arm-join widening previously broke private main after landing, and nothing on the public required path sees that repo. Surfaced consumers are listed here and migrated by discharging, never by dropping obligations.

**Not run, disclosed:** the public whole-corpus `generated_artifact_gate` main_wet is NOT a landing gate (the #15663 ruling, under the census retirement). The executed public check is heal's corpus resolve under the new checker: SUCCESS with `changed_paths=0` at the landing head.

**Consumer:** `wla_inferred_with` is migrated by bold-dove-340's #15630 (via `v2.compiler.refinement_discharge` `infer_and_discharge`). #15630 should land first.

## Update (head 3de99171): the pair is re-specified to the door's contract
Probe cc2-refusing-8958 (srv2, at d7c5/8958): the else-less member now PARSES (via #15695) and refuses at lowering, located: `body_lowering_reason_else_less_if_unlowered @ ce_refusing_member_read bytes 101..103`, as a WHOLE-EMISSION Rejected. Body lowering runs in normalization (`closure_emission` `closure_member_normalized`), and the door's contract is that a parse or normalization refusal refuses the whole emission while a member's own refusal is that member's arm. The old claims asserted an Accepted carrier with a refused arm, which the door does not give for this refusal; the fixture was wrong, not the door. No door change.
- `a_closure_member_whose_body_does_not_lower_refuses_the_whole_emission_located_holds`: Rejected + reason `body_lowering_reason_else_less_if_unlowered` + location (member file, span 101..103). Reds if it becomes Accepted or the reason or location moves.
- `the_first_refusal_of_a_closure_is_the_first_refused_arms_cause_holds` now uses `ce_emission_unbound_name` (arm refused at resolve). That fixture is therefore SHARED with `a_name_the_ingest_does_not_bind_refuses_its_member_and_never_widens_the_closure_holds`.

- Landing waits on #15695 (its fix at 09ad199b for the `review_sheet_converge_witness.dag:1745` parse-population failure); I re-merge its green head, then re-run.

The two pre-existing red claims in v2.test.claim.self_host.closure_emission (member body refuses; entry reaches a refusing member) were red for a FIXTURE reason and never evidence about body lowering. The old member text `fn ce_refusing_fn(p: Bool) -> Bool { if p { p } }` does not parse: the real front end refuses it with parse_g0_tokens_remain (receipt cc2-ceprobe, main 4314d320, gen-1 CLI 9ac7f798), so the claim saw a Rejected closure instead of a refused member arm. ## FINDING (parked as draft): two native front ends disagree on one text
srv2 cc2-ceprobe, cc2-ceprobe2, cc2-ceprobe3 (latest at main 0dc96e1e, seed gunbc 9e5ee601, gen-1 CLI 3ffe505e; receipts srv2:~/runs/cc2/cc2-ceprobe3/out/, emit.err sha256 837b2a71, byte-identical across runs): the CLI acquisition front end refuses with `parse_g0_tokens_remain` on every else-less-if member text tried, including `rtp_guard_fallthrough_source` taken verbatim from src/v2/test/claim/namespace_xl0/return_tail_position.dag, which main's claims accept on the route native_test_context_from_ingest -> native_census_module_resolution (they then refuse at lowering, else_less_if_unlowered). So the two ce_refusing claims are red for a PARSE reason on the CLI route, and no fixture change can reach the lowering refusal there (option b for the CLI route). DESIGN 4 (one grammar) says the two parse paths cannot disagree; whether it is a different parser, tokenizer mode or a stricter prefix in parse_module_prepared_seeded is not yet known. Owner: the front end (parsing). This PR is parked; not for landing until that is resolved.

**Why it could not be in #15507.** The heal job builds its generator from main's stage0 mirrors (`claim_executor --regen-round-cost --base-mirror`). Until #15507 landed, main had no `primitive_string_length` projection row, so a self-call body emitted as bare Rust recursion. Now the row is on main (#15507, 2d145445).
