The generated-DESIGN witness required every design_ruling ledger row to appear in the document, so an uncited ruling made it fail. This change checks the typed references actually used by document construction, following operator decision msg_d2a87ee2.

DocumentaryText carries literal text, citations and joins. Rendering and reference collection consume that same construction. Missing/ambiguous-reference checks remain, with controls for unused rulings, citation renames, nested lists and missing/duplicate declarations. This covers ruling citations and the existing two typed references; ordinary symbol mentions inside prose strings remain outside the checked population.

Rebased head: 1ae68f9becc33bc15c82dfa06721bdd483eb0b18, on main 4343d9944ff7fefef2907bd8a088b7ac371e85e4. The conflict resolution preserves main's new dependency-admission paragraph and carries its ruling through the typed citation path. All document string literals and ruling references remain in the same order as the new base; diff checks and pre-push cargo fmt passed.

Runtime evidence at OLD head ebfe3d75 only: the specific baseline witness fails and the candidate passes; 7/12 named candidate checks passed, five had no verdict after a live-declaration lookup timeout. Generated DESIGN.md was byte-identical to that old base. These receipts do not qualify the rebased head.

Final-head r8a at 1ae68f9b: all eight documentary controls and all three roadmap controls PASS using fresh binaries built from base 4343d994 (gunbc f6c8cc251d51…, claim_batch 14414d2bb0a9…). The twelfth, live-declaration check remains queued on Butch. Both base and candidate render commands refused at resolve on the same existing repository_envelope DecodePositions/empty_map alias regression; generated-output comparison is UNOBSERVED. Committed DESIGN.md equality is not generated-output evidence. Both original files were restored and clean status verified. No generated mirrors or DESIGN.md were hand-edited.

Source review 89928 approves the rebased head. The earlier helper-duplication suggestion is addressed by delegating to existing md_helpers. Review approval is separate from pending execution evidence.
title: Check typed DESIGN references from document construction

body:
## What this is

F6 batch A (tidy-ant-251): the ambient list join `append` moves onto the declaration `std.algebra` already has, through the one mechanism that owns head rewrites — `v2.workflow.roster_import_sweep`.

## Integration state

**Landing head `9cc6c6969cf94df544ed2af9acbc7bbd2c1d336c`**, a merge commit bringing `origin/main` `424a79c1cc8` into this branch. Merged rather than rebased, per repo policy for integrating main and to protect the receipts below: their guards assert the arm head `0ffb4f00c7a` and the built head `198f2ed596d` are **ancestors** of the landing head, and a rebase orphans both. Re-verified against the new head this session, `git merge-base --is-ancestor` for all five (`0ffb4f00c7a`, `198f2ed596d`, `f268ec7124a`, old base `799697f5c76`, new main `424a79c1cc8`): all pass.

**Head moved today to `ad67090050e66b5669132faf47c1bb298991d281`**, a merge commit bringing `origin/main` `d87b8fc55a8` (#15736, the `required_regen` cgroup memory diagnostics) into this branch, authorized by the manager. Two reasons, neither of them cosmetic: a heal running on a head that contains `d87b8fc55a8` prints the stall instrumentation (`cgroup-diag` at `child.after_digest`, `child.after_surface_roles` and `child.end`, plus parent begin, end and readback), which is the only stall data available to this PR now that the bounded reproduction rows were closed by the operator without ever launching; and GitHub had been reporting `mergeable` UNKNOWN after 56 commits of divergence. Verified at this head before pushing: `git merge-base --is-ancestor` passes for all six (`d87b8fc55a8`, `424a79c1cc8`, `f268ec7124a`, `0ffb4f00c7a`, `198f2ed596d`, `9cc6c6969cf`), zero conflict markers anywhere in the tracked tree, and the `list_append` content intact (16 references in `src/v2/workflow/roster_import_sweep.dag`).  **Re-checked at this head (ad67090050e):** the review that counts is keyed to it — review 90370, verdict APPROVE, non-blocking, and on re-read it carries no concerns and no remarks to fix. `mergeableState` moved `UNKNOWN` to `MERGEABLE`; all four review requirements report `ok` (claude review 1/1 present, 0 request_changes, 0 active reviews); `checksState` reads `pending` while heal and witnesses run. Two of that review's substantive claims were re-verified from the diff at this head rather than taken on its word, because a reviewer's summary is a claim like any other: the diff is exactly four paths (`dag/test/claim/list_append_witness.dag`, `src/v2/test/claim/namespace_xl2_subject_tree_id_witness.dag`, `src/v2/workflow/namespace_xl2_subject_tree_id.dag`, `src/v2/workflow/roster_import_sweep.dag`), and exactly four `RosterHeadRow` literals now carry `site_gated: true` — the new `append/list` row plus three rows that already existed on main (`sort_by/symbol`, `sort_by/string`, `sort_by/digest_hex`) which gained the flag, where main carries it on none. So no gated site is silently skipped, which is the §5 requirement the reviewer checked.

Every `9cc6c6969cf` citation further down is historical — it names the head its receipt was computed at — and is deliberately left exactly as written rather than rewritten to the new sha. The controls row `sb2-ctrl-0ffb4f0` is being repinned to `ad67090050e` so that its receipt binds this head; it has never been admitted or started, and the row is on Butch, which is held by operator ruling, so the repin is pending rather than done.  **Frozen artifact for that row: candidate B, `0255ef0415fd8da675a2b2d6936c84cc7edd8d3119d455e0ead4ce1e43be8d97` (3086 B, `bash -n` clean)**, chosen over candidate A because a script whose queued-echo label contradicts its own checkout would make a false claim in its own receipt. Chain of custody, all four sha256 computed offline by this session with its own `sha256sum` and independently confirmed by another session: pre-repin source `sb2.sh` `134fa8c8c624287727976085112dbb73459db86a27005a6c5aa8ec5dd761d568` (2966 B); the row's previous frozen `run.sh` `ada9798de4dae2c187d0c09e37f11e68179459fb4894aed24718fda860b6b087` (3023 B), reproduced byte-exact by applying the two substitutions recorded at 2026-11-02T16:43:57Z to that source, so the old artifact stands on a documented derivation rather than a guess; candidate A `2ab80d2bfffb64b81e8912ecd5b34b26a2f0bb06bc2534d3fe91bf068d9054a9` (3023 B), which is that artifact with line 6's checkout pin moved to this head (`X=ad67090050e66b5669132faf47c1bb298991d281;`); and B, which is A plus line 3's label corrected to name this head. **B differs from `ada9798d` on exactly two lines — line 6, the pin the checkout obeys, and line 3, the label the receipt prints — and on nothing else.** `ada9798d` was never run. The keeper freezes B unstarted; launching it still needs the operator's Butch decision plus an explicit run request.

Every receipt below names the head it was computed at. Each is still an ancestor of the landing head, so each receipt describes code this branch contains; none of them is a receipt for the merge itself.

The conflict came from main's `424a79c1cc8` ("F6.last: `std.algebra` declares `list_last`"), which edits this PR's file. Three regions, all "both sides appended to the same list", resolved keeping both sides. Two needed judgement because main cannot know shapes this branch introduced:

- `roster_head_rows()`: main's `last` row gained `site_gated: false`. This branch added that field to `RosterHeadRow`, so every literal must carry it or the file will not typecheck. False, not true: `last` has one spelling and no dual-typed overload (unlike `append`). Note main's copy of that row (verified at `origin/main` line 466, PR #15597 merged 16:30:02Z) carries no `site_gated` field at all -- the field exists only on this branch -- so nothing in main expresses a gating choice for it; `false` is this branch's judgement, not main's.
- `roster_head_controls()`: main's `collection-head-last` verdict was adapted to this branch's `roster_head_expect(row:, ...)` signature, with `row: "last"`.

Checked after resolving and before committing: zero conflict markers; all 22 `RosterHeadRow` literals in `roster_head_rows()` carry `site_gated`; `git diff` against my previous head shows *only* main's `last` additions, and against `origin/main` shows *only* this branch's `append`/`site_gated` additions -- neither side lost content. The `.dag` typecheck of that resolution is decided by `v2-bootstrap` at this head, not by me. It **passed**: run 41483799186, job 1254087023, `completed/success`, started 2026-11-02T16:40:36Z and completed 17:44:35Z (64 min), read from `gh run view` at the commit. So the two conflict edits above compile.

`heal-generated-artifacts` (run 41483798785, job 125408700799) is **red, and it is not a defect in this diff**: both attempts were killed by the job's own ceiling (`heal.yml:42`, `timeout-minutes: 90`) on the step `Converge the stage0 mirrors to the seed's own fixed point` -- attempt 1 ran 16:40:40Z->18:11:30Z, attempt 2 started 18:12:48Z and was cancelled 19:43:56Z, both with steps 1-6 green and step 7 cancelled. The evidence that this is main-side, not this branch: the same PR content healed **successfully in 40.4 min at the pre-merge head `f268ec7124a`** (run 41372623964); the regenerator build costs 5 min on both my job and a healthy job, so only the interpreted converge step differs (23 min healthy, run 41505694285 job 125484329165, versus 85+ min killed here); five other PRs passed heal in 38-41 min during the same window; and `session/swift-owl-113` hit the identical 92-min cancellation (run 41498383521). This is being routed as a stage0-convergence cost on the interpreted wire, the same family as the stall already reported from the controls lane (~4% CPU, one `started Filesystem.Read dag/std/...` per ~80 s). `heal-fork-skipped` is `skipping`, as it always is on a same-repo branch. Nothing was pushed after the merge commit; the head named above is the head every CI figure in this paragraph was read at.

One row, in the table beside the `first`/`reverse`/`take`/`flat_map` rows:

```
RosterHeadRow { call: "append", key: "append", import_name: "list_append",
  home: qualified_name_from_dotted_string(dotted: "std.algebra"),
  labels: [RosterLabelRename { from: "items", to: "right" }],
  head: RenameHead { to: "list_append", positional: ["left", "right"], appended: [] } }
```

**RenameHead, not a seam, because the body already exists**: `list_append<T>(left, right) { left |> concat(right) }` at `dag/std/algebra.dag:171`. A seam here would be a second realization of an operation that has a `.dag` body (the `char_at` pattern is for heads that have none). The disposition (`dag/gunbc/primitive_egress/dispositions_collection.dag`, `append`) is `CollectionKernel`, `DagBodyRequired` — this row supplies the "use the declared authority" half; it does not claim the arm/bridge deletion half.

## The finding: the row the brief names was unappliable, because two passes of one plan disagreed

The row must rename the label `items` → `right` (`right` is the home's parameter name), and every remaining `src/v2` spelling of `append` labels its second argument that way — there is no fully positional site left to move. All five are direct calls, positional first argument, `items:` second:

- `src/v2/workflow/namespace_xl2_subject_tree_id.dag:175` — `append(so_far, items: next)`
- `src/v2/test/claim/namespace_xl2_subject_tree_id_witness.dag:41` (multi-line), `:102`, `:111`, `:119` — `append(<list>, items: <list>)`

The pipe spelling (`xs |> append(items: ys)`) survives only in `src/v2/test/fixture/census_path_trunc/full.txt`, which is out of scope below; the `-pipe` control is there so the row's behaviour at that shape is pinned before the fixture moves.

The label pass (`roster_row_label_edits`) rewrote `items:` at those sites, while the rename plan **refused the same argument**: `roster_positional_label_edit` and `roster_pipe_label_refusal` checked the authored label against the row's positional label with `roster_named_arg_label_is`, which never consults the row's own `labels` field. So one pass relabelled the argument and the other refused the call for being labelled that way — the row could not be applied at a single one of its own sites. Only `chars` (`KeepHead`) had ever exercised `labels`, so the combination was unimplemented rather than deliberately excluded.

The repair is a declared rule, not a fallback: **a named argument is admitted when the row itself renames that label into the label at its position**, because the row's `labels` field is that row's own fact about what its home calls each parameter, and the pass that rewrites it is the same row's (`roster_named_arg_label_admitted`). Everything else keeps refusing typed:

| arm | verdict | why it discriminates |
|---|---|---|
| `append(xs, items: ys)` | lands `list_append(left: xs, right: ys)` + `import std.algebra { …, list_append }` | the pair of passes produces one call that binds the declaration |
| `xs |> append(items: ys)` | relocates to `list_append(left: xs, right: ys)` | a declared home cannot keep a pipe (`recurring_failure_mode/pipe_into_a_declared_function_resolves_as_a_method`) |
| `append(xs, parts: ys)` | refuses `rename-call-named-argument call=append` | a label the row does not rename is still a guess |
| `append(items: ys, xs)` | refuses `rename-call-named-argument call=append` | the row's rename is **positional**, never a global relabel — used out of position it would have swapped the concatenation's two operands |
| `append(xs)` | refuses `rename-call-arity call=append` | a short call never gains an operand by inference |

Controls run under `instruments/roster-import-sweep-controls` (registered names in `roster_rename_control_names`, so a dropped control fails the count guard).

## Witness

`dag/test/claim/list_append_witness.dag` (same shape and registration path as `dag/test/claim/list_head_optional_witness.dag` from #15555 — discovered as a claim module under the `dag` source root, no `instrument_targets` row). **Every arm reads an element, not a length**: joining `[7]` onto `[1, 2]` and appending the left list's *count* (2) are indistinguishable by length, and the count/element confusion is exactly what the collection disposition names. So the arms assert the joined elements at their indices, from both ends, plus the two empty-operand identities.

## The consumer rewrite is in, as commit 468156aec26 — the generator's output, with its receipts

The two `src/v2` modules are rewritten by the generator, not by hand: a hand-written migration is the named failure mode (`recurring_failure_mode`, "a migration that is not the generator's output"). The entries used:

```
roster_rename_census_exit --arg home=std.algebra --arg call=append \
  --arg paths_csv=src/v2/workflow/namespace_xl2_subject_tree_id.dag,src/v2/test/claim/namespace_xl2_subject_tree_id_witness.dag
roster_import_sweep_apply_occurrences_exit --arg root_dir=<worktree> --arg home=std.algebra --arg call=append \
  --arg row_key=append/list --arg keys_file=<keys> \
  --arg paths_csv=src/v2/workflow/namespace_xl2_subject_tree_id.dag,src/v2/test/claim/namespace_xl2_subject_tree_id_witness.dag
```

The write takes census-reported occurrence keys, not a whole-home sweep: `roster_import_sweep_apply_row_exit` is the unkeyed entry, and an unkeyed run at a `site_gated` row is exactly what now refuses (`RefusalRowSiteGatedNeedsOccurrences`). The keys are read out of the census's own `LABEL`/`EDIT` lines, so the write acts on the sites the parser itself reported rather than on a second text scan that could disagree with it.

**Receipts** (srv2, admitted row `sunny-bee-153-f6a-ev4`, `MemoryMax=12G MemorySwapMax=0`; head `0ffb4f00c7a`; binary `~/runs/sunny-bee-153-f6a-apply2/wt/target/release/gunbc` (note `wt/`), 40,660,960 bytes, sha256 `db94d2355bdc9b6ca18d9015390e0393aea9e7a048f4690e57a0f8586a30aab5`, cargo-built at `198f2ed596d` with zero `*.rs`/`*.toml` drift between build head and run head; `git status` clean; receipt dir `~/runs/sunny-bee-153-f6a-ev4/`):

- census rc=1 — 1 is the census contract when rows are reported — in 1156 s: `CENSUS src/v2/workflow/namespace_xl2_subject_tree_id.dag call=append heads=1` and `CENSUS src/v2/test/claim/namespace_xl2_subject_tree_id_witness.dag call=append heads=4`, with 15 `LABEL` lines yielding **exactly 5 keys** (`KEYS 5`, `COUNT_OK`). No file outside the two admitted ones appears.
- apply rc=0 in 1180 s: 4716 bytes written, 5 `append(` removed, 5 `list_append(` added, and the post-write check found **0** residual `append(` heads. `list_append` was merged into each file's existing `import std.algebra {…}` rather than added as a second import statement.
- `memory.peak` for the row: 4.92G, swap 0.

Every rewritten site joins two lists — `xl2_member` returns `List<Step0SubjectMember>`, `xl2_real_manifest` returns `List<Xl2ManifestEntry>` — which is the identity the row claims; a single-item `items:` call could not reach this commit, because the five keys are the census's own list-identity sites and an unkeyed run is refused.

Two refusals showed up during the run; both are the tooling behaving correctly, and both are worth recording:

- The claim route refused to attribute the binary when invoked from a different checkout: *"its dep-info names an input outside this worktree … nothing here says whether it answers for this one."* So the witness runs are invoked from the tree the binary was built in, not from a convenience clone.
- `gunbc run --function` refuses a function whose return type is not `ProcessExit` (*"printing the value and exiting 0 would report success for a run whose outcome is unknown"*), so a `test fn` cannot be executed on the interpreter lane at all; it needs an instrument target. The applied files' own test fns therefore stay a stated residual below, alongside the native-xl2 rehearsal.

Controls and witness verdicts are **the admitted run's, not CI's** — CI executes neither. `.github/workflows/witnesses.yml`'s `v2-bootstrap` job invokes `gunbc test` on exactly two subjects (`//gunbc/instruments:self-host`, `//gunbc/instruments:v2-native-cli`) and no workflow runs any `//test/claim/...` pattern, so `//gunbc/instruments:roster-import-sweep-controls` and `//test/claim/list_append_witness:all` are executed only in my ledger scope and receipted here. That is the declared state of this population, not a gap this PR papers over: claims and modules outside the two emitted closures sit under `gunbc.rung_drop v1_required_lanes_withdrawn`, whose restoration trigger is the native compiler judging that population, and `gunbc.claim_coverage_census_live` **derives** its rosters (`claim_executors()` from `emitted_subject_build_rows()`, `claim_sources()` from `local_repo_wet_schedule()`) rather than authoring them — a per-witness instrument row would be growth in the population that drop exists to keep closed.

## The controls are registered, so one that stops running fails the label rather than vanishing

The label itself is registered in `gunbc.instrument_targets` beside its siblings: `roster_import_sweep_controls_label()` binds `TargetName { name: "roster-import-sweep-controls" }` in `instruments_package()`, and `roster_import_sweep_controls_binding()` pairs it with a `CliWireProgramProducer` whose entry is `src/v2/workflow/roster_import_sweep.dag` and function is `roster_import_sweep_controls_wire`. So the controls are a `gunbc test` target the CLI can be pointed at, not a function someone might remember to call — and an unknown label is refused by the CLI rather than treated as a pass.

Nine controls are new here (`collection-head-append-site-gated`, `-whole-row-set-refuses`, `-pipe`, `-foreign-label`, `-reordered`, `-arity`, `sort-by-whole-row-set-refuses`, `sort-by-whole-row-set-clean-file-passes`, `sort-by-whole-call-refuses`). Each is named twice: in `roster_rename_control_names()`, and as the verdict its control produces in `roster_head_controls`. `roster_rename_controls_verdicts_all` ends in `roster_control_fails` plus `roster_rename_control_count_check`, which fails on a control that is declared but did not run, on a verdict that ran without being declared, and on any count mismatch. A control that silently stops running — deleted, renamed, or short-circuited by an edit above it — therefore turns `//gunbc/instruments:roster-import-sweep-controls` non-zero instead of quietly shrinking the suite. The mutation arm MUT-B in the receipts table is the same discipline one level up: delete the row itself and the row's own control fails.

**Stacked follower.** Draft batch B (`f6-b-set-cluster`) stacks on this branch: its `set_insert` / `set_contains` / `empty_set` seam rows use the `site_gated` field this PR introduces, so they cannot typecheck against main on their own. It is therefore opened as a stacked PR with base = this branch, so its diff shows only B's own paths. One warning for whoever lands this: `--delete-branch` on a merged PR closes any PR stacked on it, which has cost this project a PR before, so B is retargeted to main at A's landing — the retarget is owned by the parent, and B's main-synced head (merge of `d87b8fc55a8`, conflict-free) is held ready locally for it.

### The arms and the migration grade the same files, and that can make an arm vacuous

The apply commit and the mutation arms act on the same two fixture files, which turns out to matter. After `468156aec26` the five sites read `list_append(left:, right:)`, so at the PR tip an unkeyed run has no gated call left to refuse. Measured on row `mutc2` at head `f268ec7124a`: the unkeyed run returned **rc=0 with 0 refusal lines** in 1120 s. That is the sweep behaving correctly and a trap for the evidence at the same time — scored against a pre-apply expectation it reads as a failure, and the un-gate arm sitting behind it (remove the gate, expect no refusal) would have printed **PASS without the gate ever being tested**.

So the arms are measured where the fixture is live, and the run is not allowed to assume it:

- baseline, MUT-A and MUT-B ran at `0ffb4f00c7a`, the commit before the apply, where the five gated calls exist;
- the un-gate arm runs at that same head and refuses to issue any verdict unless `git diff --stat <arm head> <pr head> -- src/v2/workflow/roster_import_sweep.dag` is **empty**, so what it grades is provably the shipped rule rather than an older copy of it;
- it also refuses unless the fixture holds exactly five `append(` heads. That guard exists because `list_append(` **contains** the substring `append(`: an early grep of mine counted the migrated calls as still unmigrated. It is the same wrong-correspondence error the row itself is about, caught in the harness rather than in the tool, and it is why the head count is asserted positively rather than trusted.

What keeps the unkeyed-refusal semantic alive at the tip, where the migrated files can no longer demonstrate it, is the controls fixture for `collection-head-append-whole-row-set-refuses`: it carries its own gated call in source, so no migration can empty it. That is the difference between a control and an arm — the control's fixture travels with the rule.

## Claim-route witness verdicts (the run that found my own witness defect)

`//test/claim/list_append_witness:all` is executed by no CI job, so its verdict is the admitted run's. srv2, ledger row `sunny-bee-153-f6a-claims2`, `MemoryMax=12G MemorySwapMax=0`, head `f268ec7124a`, binary sha256 `db94d2355b…` re-verified against the build record with zero `*.rs`/`*.toml` drift since it was cargo-built at `198f2ed596d`; invoked from `~/runs/sunny-bee-153-f6a-apply2/wt`, the tree the binary was built in:

- route control `//test/claim/list_head_optional_witness:all` rc=0 in 165 s — **2 claims held, 0 did not hold**. Run first on purpose: if the route is unhealthy the witness verdict means nothing.
- `//test/claim/list_append_witness:all` rc=0 in 166 s — **5 claims held, 0 did not hold**, including `list_append_never_appends_the_element_count` (the equal-count wrong-correspondence case: a rewrite that appended the left list's *count* instead of joining would produce a same-length list, so it is checked element by element, not by length) and both empty-operand identity arms.
- `memory.peak` 9.69G under the 12G cap; receipts in `~/runs/sunny-bee-153-f6a-claims2/`.

The first attempt at this run did not pass, and the failure was the run's value: the witness module refused to resolve at `list_append(left: [], right: two_items) == [1, 2]` — *"equality admission for '' cannot be judged: declaration identity unavailable — '==' is refused rather than admitted on an unjudged member."* An empty list literal in the **left** operand leaves the element type with no declaration to resolve against, while the same literal on the right resolved because the left operand carried the type. The identity arms now take a declared `no_items: List<Int>`, so the identity that matters — an empty operand is a join, not a replace — is actually judged rather than silently skipped. CI would never have shown this: it executes no `//test/claim/...` pattern.

## The revert arms: break the rule, show the RED fires

Each arm mutates one thing in `roster_import_sweep.dag`, re-runs the sweep over the same two files with the same binary, and restores the file. All four ran on srv2 rows in the interpreter lane; the tree came back clean after every one.

| arm | what is broken | expected | verdict, from the log |
|---|---|---|---|
| baseline | nothing: unkeyed run, gate on | refuses with the gate's own reason | **PASS** -- `rc=1`, 2 refusals, `secs=1177` |
| MUT-A | the two-pass label rule (`roster_named_arg_label_admitted` reverted to the single-pass form) | the rewrite can no longer admit `items:` | **PASS** -- `rc=1`, 2 `rename-call-named-argument` refusals, `secs=1130`, rule restored byte-identical |
| MUT-B | the append row deleted | nothing matches the call | **PASS** -- `rc=1`, 1 `scope-selects-no-row`, `secs=142`, row restored byte-identical |
| MUT-C | the gate itself: `site_gated: true` to `false` on the append row | the refusal disappears and the sweep proceeds | **PASS** -- 0 refusals, 2 `EDIT` + 15 `LABEL` lines covering exactly the five gated sites |

**Where each of those four verdicts was read from, and what is retained.** The baseline and MUT-C rows come from row `mutd2`, which retained each arm's full run output (`baseline.log`, `mut-c.log`, sha256s below), so every figure there can be re-counted from the artifact. The MUT-A and MUT-B rows come from row `ev5`, whose receipt is `steps.log` only (sha256 `b6e28c4e…`): the counts there (`named_argument_refusals=2`, `no_row_refusals=1`) are the harness's own counts of the tool's refusal text on a run that exited non-zero, and the arm's stdout was **not** retained by that row, so those two arms are executed receipts without a re-countable artifact. One attempt to re-retain them (`arms2`, below) failed on my expectations, not on the sweep, and my manager withdrew the follow-up row rather than spend srv2 headroom on it; both arms are independently corroborated by MUT-C, which shows the same five sites refusing when the gate is on and being rewritten when it is off.

## The coordinate is positional: what an edit above the site does to it

A site key is `path:line:byte column` of the call's head. `DESIGN.md` §3 treats that as a second, positional naming scheme, legitimate only where no symbol exists — so both halves of it refuse rather than guess:

- A key that no longer names a call head — an edit above it moved the line, a rename changed the head, the column is one off the head, the text before it is multibyte, or the site is already rewritten — meets `RefusalOccurrenceKeyUnmatched` at the site join, and the refusal names the path, the call and the key. `roster_apply_occurrences` then writes nothing; there is no nearest-match fallback. The registered controls for this are `occurrences-stale-key-refuses`, `occurrences-key-off-the-head-refuses`, `occurrences-scalar-column-after-multibyte-text-refuses`, `occurrences-key-on-a-bound-site-refuses` and `occurrences-key-outside-the-paths-refuses`, which run with the rest of the label.
- The two shifts the brief asks about are both real edits this PR itself makes: an import insertion **above** a site (the write adds `list_append` to each file's `std.algebra` import, which moves every later line by one), and a label rename **on** the site's own line (`items:` to `right:`). Each changes the coordinate of anything measured afterwards.
- What stops a shifted key from being answered by whatever call has drifted into that position — the false-join case — is that keys are only admissible at the head the census reported them at. My run reuses a census's keys only when the census recorded the same commit it is applying at, and re-runs the census otherwise; a key file carried across an edit therefore never reaches the site join at all. The false-refusal case (a valid site refused because its line moved) cannot silently pass either: it is a refusal with the key named, so it is visible in the receipt rather than a missing rewrite.

The converge step runs exactly `target/release/claim_executor --regen-round-cost --base-mirror --source-root dag --source-root src/v2`. R2 of the text-port route rules. tidy-ant-251 ruled that the generic prefix/suffix pair lives in `std.algebra`, with element equality as a declared parameter, and that the same PR repoints each specialised sibling or keeps it with a stated reason.

## What changed

- **One prefix predicate.** `std.algebra` had two: `is_prefix_of`, which is the law witness and has about 10 callers, and `list_starts_with`, a fork inside the same module. `list_starts_with` is deleted and its three callers use `is_prefix_of`.
  - This differs from the ruling's wording, which kept `list_starts_with` and added `list_ends_with` beside it. Keeping both prefix names would keep the nickname §3 forbids. So the surviving prefix name is the one the laws already cite, and the new suffix predicate mirrors it as `is_suffix_of`.
- **One suffix predicate.** `is_suffix_of(suffix, xs, eq)` is added beside `is_prefix_of`.
- **Fork census, each sibling repointed** to the pair, with its element equality passed as the declared argument:
  - `std.effect_grant` `path_is_prefix`
  - `std.materialization_ladder` `frame_path_is_prefix`
  - `gunbc.publication_policy` `segment_prefix_is_prefix`
  - `std.occurrence_identity` `occurrence_id_list_is_prefix_of`
  - `std.declaring_identity_spelling` `authored_is_suffix_of_canonical`
  - the claim helper `detail_ends_with` (`v2.test.claim.provenance.occurrence_file_attribution`), which reversed both lists to reuse a prefix walk.

  The other callers are `std.observation`, `std.scoped_authorization`, `v2.std.text` `string_split_step` and an emit claim.
- **Main merged in** at 827e22fd. None of the deleted names has a caller on main.

## Not yet evidenced

- `is_prefix_of` recurses to the length of the prefix. That is unchanged here; it is noted only because more callers now reach it.
- This touches the load-bearing `std.algebra`, `std.occurrence_identity` and `v2.std.text`, so the stage0 mirrors move. Heal has to converge them, and an exact-head regeneration fixed point is owed.
- Executed claims (to follow, on srv1 through the ledger): the touched claims (`occurrence_file_attribution`, the emit claim) and the witnesses of the repointed modules.

body:
The root repair named by #14553, as planned with tidy-ant-251 and approved by them.

## The chain, and its earliest unjustified link

A consumer calls `v2.std.decl_index` `decl_facts_at`, which is a self-call seam. The seed realizes it through `coproduct_reflection` `eval_decl_facts_at` → `decl_facts_for_roots_shared` → `decl_facts_corpus_walk`.

Under `gunbc test` no memo is registered, so the walk parsed every file under the roots and kept a `DeclFactRaw` (an Rc Node plus SourceIndices) for every declaration, and only then filtered to the asked keys. The name-to-path rule (DESIGN §3) already says where module `a.b.c` lives, so reading the corpus to answer one key is the cost §3 names. (An earlier version of this body said this walk was what pinned `roster-rehome-controls` at 12.55 GiB. The measurement below falsified that.)

## Repair (seed: `src/v1/stage0/src/coproduct_reflection.rs`)

- **One parser path.** The walk's per-file body is factored into `decl_facts_of_file`. The walk and the keyed read share it.
- **The qualified-key arm reads only the files its keys derive.** Each key splits into `<module>.<name>`. Its file comes from `cli_run::source_layout_lookup` `module_storage_relative`, the seed's existing encoding of `v2.compiler.source_authority` `module_file` over `gunbc.source_layout`, which already has its drift test. There is no new layout reader.
  - Each derived file is acquired through `derived_row_roster::acquire_dir_files`, the walk's own acquisition, so a derived roster module is read the way the walk reads it.
  - Each file is read once and contributes once per pool root that holds it. That keeps the walk's multiplicity for `[r, r]` and for nested roots, the ambiguity signal.
- **Typed refusals (`DeclFactsKeyedRefusal`, surfaced as `InterpError::DeclFactsKeyedReadRefused` and witness cause `decl-facts-keyed-read-refused`).** None falls back to the walk:
  - a key with no module part, or a module the layout cannot derive;
  - a pool root outside the layout trees;
  - a derived file that declares a module other than the one its path derives;
  - an unacquirable directory.

  An absent file is a genuine miss and yields zero rows, as before.

### Review asked at 65215c3e: is a lexer-unspellable module part a miss under the decl-facts walk contract?

The walk (`decl_facts_for_roots_shared`) keys each fact by the qualified name its file **declares**, and a file contributes only if it parses (`parse_dag_content`). So the walk can return a row for `m.n` only if some parsed file carries a `module m` header.

- **9fd41500 (superseded)** made every module part that `module_storage_relative` rejects a miss. That was wrong: the dag lexer (`v1_compiler_tokenize` `is_ident_start` / `is_ident_char`) accepts XID_Start identifiers and emoji, which the layout's ASCII rule rejects. A file declaring `module std.café` parses, the walk would return its rows, and 9fd41500 answered a silent miss.
- **65215c3e** returns a miss only when the lexer cannot spell the module part as a dotted identifier sequence (`std.9underivable`: `9` is not an identifier start). No header can carry such a name, so the walk's answer is zero rows and the keyed read returns the same thing. A lexable but layout-unstorable module part still refuses `KeyUnderivable`, as does a key with no module part.

**Semantics, stated plainly:** a lexically impossible module part is a **MISS** (zero rows, the walk's answer). A lexable but layout-unstorable module part remains a **REFUSAL** (`KeyUnderivable`). That refusal is **not** claimed to be equivalent to the walk, which could return rows a file declares there. It refuses because the keyed read cannot derive that file.

Unit controls: `a_key_whose_module_no_file_can_declare_is_a_miss`, `a_lexable_module_the_layout_cannot_store_refuses`, `a_key_without_a_module_refuses`. Reviewer: please confirm that `module_is_lexable` matches the header grammar the parser accepts.

An srv2 row (approved at 9fd41500; repin to 65215c3e requested) is for execution only (not acceptance): a fresh build, `keyed_decl_facts_tests`, then roster-import-sweep-controls alone.

body:
## What this PR changes

The second half of the OpenAI-compatible wire model (brief gap 2): the **legacy `/v1/completions`**
endpoint, in `dag/extdeps/llm/openai.dag`. First half (#15580) added the chat request and the streamed
chunk payload.

Home, again, is the plan's ruling and not a preference:
`dag/gunbc/plans/fabric_serving_router.dag:13` — "OpenAI wire belongs to
`extdeps.llm.openai/openai_contracts/openai_compat_sse/openai_errors/openai_rest`, not a new
`extdeps.openai` or OpenRouter key API." This endpoint is documented and versioned separately from chat,
so it gets **its own `ExternalAuthority` anchor**
(`platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/completions/create`, read 2026-11-01) rather than borrowing the
chat anchor: borrowing it would let a change to one endpoint silently claim authority over the other.

**Stacked on #15580** (base is that branch) so the review sees only this change; GitHub retargets to
`main` when #15580 lands.

## The modelling, and why it is not "chat minus messages"

A borrowed chat record would have implied the two endpoints differ only in `messages`. They do not:

- **`prompt` is a union of four shapes** in the endpoint document — one string, a list of strings (one
  completion per entry), one token list, a list of token lists — so `OpenAiCompletionPrompt` is a
  coproduct. A `String` field folds "one prompt containing a comma" together with "two prompts", and that
  is the difference between one completion and two: not recoverable by a reader.
- **three members exist only here**: `suffix`, `echo`, `best_of`.
- **`choices` is not shared** — a text choice carries a `String`, a chat choice carries a message or a
  delta. **`usage` IS shared** with `OpenAiChatCompletion200Usage`: both endpoint documents give that
  member the same shape, and a second record with the same fields would put one fact in two places where
  they could drift while both claimed to be usage (§3).
- **the streamed choice differs from the non-streaming one in two facts a reader cannot infer**: the final
  event carries a `finish_reason` and **no text** (so `text` is optional there and required above), and a
  closing frame may carry `usage` with an **empty** `choices` list (so the list is not non-empty).

Sampling members keep the json parser's own `JsonNumber` lexeme, with the same rule as the chat request:
no comparison, no range check, no float conversion (`std.float` has no ruled literal/operator home;
`infer_reason_float_literal_home_unruled`). The frontier row from #15580 covers **both** endpoints'
requests — a ruled float home dissolves one row, not one per endpoint.

## What is declared missing, and who reads this

- `structural_coverage_gap_openai_text_completion_members`: `logit_bias`, the request `logprobs` selector,
  the deprecated `user`.
- two rows for per-token `logprobs` in the two answer shapes, naming the chat `...200Logprobs` record as
  the thing to compare against before inventing a second one.
- `openai_text_completion_wire_frontier_rows` (declared in this module and read where declared -- the repo-wide fold that used to enroll such rows, `gunbc.census_closure_frontier`, was retired on main by #15531 at `aac228c337f3`): nothing reads the
  request, the 200 body or the chunk yet. The consumer is named, not assumed — the serving path's request
  and answer reads that `gunbc.plans.fabric_serving_router` places in its S3 decisions, on whichever
  endpoint the client called. Each row dissolves only when that reader lands **with a witness that decodes
  a recorded response into the record** (a completions 200 with its choices and usage; a completions chunk
  including the final event, which carries a `finish_reason` and no text). A reader that compiles is not
  payment — otherwise the row would be discharged by the compile that the row exists to distrust. The two
  chat rows on #15580 were tightened to the same standard, so the module holds one rule, not one per
  endpoint.

## Why there is no witness module in this change

Not an omission: there is no decision function here to execute. A row asserting
`openai_text_completion_object_wire == "text_completion"` would be a green identity — the failure mode the
merged recurring-failure-mode row `a_green_case_set_that_counts_row_identities_and_never_the_branches_those_rows_take`
(#15510) is about, where a case set counts row identities and never the branches. The witness for this half
belongs to the first reader, which is the place a wrong shape can actually fail; #15580 shows what that
looks like when there *is* behaviour (four rows, each naming the mutation that turns it red, each executed as a booked claim row at that head).

## Not in this PR

No route, no body rewrite, no product policy, no endpoint or key. `openai_compat_sse` keeps the SSE
framing; `gunbc.instruments/v1/vllm_route_completions` keeps the route path — this module deliberately
declares no path constants, so a string does not get a second home.





---

**Added by review 89556 and its follow-ups (head `0285374c7698`; wire model, then the carrier fix, then review 89568's citation fix).** The reviewer found `data openai_text_completion_object_wire` dangling: no consumer, no frontier row — and, underneath that, nothing tying it to the two bodies' `object: String` members, so a `chat.completion` or an error envelope would type-check as a text completion. Fixed as one fact rather than a tracked gap.

`object` is now a carrier with a **checked constructor**, following `extdeps.languages.json.grammar`'s `JsonNumberLexeme` (carrier at `:36`, `valid` / `unchecked` / smart constructor at `:149-159`):

```
type OpenAiTextCompletionObject = String where brand("OpenAiTextCompletionObject")

fn openai_text_completion_object(s: String) -> OpenAiTextCompletionObject? {
  if openai_text_completion_object_valid(s: s) {
    Present { value: openai_text_completion_object_unchecked(s: s) }
  } else {
    Absent
  }
}
```

`Present` for `text_completion`, `Absent` for everything else including `chat.completion` and `chat.completion.chunk`; both bodies type `object: OpenAiTextCompletionObject`, so a decoder must pass the check to build one and there is no default to launder a chat answer through. The first cut of this used `String where openai_text_completion_object_is_documented`, which was the wrong precedent: DESIGN §4 records `gunbc.design_ruling where_refinements_retire_for_checked_constructors` (`dag/gunbc/design_ruling.dag:227`, quoted at DESIGN.md:329) retiring where-refinements in favour of constructors returning `Optional`, and `std.types`' `NonEmptyStr` at `std/types.dag:264` is that ruling's legacy, not a pattern — so this PR does not add a new one. A where-**brand** is different from a where-predicate and stays: it yields a `WherePredicateMarker` that is never evaluated as a refinement (`std/types.dag:280-292`), so it carries nominal identity and no validation claim.

Both unread-shape frontier rows now say the future reader must refuse a body whose `object` is not the documented constant, and `dag/test/claim/extdeps/openai_text_completion_wire_witness.dag` executes the constructor — documented value gives `Present`, both chat values give `Absent`.

**Evidence for those rows: EXECUTED at the final head** — see Round 4 below. The earlier state of this line said "authored, parsed, not executed here"; that is superseded, and the third row (`the_declared_frontier_rows_are_well_formed`) was added precisely so the frontier rows are executed rather than only declared.




---

**Round 2 — head `3a42514c647b`** (merge-forward of #15580's `d1771bde0c17` + two fixes).

- **Review 89578 (parse):** the coverage row had been spliced inside `OpenAiTextCompletionChunkBody`'s argument list, so the list and the census frontier that imports it could not parse. Split into two complete `frontier_row_decl` entries in `ad2188237b08`. My earlier "parsed" claim rested on a whole-file delimiter count, which a balanced splice defeats; the check now validates each list element (and demonstrably fails on `b2d65839c6bf`).
- **Review 89585 (required member):** `prompt` is now `OpenAiCompletionPrompt`, not optional — the generated parameter is `Required[Union[str, SequenceNotStr[str], Iterable[int], Iterable[Iterable[int]], None]]`. The union's `None` is present-and-null, refused upstream, and deliberately not an arm.
- **Same-class audit:** `stream` → `Bool?`; sampling members → `JsonNumberLexeme?` (the old `JsonNumber?` named a `JsonValue` variant and would not resolve); the chat `OpenAiFinishReason` reuse declared as a superset gap with the name-collision reason; last `read 2026-11-01` retired for the pinned anchor.

**Evidence standing at this round:** two witness rows (`//test/claim/extdeps/openai_text_completion_wire_witness:all`) authored, structurally checked, not yet executed at `3a42514c647b`; the chat witness target also re-runs against this head since the base moved. Superseded by Round 4, where all three rows are executed.

---

**Round 4 — final head `20f07b790e74953d58ea5efdde2dc9177b3b6007`, and the rows were EXECUTED.**

The head is a merge-forward of main plus one addition: a third witness row, `the_declared_frontier_rows_are_well_formed`, so the frontier rows are executed rather than merely declared (`frontier_rows_well_formed` from `std.roster_frontier` applied to `openai_text_completion_wire_frontier_rows`, which is also folded into the existing `extdeps.llm.openai` import rather than given a second import statement).

Row `pb756v4-15583-20f0`, booked claim runner (runner script sha256 `f176c14e`), head `20f07b790e74`, entry `dag/test/claim/extdeps/openai_text_completion_wire_witness.dag`, `DECLARED_ROWS n=3`, `BUILD_OK`, admitted 12:26:52Z, ended 12:34:45Z, scope exit=0:

- `CLAIM_COUNTS pass=3 fail=0 unobserved=0 total=3 declared=3 producer_rc=0`, no `JOIN_MISMATCH` line, and the row's name-by-name join of the three `ROW` lines against the result lines is exact
- the three PASS lines: `the_documented_object_value_builds_the_carrier`, `another_endpoints_object_value_is_refused`, `the_declared_frontier_rows_are_well_formed`
- resolve 3383 ms (39 modules, 1314 items); memory peak 10.0G against a 16 GiB scope cap, swap 0, `oom 0 oom_kill 0`

CI at this head: `v2-bootstrap` green. `heal-generated-artifacts` is RED and is **not this PR's drift** — the diff from the merge-base is 2 `.dag` files (+334) with no stage0 mirror, every file the drift names is byte-identical to main at this head, and for `std_types` / `std_roster_frontier` / `std_measure` / `std_content_hash` the mirror's last regen commit is an ancestor of the commit that changed its `.dag` source (#15686 / #15700 / #15717 / #15742). Every completed heal run that day is a failure across unrelated lanes. The full evidence and the reason no repair commit is added here are in comment 6626859475 on this PR; the heal hang tracked in #15760 is a separate defect.

M1.5 (D13 consumer): the uses-row restatement fold over derived dependency demand, restacked on #15541 and repointed off the census.

STACK: base is `session/jolly-bat-409-d13-facts` (#15541), which sits on #15382 (#15423 below it). Land order #15423 -> #15382 -> #15541 -> this.

WHAT LANDS
- `v2.compiler.uses_row_restatement`: the standing for one authored `uses` row over `v2.compiler.dependency_demand` `DependencyDemand` -- `Restates` / `NotRestated` / `Undecided { cause }` / `Unobserved`. Judged by MEMBERSHIP of that row's own resource in the fn's derived set (`resource_set_has`), never by equality of the whole set: a fn that derives several resources licenses deleting only the rows it restates (gunbc#12992). Only `Restates` licenses a deletion.
- `v2.compiler.dependency_demand_facts demand_facts_closure_facts`: the closure-level producer entry the walk was missing. `demand_facts_module_facts` is per module, but the callee normalization (`demand_facts_normalize_callees`) needs the KNOWN SET of the whole closure -- a callee may name a declaration in another module -- so no caller could use it correctly at module scope, and each consumer that normalized for itself would be a second local implementation of one rule (DESIGN section 6b). This entry accumulates the per-module facts and returns them with callee paths already mapped to the longest known declaration path. It lands here because its callers and claims are here.
- `v2.compiler.uses_row_restatement_route`: the consumer's route. It takes the two things D13 produces and nothing else -- the FACT WALK's closure facts (`demand_facts_closure_facts`, handed to `dependency_demand_of` untouched) and the AUTHORED-ROW READER's readings (`demand_facts_strip` / `demand_facts_authored_readings`, whose `AuthoredRowReading` is the only fact-walk value that crosses the boundary). Demand is derived ONCE over the whole closure, because a fn's demand is a join over callees that may live in another module of the ingest. The route does no normalization of its own.
- Claims: 5 supplied-row controls on the fold (`v2.test.claim.compiler.uses_row_restatement`), plus a route claim module that runs the fold on the REAL front end over one closed four-module ingest: two inhabitance claims (direct call, transitive call), three REDs (over-claim, a `requires none` operation, an opaque reach), one carrier-boundary RED (Get loses its `requires Network` declaration, everything else byte-identical, the row stops being a restatement), and one harness-soundness claim (one entry per authored fn).

WHY IT NO LONGER TAKES A REPORT (the doctrine change)
The previous draft consumed `DemandCensusReport` / `DemandCensusRow` and the demand-census claim module. The census PROCESS is retired by default with no successor instrument (#15415 `gunbc.design_ruling bad_process_is_worse_than_no_process`; #15428 deleted the instruments), and building a new consumer on a whole-population report is exactly what that ruling forbids. The D13 symbols themselves survive and are what this consumer now reads. Their home is `v2.compiler.dependency_demand_facts` (#15541) -- NOT `v2.compiler.dependency_demand`, which would close an import cycle with `v2.std.operation_declaration`. The authored-fn/reading pairing that used to arrive with a report is now stated by the consumer (`UsesRowAuthoredRows`), and the claims assemble the same bounded strip-and-fold read the surviving driver in `v2.compiler.source_root_eval` performs (`native_demand_facts_read`, `native_test_resolve_module`, `demand_facts_module_facts`, `demand_facts_authored_readings` over the module's root scope). The harness reports itself: a module it cannot resolve makes the entry list `Absent`, so no absence-claim can pass vacuously.

THE FILESYSTEM DIFFERENCE THE PREVIOUS BODY NOTED
It said a Filesystem row is `NotRestated` here and `OutOfVocabulary` in the census, both non-deletable. With the census retired there is no longer a second vocabulary to compare against, and the distinction has a home in the demand itself rather than in two vocabularies: `NotRestated` is a DECIDED judgement -- the demand settled and the row's resource is not in the derived set -- while a demand that cannot settle is `Undecided { cause }` (e.g. an operation whose requirement is opaque) and never reads as empty, so nothing that is merely undecidable is ever reported as "not restated". That arm is pinned by `reaching_an_opaque_operation_leaves_the_row_undecided_RED` (route label) and by `an_undecided_demand_never_licenses_a_deletion_RED` (fold label); the DECIDED side, a settled demand whose own resource is absent, is pinned by `an_over_claiming_row_is_not_restated_by_the_real_route_RED` (route) and by the `fs`-carrying supplied row in `a_row_is_judged_by_its_own_resource_not_the_fn_set_RED` (fold). Naming them here as the assertions the labels carry, not as results: neither label has produced a verdict yet, both are refused behind #14876 / #15507 (runs below).

RUN, TWICE, AND STILL REFUSED BY TWO WALLS THIS HEAD DOES NOT CARRY. Both labels ran at `26ffb1382c7` on srv1 (fresh worktree, `GITHUB_SHA` = the tested tree, one named 16G/swap-0/1h scope each; receipts with the telemetry are in the comment thread). `uses_row_restatement:all`: 5 tests, all `refused at prepare`, chain `resolve_reason_unbound_symbol @ src/v2/std/qualified_name.dag bytes 13113..13126 "string_length"` -> `declarer_refused @ <node occurrence #436 "qualified_name_from_dotted_string">`, admission refused `positive_population_empty, required_native_pass_regressed` -- the ambient `string_length` primitive, whose egress is #15507. `uses_row_restatement_route:all`: clears the fixture closure's prepare and reaches the native demand transition INSIDE THE EMITTED COMPILER, then `resolve_refused first=resolve_reason_unbound_symbol @ dag/std/algebra.dag bytes 77075..77078 "Map"` (the N7 wall-2 `Map`, retyped by #14876), same admission refusal. Neither is a defect in this consumer: the route change type-checks through seed emit and codegen (253 files, `file_refusals=0`). Prior state (359ae63fa1d6, seed claim_batch sha256 67ede97963154c90c225ea2cf11481bbe503075e11d8ce6fefa7f6339c3df9dc): the 5 supplied-row claims passed rc=0; the route claims had not run past a type error in the old report-consuming route.

DESIGN 3c: consumed by the route, which is the declared frontier for deleting rows.

# Flex autoscaler, items 3 and 4: the pass's DEMAND and its SELECTION, on the deciding path Stacked on `session/deep-raven-765-item6` (#15462). One PR because the two are one chain: the demand's directive is what decides whether a selection is attempted at all, and the selection is what the demand is a demand *for*. ## What this removes It removes the entry's **temporary authority over WHAT to rent**. Before this, `gunbc.fleet.flex_pass_run` hard-coded the receipt line `selection=needs-evidence (select_supply unwired ...)` and had no demand input at all — the pass decided nothing, but it also *could not say why*. After this, the pass calls the fabric's own authorities (`arbitration.decide_demand_command`, `selection.select_supply`) and reports their typed answers. No ctrl dependency is removed by this PR; it removes a placeholder line and a silence. ## Item 3 — DEMAND The demand arrives as the **fabric's own command vocabulary**, not a flex-shaped row: `product.fabric.demand`'s `Demand

` / `CoreCommand

` over a sealed `DemandPopulation

`, decided by `product.fabric.arbitration.decide_demand_command`, whose `SatisfactionDirective` is what says whether the pass seeks new supply at all (`RequireNewAttempt` / `AttachToExistingExecution` / `AwaitAdmission` / `satisfied-by-terminal-receipt`). * `FlexDemandStanding` is the declared interface: `FlexDemandRead { population, core }` or `FlexDemandUnread { reason }`. * **It is NOT the srv1 router's hand-patched pending counter** (that counter is being deleted), and the pass does not invent demand: an unread demand is reported unread and the pass plans nothing on it. * **There is no producer yet.** `flex_demand_standing()` returns unread, naming why. The owed producer is the fabric front door's admission callout (`front_door_admit_on_store`, proud-bear-756's S3), recorded as a new frontier row `product.fabric.flex_vast_loop flex_demand_producer_frontier`, whose trigger is a pass receipt reading `demand=read population=N` and a witness pairing the entry with a **real** front-door callout instead of a supplied demand. * The receipt gains `demand=` and `directive=` lines, in the fabric's own words (refusal arms, reuse policy), so an operator can tell a refused demand from an absent one from a demand that says *attach*. ## Item 4 — OFFERS / SELECTION `select_supply` is now called **on the deciding path** (`flex_pass_select` → `flex_select_offers`), under `flex_objective`'s terms and `flex_delay_unvalued`, with the cohort affinity **declared** (`flex_pass_affinity`) rather than invented per offer, and the horizon from `flex_horizon_duration`. Per calm-crab-645's conditions: * **(b) Nothing is filled in.** The candidates come only from the shadow adapter `flex_candidates_from_vast_offer`, which refuses every search offer because the search answer carries no start cost, transition, opportunity cost, readiness, cited region or use permit — and the refusal **names the fields**, which is what the receipt now prints (`selection=candidates-unestablished offer=... missing=...`). The recipe→`ExecutionRequirements` gap is likewise a typed stop (`FlexSelectionRequirementsUnread`) naming the producer owed, not a shape invented at the call site. * **(c) No second binding path.** `bind_candidate` / `select_supply` are the only route; this entry never ranks offers and never constructs a `CandidateOffer` (it is `sole_constructor` and stays that way). * **(a) The pairing claim is unverified and carried as a frontier row.** `flex_select_supply_consumer_frontier` is rewritten to say what is now wired and exactly which two producers are owed, so the row cannot be read as "wiring missing" nor as "selection runs". ## Proof, and what is NOT proven * **Type gate: green.** The entry is imported by `test.claim.fabric.flex_pass_carry_witness`, whose claim-run typechecks the whole entry closure: **exit 0, 14 claims PASS** (local `gunbc` built from `1170b706a63`). What it caught, and what the second commit fixes: `DemandAdmitted`/`CommandRefused`/ `decide_demand_command` live in `product.fabric.arbitration`, not `demand`; `population_demands` takes `p:`; and `decide_demand_command`'s effect has **six** arms, not two — the four `Work*` effects (a withdraw or supersede that changes the *work's* standing) are not "no demand" and do not authorize a purchase, so they now report as `work-changed` in the fold's own words. * **Witness: `test.claim.fabric.flex_demand_selection_witness`, 5 claims, all PASS** (same local run). The demand is **supplied** — minted through `admit_command` over an attested principal, and the population is read back out of the fold's own effect rather than hand-assembled: 1. an unread demand stops the selection before any offer is touched; 2. an admitted demand that *requires a new attempt* stops at the requirements gate, naming the producer owed (this is the fold saying *buy*, and the pass still not being allowed to invent what to buy); 3. an admitted demand that does **not** require a new attempt seeks no offer — the fold, not the pass, is what stops it, which is what makes claim 2 mean something rather than "the pass is always stopped"; 4. a duplicate submit reaches the receipt as the fold's own refusal, naming the demand; 5. the pass's own demand standing is unread and names `flex_demand_producer_frontier`. * **Unverified, stated plainly:** (1) the **pairing with a live front door** — no producer exists, so no test can pair it yet; the frontier row carries that, and its trigger is a receipt reading `demand=read population=N` plus a witness against a real callout; (2) `select_supply` never ranks a **live** offer in this PR, because no producer establishes the six search-offer facts — the route is wired to that gate and the gate names the fields; (3) the flex witnesses are **not** in the opt-in CI `witness_entries` roster, so CI compiles them and does not run them. ## Not in scope No wet (item 9), no cutover (item 10), no edits to `flex_vast_template*.dag` or the credential modules (the sibling's items 1-2), no enrollment (item 8). ## Known cost of the selection witness (measured, both runners) `dag/test/claim/fabric/flex_demand_selection_witness.dag` costs about **14 minutes of wall time** under the judge CI uses: `claim_batch --source-root dag --source-root src/v2 --entry --functions --claim-run` measured **823 s** locally and **859 s** on srv1 at `8f1cce2a3488`. `gunbc run --claim-run` on the same closure measured about 10 minutes with an older binary. The cost is the closure, not the assertions: the positive control needs a bound offer and a use permit, so the file imports the fabric's own fixtures for exactly that interface - `test.claim.fabric.selected_offer_fixture` (which is `product.fabric.selection bind_candidate`) and `test.claim.fabric.provider_use_fixture` (the admitted-for-use permit) - and those pull `product.fabric.provider_admission` / `product.fabric.provider_route` into the closure. An earlier revision imported `test.claim.rtx_pro_6000_catalog_witness` instead, which reaches the same interface through a neighbouring witness and drags a whole catalog closure; that is gone. The pairing claim and the deciding-path claims stay in ONE file on purpose: one interface, one place, per DESIGN 3 - splitting them to save minutes would separate the control from the path it controls.

# Item 6 of the flex-autoscaler lane: the pass reads what it holds

Base is `main`; item 7 (#15349: the pass destroys its own dead cards, loading cut 600 s → 120 min) is what the card list this PR builds feeds: a dead-card fold that is handed `cards: []` is dead code, which is exactly the state the lane was in.

## What this removes

`gunbc.fleet.flex_pass_run` built `FlexPassInput` with `cards: []`, `allocations: []` and `cooldown: none` — **always**. Nothing in the repository ever constructed a `FlexOwnedCard`, so:

* the pass could not destroy a card it had itself rented, however long that card sat loading (#15349's fold had nothing to fold);
* the pass could not see that it had already asked for a card, so a lost create answer was invisible to the next pass;
* ctrl's bidder (`lib/vast_bidder.mjs` + `lib/pool_autoscale.mjs`) remained the only thing that keeps a table of "our cards" and a loading clock. **This PR is the .dag-side replacement for that table and that clock**: the cards come from the labelled roster, the loading clock from the pass's own carry, and ctrl's numbers are no longer the authority for either.

Frontier row dissolved/rewritten: `product.fabric.flex_vast_loop flex_run_pass_caller_frontier` (its trigger 1, "nothing feeds a previous pass's create standing … and the pass's cards and allocations are not yet built from the labelled instances it observes", is now half-dissolved: cards and standing are built; the allocation still needs the placement slice, and the row says so).

## What is in it

**1. The cards (`product.fabric.flex_vast_shadow`).** `flex_cards_from_roster(ours, roster, sightings, now)` builds a `FlexOwnedCard` per instance row carrying **our** label — never from a create answer, because the answer can be lost and the roster cannot lie about what is being paid for. A partial or unreadable roster builds **no** cards (the same rule the cap reads: a partial walk under-counts what we hold). A row that cannot be priced or sized is **refused and reported**, not priced at zero — a zero rate would make the card look like the cheapest thing on the market.

**2. Three fields the instances row cannot say, each declared rather than invented:**

* `actual_status` — the vendor types it `string | null` and gives examples, not a closed set. This pass reads exactly the two words the flex lane has seen live, `running` and `loading`. **Any other word, and a null, is reported UNREAD and the row is left out of the card list**: an unknown status is never read as not-running, so a card in a state this lane has not seen cannot be counted dead by the loading cut. `"interrupted"` is the word Vast's own examples use for a contract taken back, and this pass still does not read it — reading it would let a guess destroy a card.
* `loading_age` — `GET /api/v1/instances/` carries **no time field at all** (`VastAiInstance` has none), so the age is not on the wire. It comes from the pass's own carry: the instant an earlier pass **first** saw that id loading. Three cases, and only two are numbers (see 4).
* `outbid` — whether a host has taken an interruptible contract back is a fact of the **market** (our bid against that host's floor), not of the row, and `extdeps.cloud.vast_ai` refuses to read `is_bid` as interruptibility on live evidence (every bid-search offer read `is_bid` false). So the roster fold builds `outbid: false` and says so: until the market slice supplies it, the roster fold can destroy a card **only** through the loading cut. `held` asks the weaker question — is this contract a bid contract, which is what the vendor's own `is_bid` names — so it is read from `is_bid`, **UNVERIFIED against a live instance row**; it moves only the switch premium in the ranking, never a destroy.

**3. The carry (`gunbc.fleet.flex_pass_run`).** One JSON document (`extdeps.languages.json` both ways) at `host_layout srv1_flex_pass_carry_root`, `flex-pass-carry.json`, readable only on its home host srv1 (any other host reads it unread and the create refuses): the loading sightings, the standing of the last create ask, and the cooldown. It carries no secret — an ask id, a contract id, a machine id and two instants. The receipt gains `cards=…`, `reconcile=…` and `carry=…` lines, so a pass that destroyed nothing says **why** it destroyed nothing.

**4. A missing or unreadable carry is typed, not defaulted** (calm-crab-645's review point on the first shape of this PR). `flex_carry_read` yields `FlexCarryLoaded | FlexCarryUnread`; `FlexOwnedCard.loading_age` became `Second?`; and `flex_card_dead` **cannot fire the loading cut on an unread age**. So:

The field is `loading_age_sampled`: now minus the first instant a pass SAMPLED the card loading. It is not a lower bound on the current loading spell (a card can run and load again between two samples, and its current spell is then shorter), so the loading cut rests on a stated premise, loading throughout the span between samples, which the carry cannot check. It was named `_at_least` and documented as "a destroy can never be early" until the review of this head showed that contradicted `FlexLoadingSighting`; the name and the docs now say what is measured.

* carry read **from a complete baseline**, id absent from the sightings → bound **at least 0**, which is sound only because the previous pass read the whole account and this id was not loading in it;
* carry read, id already sighted → the bound runs from the **first** sighting, never the last;
* **the baseline is a recorded premise, not an assumption**: the carry records `basis` as complete or incomplete (what the walk that produced it actually read), and the fold **checks** it. A carry written from a partial, unreadable or otherwise unfinished walk yields `FlexSightingsUnread` for every id — absent ids read UNREAD, not 0 — and the prior sightings are DROPPED, not kept (`flex_loading_sightings_after`), so nothing is aged until a complete walk re-takes the baseline.
* carry missing/unreadable (cargo clean, fresh worktree, different runner, two passes racing) → **every** loading bound is UNREAD, the cut cannot fire, no cooldown is claimed, and the pass keeps cards it cannot age. The state repairs itself: the next pass that reads a complete roster writes a fresh complete baseline.

**Why a file and not `std.durable_compare_and_set` or a fabric store slot**, stated because it is a real limitation and an ADMITTED DEBT: the operator ruling `gunbc.design_ruling flex_pass_carry_is_admitted_single_host_file_debt` (2026-11-01, calm-moth-166) accepts the plain file on srv1 only, other hosts refusing, and `flex_carry_home_frontier` is the dissolution row that says how it ends (a `durable_cas_file_store` slot or a shared store). The pass is dispatched by hand (fleet-converge mode `flex_pass`, no schedule) under the account-wide concurrency group `gunbc-flex-vast-account`, so passes do not overlap; the carry is one file on its home host srv1 (`host_layout srv1_flex_pass_carry_root`), and any other host reads it unread and refuses to create. A CAS slot would need `flex_pass_run` admitted as a caller and a `VerifiedCasAttempt` constructor.

**Write-ahead.** The pass creates first and records after, so before the effect it writes the carry with standing UNKNOWN (`flex_carry_in_progress`); the final write replaces it. A failed final write, or a crash between, leaves UNKNOWN and the create gate shut. A failed write-ahead shuts the gate for that pass (`flex_carry_trust_after_write_ahead`). Witnessed by `the_write_ahead_record_reads_back_untrusted_and_keeps_the_cooldown` and `a_failed_write_ahead_shuts_the_create_gate_and_a_landed_one_leaves_it`.

## Also in this PR

* `product.fabric.flex_vast_loop flex_release_inputs_producer_frontier` — a new frontier row for item 7's second half. `flex_run_pass` takes `FlexReleaseInputs { roots, protected, readings }` and the entry passes none, so a wet destroy stops **typed** at `FlexPassReleaseReadingsUnread`, naming the allocation whose readings are owed. Nothing in the repository constructs `RentedReleaseReadings` — the producer owed is the rented_* carriers (S5, witty-lynx-354's lane). Reported rather than invented, per calm-crab-645's decision.
* Comments at the two receipt-string sites that went through a parse failure, saying what the failure actually was: an argument list left open is reported at the **enclosing block's closing brace**, several lines below the call, naming no call — which is what made this site cost an hour of bisection and produce a wrong theory about the lexer. The row is filed separately (`an_unclosed_call_reports_at_the_enclosing_blocks_closing_brace`).

## Unverified — read this before trusting it

* **Nothing executed against Vast.** No card was rented, no live instance row was read. The proof below is claim-runs of pure functions over supplied rosters.
* The flex witnesses are **not in the opt-in CI `witness_entries` roster**, so CI only *compiles* them. The claim-run output is pasted below; re-running them is `claim_batch --source-root dag --source-root src/v2 --entry dag/test/claim/fabric/<name>.dag --functions <every test fn in the file> --claim-run` — **claim_batch, not `gunbc run --claim-run`**: at one head an older `gunbc --claim-run` reported green while claim_batch caught a non-exhaustive match, so claim_batch is the gate used here and on srv1.
* `is_bid → held` is unverified against a live instance row (see 2).
* The carry is a plain file on one home host, not a CAS slot; `flex_carry_home_frontier` names the shared store that removes both limits.

## What the claims cover (executions: see the next section)

* `flex_vast_shadow_witness` — 10 new (30 total): a labelled running row becomes a running card; a row we do not label is never a card we hold; an unread status word (and a null) is reported unread and never becomes a card; a loading card's bound runs from the sighting an earlier pass left and from nothing otherwise; an unpriceable/unsizeable row is refused rather than priced at zero; a partial roster builds no cards; the sightings a pass leaves keep the first time a card was seen loading; **a partial walk marks the baseline incomplete and drops the prior sightings**; an unread carry leaves every loading bound unread where a known one leaves at least zero.
* `flex_vast_loop_witness` — 3 new end-to-end: **the card the roster builds is the card the pass destroys** (roster + a 121-min-old sighting → `FlexPlanDryDestroy { FlexDestroy { id "1001", FlexCleanupStaleLoading } }`); a loading card seen for the first time is left alone; a loading card the pass cannot age is left alone.
* `flex_market_witness` — an unread loading age is never dead by the loading cut, while an outbid card with an unread age still is.
* `flex_pass_carry_witness` (new file) — 14: the carry wire round-trips a **baseline**, a cooldown, two sightings and an answered ask; **an incomplete baseline makes absent ids read UNREAD where a complete one yields a bound**; a line the pass cannot read is reported unread and never guessed at; a sighting line missing its instant is dropped rather than read as aged-to-zero; a create performed this pass supersedes the ask carried in; a refused ask with nothing on its machine is retired and an expired cooldown dropped; an answered ask whose contract the account does not show is **still carried**; a partial account concludes nothing; an unread carry claims no cooldown, no standing, and says so on the receipt; a read carry reports what it holds.


## Executed

The receipts that were in this body (7b48f8ea, c1d09f7, 82ba5701) predate the current tree and are withdrawn. The last srv1 receipt is calm-crab-645's `fx5-b67a6ae` at `b67a6aea49ac`: carry 26/26, loop 42/42, template 12 PASS / 1 UNOBSERVED. This head changes the write-ahead, the sibling shadow claim (`a_partial_roster_marks_the_baseline_incomplete_and_drops_the_prior_sightings`) and the `loading_age_sampled` rename, so every `flex_*_witness` file is to be re-run at it; no receipt covers it yet.

The UNOBSERVED template claim is `two_mints_differ_and_each_carries_the_launch_and_names_pool_api_key` (formerly `..._each_names_pool_api_key`): the hermetic route has no `ReadPassword` mock_response, so it is a stated route gap and NOT a pass. It belongs to the items 1 and 2 lane and needs an authorized `--wet` run.
