body:
Draft — native body lowering: a braced arm body that opens with a `let`

Manager assignment (sleek-owl-397 approved), DESIGN §6b method. Three native body-lowering gaps that
refuse at native normalize on plain main, each keeping the parse_int wave on its fallback for that file.

## Attribution (one line each, as asked)

| fixture | reason | attribution |
|---|---|---|
| `gunbc/machine_intake/mtcollins1_boot_run.dag:408:29` | `body_lowering_reason_return_not_in_tail_position` | **correct refusal, not touched.** A `return` statement that ends a spine is not a value; the fold already refuses it by name. |
| `dag/gunbc/instruments/fabric_control_plane_live_probe.dag:1053:3` | `body_lowering_reason_let_body_not_reachable_from_node` | **producer: `body_lower_block_value_lowered`'s sole-statement fallback.** |
| `dag/gunbc/instruments/compute_run_unit_cold.dag:97:7` | `normalized_tree_reason_wrapper_retention_not_normalized` | **same producer.** |

Gaps 2 and 3 share one producer. A braced arm body (`=> { let …; … }`) is a term-position `block_expr`
delegating to `fn_body` (`dag_grammar_block_expr_expr`, `src/v2/extdeps/languages/dag.dag:2165-2166`, which delegates to `^dag_production_fn_body`) — the arm-body production itself is
`stmt stmt*` with no braces (`dag_grammar_match_arm_stmt_body_expr`, `src/v2/extdeps/languages/dag.dag:2282-2285`), so the braces arrive as an
expression statement. `body_lower_block_value_lowered` (`src/v2/compiler/body_lowering_fold.dag:5627`)
walks the spine, and when the spine has a single statement its fallback read the block **head** with
`body_lower_value_read`. A `let` head goes to `body_lower_let_expr` (`:8815`), which refuses on both arms —
no `let` is a value, the `in` form left the grammar — so the block's own body was never lowered and the
fold reported `let_body_not_reachable_from_node`. Where the block was not recognised at all, the fold kept
the `fn_body` shell and normalization reported `wrapper_retention_not_normalized`. Both are the same
earliest unjustifiable output: a statement `let` reached a value reader.

## The fix (one fold function, plus its cause row)

`body_lower_tail_statement_read` (`:13075`) already refuses a spine-ending `return` by name. It now also
matches a spine-ending statement `let` and refuses it with its own cause,
`^body_lowering_reason_statement_let_in_tail_position`, instead of falling through to
`body_lower_value_read`; and `body_lower_block_value_lowered`'s sole-statement fallback calls
`body_lower_tail_statement_read` rather than reading the head as a value. Sibling leaves of the same rule
were checked: the match-arm non-empty body (`:7984`) and the statement spine (`:9179`) already route through
`tail_statement_read`, so they get the new refusal for free and needed no separate arm.

No widening, no new fallback, and neither source file was edited to dodge a refusal.

* `src/v2/compiler/body_lowering_fold.dag` — the fold change.
* `src/v2/workflow/compile_door_cause_ownership.dag` — the CauseOwnership row for the new cause (lane
  `SharedSelfCriticalPath`), so it is a registered cause with an owner rather than a bare string.

## Fixtures

15 corpus files `src/v2/test/fixture/namespace_xl0/lst_*.dag`, one module each, driven by the claim module
`src/v2/test/claim/namespace_xl0/let_statement_position.dag`:

* positives (must lower today): `ctl_body_let`, `ctl_arm_expr`, `ctl_arm_block`, `ctl_if_branch`, `ctl_fn_value`
* REDs (refuse today, must lower with the fix): `tail_let`, `tail_let_after_let`, `tail_let_match`,
  `arm_block_let`, `arm_block_two_let`, `arm_tail_let`, plus the two gap-shaped ones —
  `lst_arm_block_if_match` (the `fabric_control_plane_live_probe` shape: `let chosen = if c { match … } else { match … }`
  as the first statement of a braced arm block) and `lst_if_match_branch` (the sibling leaf: braced `if`
  branches at term position)
* undeclared-atom probes (must still refuse, so the fix cannot be a widening): `tail_let_und`, `arm_rest_und`

One correction worth stating rather than burying: the fixtures first carried their header note as `-- `
lines. `--` is not a comment in the lexer (a line comment opens at `/` `/`,
`v2.extdeps.languages.dag dag_line_comment_annotation_rule`), so that text sat unlexable ahead of the
module line, `module_header_read` settled `ModuleHeaderAbsent`, and the layout inventory refused every
fixture with `no module line` — no fixture reached body lowering at all. Fixed in 5b7dcf39451 (and in
ff79787a38c on the RED baseline). The claim module's embedded `data … _source` strings begin at `module`
and were never affected; the census lane reads the files, so only that lane saw it.

## Evidence (bounded witnesses on the real path; filled in as runs finish)

Heads under test: fix `44cc9287dfd`, RED baseline `b73fdbbd8c9` — the same tree with the fixtures, the claim
module and the layout row but **no fold change**, so RED is authored before the fix rather than inferred from
it. The witness is one bounded label, `gunbc test
//v2/test/claim/namespace_xl0/let_statement_position:all` (19 rows, ~12–25 min per head, `gunbc run`-style
native route, seed recorded in the run log).

**Standing (ruling from tidy-ant-251, 2026-11-01): this PR stays draft, the boxes below stay unchecked, and
no evidence restatement is offered until the label can run.** Both heads refuse at `prepare` on walls this PR
does not touch and will not patch: `resolve_reason_unbound_symbol` on `Map` in three `dag/std/algebra.dag`
signatures (locus bytes 77075..77078; retyped to `FinitelySupportedFunction` by #14876), on `string_length`
(`src/v2/std/qualified_name.dag` bytes 13113..13126; egressed by #15507), and `first`
(`src/v2/std/node_query.dag` bytes 27473..27478; the egress lane). What is shown independently of those walls
stands: the new cause row is carried by the emitted compiler's own seed emit of `source_root_eval.dag`
(`~/sunny-bee-153-repro/seq26.log`), the 19 fixtures parse, and the RED baseline is an authored branch
(`b73fdbbd8c9`), not an inference.

* [ ] RED — the label at `b73fdbbd8c9`: the tail-let fixtures refuse, and the rows asserting
      `body_lowering_reason_statement_let_in_tail_position` fail while the positives pass.
* [ ] GREEN — the label at `44cc9287dfd`: those rows pass on the located cause; the five positive fixtures
      still lower; the undeclared-atom probes still refuse `resolve_reason_unbound_symbol`, so the fix did not
      absorb them.
* [ ] Gap files — each gap function gets a bounded witness of its own shape rather than a corpus delta:
      `lst_tail_let` / `lst_tail_let_after_let` / `lst_tail_let_match` (statement let in tail position),
      `lst_arm_tail_let` / `lst_arm_block_if_match` (the arm-block sibling leaf). #15511 corrects the fabric
      source directly.
* [x] `dag/gunbc/source_layout_namespaces.dag` is emitted, not hand-written: `layout_namespaces_emit` run at
      both heads (`gunbc run --source-root dag --source-root src/v2 --entry
      dag/gunbc/instruments/layout_migration.dag --function layout_namespaces_emit --arg report=…`), rc 0 at
      both, emitted bytes sha256 `f5bbf50f78cacf84e1dba1afd09a7c7f53ba2560f58e6d6c35d9ac035dbe9945` equal to
      the committed file and `git diff` empty after the emit at both heads (log `seq26.log`).
* [ ] Blocked, named rather than hidden: both label runs currently refuse before any row is adjudicated, on
      walls this PR does not create — (i) `resolve_reason_unbound_symbol @ dag/std/algebra.dag bytes
      77075..77078 "Map"` → `resolve_reason_declarer_refused` (N7 wall 2, which #14876 retypes), witness
      `seq33.log`; and (ii) at #14876's head, `cause=EmittedCompilerBuildFailed first_error=error[E0373]:
      closure may outlive the current function, but it borrows `e`` at
      `v2_std_demand_engine.rs:573:54`, emitted from that PR's new `src/v2/std/demand_engine.dag`
      (`demand_engine_seal` → `demand_engine_entries_mapped(e: e, f: fn(entry) { … e … })`), witness
      `seq36.log`.

**Retire-by-default note.** Earlier drafts of this body gated landing on full-corpus census runs (base vs fix
head, identity joins over `file_refusal` rows). Those gates are withdrawn: the bounded label above plus the
required CI (v2-bootstrap, heal) is the landing evidence. The census runs already executed stay as historical
receipts on the runner (`~/sunny-bee-153-repro/census_main.log`, `seq18.log`); they are not a prerequisite.
The placed hypothesis about `source_root_eval.dag`'s `declarer_refused` population was answered in that
lane's terms and came back negative (no `resolve_reason_declarer_refused` row at either head; 399 residual
identities at both, 395 with identical reason sets) — recorded here so nobody re-runs it.

## Out of scope

`uses_clause_unmodeled` (a correct refusal under D13) and `service_realization_argv_refused` (the
service-lowering item). `mtcollins1_boot_run.dag:408:29` stays refused.

body:
Native-serve request headers, plus a separate versioned contract for the locally patched Strata engine. This PR does not connect the router's S3 save path; that consumer is a declared frontier (`request_bound_save_consumer_frontier`).

## What lands
- Native request headers preserve order and duplicates (`ServeRequestHeader`); the native-serve instrument gains TCP probes and a modeled dispatch option.
- `extdeps.strata.session_file` is the upstream-only contract at its pin.
- `extdeps.strata.request_bound_save` is the patched engine's own identity (Strata `8183c6b6` plus `dag/extdeps/strata/patches/request-bound-save-8183c6b6.patch`). It owns `expected_request_id`, the 409 conditions and the echo. A stock 200 reply with no echo is the typed `BoundSaveEngineLacksPatch` refusal, never `SlotReplyUnreadable`.
- Witness `strata_request_bound_save_witness` covers that refusal, echo match, mismatch and duplicate, and the 409 conditions.

## Vendored patch: admitted temporary deviation, kept vendored
Operator ruling 2026-11-01, `gunbc.design_ruling vendored_strata_request_bound_save_patch_is_a_temporary_deviation`, admits the hand-applied patch. A second ruling the same day, `gunbc.design_ruling vendored_strata_patch_stays_unoffered_upstream`, supersedes its upstream-PR condition: the patch stays vendored, with no upstream issue or PR and nothing posted to Niko1221/Strata. Dissolution row `request_bound_save_patch_build_route` stands as "not yet offered upstream"; it ends when the operator decides to offer it upstream or an upstream equivalent lands. Condition 1 of the first ruling is met by this PR (own versioned module, typed refusal on stock Strata, dissolution row).

## Validation
- Native-header validation: [native-serve run 40852025306](https://github.com/gunb-ai/gunbc/actions/runs/40852025306) at 935806c0c47 held all 28 TCP requests including header and framing probes. This qualifies the transport prerequisite only.
- Patch tests, run on srv1 at 13:52Z with Python 3.12.3 and Strata's pinned requirements.txt: `python -m unittest serve.test_request_bound_save -v` gives 15/15 OK on 8183c6b6 plus the patch. Control, the same tests against unpatched server.py: FAILED (failures=19, errors=1).
- Real srv4 save/restore checks were synthetic, manual qualification and are not re-verified here.
- Slot-contract witnesses are queued on srv1; results pending.

## Not in this PR
Authenticated turn identity, placement/admission integration, grant retention through publication and recovery, and the srv4 enrollment prerequisites (two-device replica identity, observed owned supply, an attributable Strata launch reading). None is fabricated or bypassed.

## Reviewed upstream PR text, kept for whenever it is wanted (not posted)
Title: `[Engine] bind conditional session saves to completed responses`. Problem: a save writes whatever state the process holds, so a caller wanting one completed response's checkpoint cannot tell it was replaced. Change: optional `expected_request_id` on save; success echoes `request_id` only if the same native process still holds that response's state, else 409 `request_not_current`, `request_in_flight` or `engine_changed`; `error.published: true` means written but unverified. Omitting the field keeps current behavior. Strata's CONTRIBUTING asks for maintainer scope agreement first, so an issue would come before any PR.



## Unrelated riders
This PR also carries repo_self_build_environment_witness and an rfm receipt that are unrelated to the Strata identity work.

body:
## What

Ruling (tidy-ant-251, 2026-10-25): **a module-local declaration beats an ambient/kernel name in every position, type and value alike, and a type use's arity is the arity of the declaration it resolves to, never of its spelling.** Seed maintenance under `gunbc.v1.v1_maintenance_standing`: the seed silently binds one spelling to two declarations in one scope.

## Measured first, on main `88e8991e557` (seed built from that tree)

A module declaring its own `type List<T> = Nil | Cons { head: T, tail: List<T> }` (quick-stag-725's `gunbc.instruments.cons_tail_recursion_user_list` @ `e0d0c410c14`):

| shape | seed on main |
|---|---|
| non-generic local `type List = Nil \| Cons { head: Int, tail: List }` | refuses `type List expects 1 type arguments, got 0`: `tail: List` binds the kernel List |
| `fn kernel_literal() -> List<Int> { [1, 2] }` | **accepted**: the return type binds the kernel List; `Nil`/`Cons` in the same scope bind the local one |
| `fn local_nil() -> List<Int> { Nil }` | typechecks, but emits `-> Rc<Vec<i64>>` while the body builds the module enum |
| `fn keep(m: Map<String>) -> Map<String>` (std.types Map, 2 params) | **accepted** (warm-crane-888's RED) |

**v2** (the authority) is clean on the kernel-literal shape: `-> List<Int> { [1, 2] }` against a local List refuses `arrow_body_does_not_inhabit_declared_return`. On a local declaration plus an explicit import of the same name, the seed already refuses at the import, as the ruling requires.

## Chain (DESIGN §6b): five spelling-keyed links; this PR repairs three, as one rule

1. **`v1.compiler.resolve` `is_user_generic_use_site`** asked the use's *spelling*. It now asks whether the *resolved declaration* is a member of the container family by identity (`declaration_is_container_family` / `container_family_declaration`): `std.types` `List`/`Set`/`Map` (the declarations of the spellings that carry arity rows), `std.algebra` `FinitelySupportedFunction` (the keyed algebra), or the kernel mint of a container. `FreeMonoid`, `FinitePowerSet` and `PartialFunction` carry no arity row and stay user generics, as before.
2. **Arity was three partial rules.** `v1.compiler.normalize` refused a bare container by spelling *before any declaration is known*; resolve refused only bare or wrong *user* generics; a container-family use was minted from its own children with no arity check at all. Now there is **one rule**, `type_use_arity_diagnostics`, read from the resolved declaration (the kernel row's arity for a kernel mint). It applies to applied uses anywhere, to bare uses nested in a type, and to bare uses at the four field/parameter/return positions. Normalize's arm, `missing_generic_args_diagnostics` and the user-generic branch's own check are deleted. `alias_chain_arity_diagnostics`' `is_container_type` exemption is deleted too.
3. *(shared with 2)* Wrong-arity container-alias use: now refused, located.
   **One class too:** infer's `alias_chain_arity_diagnostics` re-reported the same fact at the same span as `TypeArgumentArityMismatch`. Measured on main for a user generic: both diagnostics appear. It had no position of its own once resolve covered container aliases (parameter, return, `let` annotation, alias carrier and cast target all refuse at resolve first), so the rule is deleted. Its `TypeArgumentArityMismatch` enum row STAYS (declared, unproduced): deleting a
   public diagnostic variant is not a one-step change — heal bootstraps its regenerator from the base commit's
   mirrors, so a head that drops the hand-carried `cli_run/compile_clean.rs` arm with the row cannot build on the
   mixed tree (E0004; heal 40558793178), and regen cannot run. The variant is deleted by its own migration commit,
   later. `test.claim.type_argument_arity_witness` asserts the one class, `ArityMismatch`.
   **One lookup per use** (DESIGN §6, warm-crane-888's review): `resolve_node_at` resolves a use's declaration once and hands it to both the arity rule and the structure arm. An applied user generic used to cost two lookups (`is_user_generic_use_site`, then the branch again); now it costs one. Root positions go through `resolve_type_position` rather than a second check.
4. **Not here:** the inhabitance judgment of a kernel *mint* against a module-local *declaration*. That needs the kernel-carrier relation (valiant-badger-855's kernel-Int crossing PR, after #14769, not yet opened). PR B (sunny-deer-180) deliberately leaves mixed pairs undecided. Pinned below.
5. **Not here:** the Rust emitter's spelling lowering (`node_is_collection` / `is_declared_container_alias_spelling`), #13936 (wise-lark-652). Pinned below.

## Evidence: `test.claim.module_local_type_binds_witness`, 6/6 on this tree (seed sha256 `aa2c889057d84d8e…`)

- climb: a module-local non-generic `List` binds its own declaration (field and return)
- control: a module-local generic `List` typechecks
- climb: `Map<String>` refuses (`type Map expects 2 type arguments, got 1`, located) beside the `Map<String, Int>` control
- preserved: a bare kernel `List` still refuses, at the root and nested (`List<List>`), now from resolve's declaration arity, not normalize's spelling
- **PIN** `pin_the_seed_still_accepts_a_kernel_list_as_a_local_list_until_kernel_carrier_relation_test`: asserts today's acceptance; retires (goes red, then flipped) with the kernel-carrier relation
- **PIN** `pin_the_emitter_still_lowers_a_local_list_by_spelling_until_13936_test`: asserts today's `Rc<Vec<i64>>`; retires with #13936

Ledger: a receipt on `emitter_keyed_container_lowering_is_keyed_by_leaf_spelling`. The resolver half of its trigger is met; the emitter half is not, so the rung doesn't move. warm-crane-888's row `a_wrong_arity_use_of_a_container_alias_is_silently_accepted` lives in #15118; it climbs when both have landed.

## Out of scope, named

Over-application of a declaration that declares no parameters (`Int<String>`, a local non-generic `List<Int>`) is still silent, and that predates this PR. `declared_type_parameter_count` answers 0 for a kernel mint that isn't a container (e.g. the kernel `Optional`), so refusing 0-declared vs n-supplied would refuse legitimate kernel uses. Its trigger is the kernel-carrier relation stating what a mint declares. Same class as `a_wrong_arity_use_of_a_container_alias_is_silently_accepted`.

## Behaviour change to watch, and why this is a draft

The one kernel *container* name the corpus redeclares is **`v2.std.witness` `Witness<C> = Holds | Violates`**: 297 uses across 146 importers in the self-host closure. On main the seed resolves them by spelling to the kernel `Witness` container. Under this rule they bind v2's own coproduct, which is the ruling's intent, but the emitter still lowers `Witness` by spelling. **`v2-bootstrap` (self-host + v2-native-cli) on this head is the decisive check**, followed by a per-module census (every module, main vs this head, NEW 0). This stays a draft until both are in.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Census of `Node.params` reads in `v1.compiler.resolve` (side-chat finding on `9d9674cfc1ad`, item 3)

`Node.params` carries two different facts (the helper's own comment states it): a type declaration's TYPE-parameter
list, and an Arrow's callable VALUE-parameter types. All 34 raw reads at this head are classified (line numbers are
this branch's `src/v1/04_resolve.dag`). Every read that asks "how many type parameters does this declaration declare"
of a RESOLVED declaration goes through `declaration_type_parameters(decl:)` — that is the helper body itself (`:614`,
the `Arrow => []` rule) and, after this PR, exactly two consumers: `resolve_paramless_generic_use_decl_with_children`
(`:476`, the retry filter — the finding's fix) and `is_parametric_type_alias_decl` (`:673`).

**Structural copies — 23** (params moved unchanged through a node rebuild; no arity question asked):
`:305` with_authored_identity, `:678` resolve_nominal_alias_rhs, `:774 :789 :797 :828 :836 :843 :908 :922`
resolve_node_bounded_structure rebuilds, `:1059` stamp_kernel_collection, `:1064 :1066` rendered_use_site_type,
`:1395` stamp_collections_in_reference, `:1442` reference_argument_with_declaration, `:1454`
reference_param_with_declaration, `:1482` node_with_declaration, `:1522` binder_marked_param, `:1532 :1534`
binder_marked_member, `:1612 :1623 :1630` resolve_item_types child/field/variant rebuilds.

**Arrow value-parameter walks — 6** (params ARE value parameters at these sites; routing them through the helper
would erase what they read, returning `[]`): `:728` resolve_node_bounded_structure resolving an application's
parameter nodes, `:928` `n_is_callable` (callability is an Arrow fact), `:1333` fn_type_param_names (filters
`T: T`-shaped value params out of an fn header — its own pre-resolution header, not a resolved use), `:1420`
reference_tree_with_declaration `if is_arrow { map(n.params, …) }`, `:1503` binder_marked_type (same shape),
`:1558` resolve_item_types resolving a callable's value params.

**Shape tests on unresolved nodes — 3** (`params |> count == 0` as "is this a bare reference", not "how many type
parameters"): `:585` node_is_type_use_shape (guarded by `connective == NoConnective` first, so no Arrow case exists),
`:1413` reference_tree_with_declaration and `:1496` binder_marked_type binder-reference shapes. These run before any
declaration is resolved; there is no resolved declaration to route them through.

**Header name scan — 1**: `:1544` resolve_item_types' `item.connective != NoConnective && item.transport == none`
branch — the fn header scanning its own value params for `fn f<T>(T: T)`-style collision names. Routed through the
helper it would return `[]` and silently delete the bound-twice refusal (`first_duplicate_type_param_name` below it);
this is the pre-resolution header, and no claim currently pins that refusal — noted here rather than asserted.

The mutation this census guards: at `:476` with the raw read restored, the retry-path pair goes red at
`a_paramless_primary_in_front_of_a_fn_type_alias_sibling_keeps_the_paramless_declaration` (the Arrow's value params
count as one type parameter, the retry selects the alias) and green at its sibling
`a_paramless_primary_in_front_of_a_generic_sibling_still_selects_it`.

## Witness receipt at the current head

**RED**, measured twice at a tree equal to `6edbdff0567` in all non-mirror files (first at `1b8b3de518b` before the
insertion-order fix, whose only delta was the enum-row placement in `00_core.dag`) with the **main-built** binary
(`gunbc` from main `0660b69843b`, sha256 `3a29de9da5a7…`; second run main `c384c4e561b`, sha256 `7f77a2e91be4…`;
GITHUB_SHA=head): `module_local_type_binds_witness` refuses (exit 1) at
`a_module_local_non_generic_list_binds_its_own_declaration` (the module's own `type List` never binds),
`a_wrong_arity_container_alias_use_refuses` (Map<String> still accepted), and
`a_bare_function_type_alias_binds_and_a_bare_generic_one_refuses` (a fn-type alias's Arrow is mistaken for a
parameterized declaration) — while the retry pair's sibling arm
`a_paramless_primary_in_front_of_a_generic_sibling_still_selects_it` PASSES (the pair is discriminating).
`type_argument_arity_witness` control rc=0 on the same runs (no regression from this PR's rule deletion).

**GREEN** (head-built binary after the regen commit, mirrors at candidate sha256s `fe6ece27d2da…`
`v1_compiler_infer_resolve.rs`, `7c574619fa07…` `v1_std_core.rs`): every arm of both witnesses PASS, exit 0 — filled
below when the regen commit lands.
title: seed resolve: a type use binds the declaration it resolves to; one declaration-keyed arity rule

body:
NAMESPACE-XL: `map_keys` gets its one declared home, `std.algebra` `fn map_keys<K, V>(m: Map<K, V>) -> FreeMonoid<K>`, the map's key support. This is a root-coordinator decision by sleek-owl-397 (one ambient name, one declared home). The `std.primitives` `map_keys_contract` row is retired in the same head as the generated import sweep, atomically, as #14751 did for `list_push`.

## Update at 237b71c69825: merged main (#15415 and #15428 doctrine)

- **Census files follow main's deletion.** #15428 deleted `gunbc.instruments.{ambient_name_census_reading, ambient_operation_disposition_reading, namespace_wave_binding_diff, namespace_wave_binding_shard, namespace_wave_occurrence_join}`. Each was a modify/delete conflict, resolved to the deletion. The sweep's `map_keys` additions to them are therefore gone.
- **Generated mirror.** `src/v1/stage0/src/std_algebra.rs` takes main's bytes, and heal regenerates it; no bytes are hand-resolved.
- **Acceptance (tidy-ant-251 ruling, 2026-10-31):**
  - the `map_keys` home, i.e. the delegate seam;
  - this PR's own bounded REDs and controls (the receipts below);
  - v2-bootstrap.

  The d0 four-surface identity join (`primitive_d0_map_keys_four_surface_join_exit`) is **no longer landing evidence**, per `gunbc.design_ruling bad_process_is_worse_than_no_process`.
- **The `let` workaround.** `v2.compiler.occurrence_resolution_census` `occurrence_resolution_partial` is **still on main**: #15428 deferred the v2 census modules to #15423. So the `let` and its marker (citing `gunbc.recurring_failure_mode` `by_ref_primitive_over_a_generic_call_argument_infers_from_the_borrow`) stay for now. The marker becomes moot when #15423 deletes the module, or when #15509 lands and the `let` unwinds.
- **The RFM row and RED fixture pair stay.** The by-ref class is real, and the pair is the RED for crisp-bee-97's #15509. It flips to expect-success when #15509 lands.

## What changes

- **The home.** `dag/std/algebra.dag` declares `map_keys` beside `map_insert` and `empty_map`.
  - It is a HostRealizedSeam self-call (the `list_push` / `std.host_text` `chars` shape).
  - `std.primitive_projection` carries its row `primitive_map_keys -> std.algebra map_keys, HostRealizedSeam`. The `primitive_map_keys` identity moves into `std.primitive_projection` beside the other projected identities, and `std.primitive_identity` imports it.
  - The declaration carries its **dissolution note**: the home is `std.algebra` for now, and if #14876 moves Map's operations onto FinitelySupportedFunction's own home, `map_keys` moves with them.
- **The contract is retired.** The `map_keys_contract` block and its `primitive_contract_roster` slot are deleted, not aliased. `builtin_registry_surface_names` still lists `map_keys`, because v1's seed path resolves through it.
  - No `rung_drop` is needed. Unlike `list_push` and `chars`, no cost fact is lost: `std.primitive_identity` `primitive_map_keys_cost`, a PrimitiveCostFact keyed by identity, already models it.
- **The fold** (wise-moth-707's escalation answer, DESIGN §3, one fact one name). `std.algebra` `map_support_keys` was a second name for the same key support (`m |> map_keys`). It is deleted, and its 10 importers now call `map_keys`; each edit changes only the spelling.
  - **`v2.compiler.infer` is among them, and it is load-bearing.** Its two call sites (`fold_list(xs: map_keys(m: …))`) are the only lines that change there. Its closure receipt is below.
  - The other importers: `v2.compiler.{occurrence_binding_census, source_root_eval, value_use_dependency}`, `gunbc.compile_diagnostic_census`, `std.source_annotation`, and three v2 claims.
- **The roster row.** `roster_head_rows` gains `map_keys -> std.algebra` with `head: KeepHead`.
- **`gunbc.primitive_egress`:**
  - The `dispositions_collection` `map_keys` evidence row now names the declared authority.
  - The d0 join `primitive_d0_map_keys_five_surface_join_holds` becomes `primitive_d0_map_keys_four_surface_join_holds`. It now also asserts that the PrimitiveContractRow surface carries **no** `map_keys` row, so the ambient authority reappearing turns it red. The five-surface form failed by execution once the contract was retired.
- **Stage0 mirrors** (`std_primitive_projection.rs`, `std_algebra.rs`) were hand-seeded once, as in #14751. The heal job owns them from here.
  - Without the projection row the seam emits as self-recursion.
  - At the merge with main, `std_algebra.rs` was a GeneratedArtifactConcurrentDivergence. It is main's bytes plus exactly this PR's two hunks (`map_keys` added, `map_support_keys` removed). Heal convergence on this PR is the oracle.

### Divergence, stated (§3b)

The brief said to follow the `*_primitive_delegate` pattern of `map_insert` / `empty_map`. This PR uses the same-name HostRealizedSeam instead, like `list_push` and `chars`. The reason:
- The existing interpreter arm `free_call.map_keys` / `method_call.map_keys` and the existing `extdeps.languages.rust.emit` `rt_function_registry` row `map_keys -> map_keys` already realize the seam.
- A delegate pair would need a new primitive identity, a new `v1_map_grounding_arms` arm, a generated dispatch row, and new `authored_spelling` / `spelling_alias` rows. Every one of those is keyed by spelling, which widens the residue `gunbc.recurring_failure_mode` `host_seam_realization_is_keyed_by_primitive_spelling`.
- The same-name seam needs no new Rust.

The bridge and the homonym control below show that the self-call is intercepted by the declaration's projection row, not by its spelling.

## The generated import sweep

`v2.workflow.roster_import_sweep` `roster_import_sweep_apply_row_exit` ran with `home=std.algebra`, `call=map_keys`. It is row-scoped, so no other name moves.
- **Population:** the 48 files on main with a code occurrence of `map_keys` (49 more mention it only in comments or strings).
- **Where it ran:** 2-file shards plus single-file shards on BuildBuddy amd64. Each shard used a detached worktree of `59bc7a19aa76` with a seed built from that tree in a private `--target-dir`, hashed before and after.
- **Convergence:** each shard then re-ran `roster_import_sweep_row_exit` over its own paths and returned 0.
- **Result:** 19 modules gain `map_keys` in their `std.algebra` import, including the gate tip's instruments `gunbc.instruments.{ambient_name_census_reading, ambient_operation_disposition_reading, namespace_wave_binding_diff, namespace_wave_binding_shard, namespace_wave_occurrence_join, native_emission_controls}`.
- **Excluded, following #14751** (main still carries bare `list_push` in ten `src/v1` sources):
  - `src/v1/**`: seed sources, resolved by v1's builtin registry, not the v2 contract tier.
  - `fixtures/fixture_closure_rustc/empty_map_data_turbofish_probe.dag`: seed-compiled, and its import list is the fixture.
- **Refusals:**
  - `src/v1/03_resolve.dag` (parse-refused): excluded above anyway.
  - `src/v2/test/claim/callexec/synthetic_facts_key_collision.dag` (normalize-refused): it already imports `map_keys` through the fold, and the claim passes.
- `dag/gunbc/roadmap/roadmap_belt_actuate.dag` (16k lines, 2 bare calls) exceeded BuildBuddy's 45-minute cap, so it ran on srv1 via sleek-owl-397.
  - Isolated clone at `d159a9f1338c`, seed sha256 `17ea2624…8fa` before and after.
  - The apply returned rc 0 with exactly one line, `import std.algebra { trim, skip, map_keys }`, and the convergence census returned rc 0.
  - Commit `cb30069376b6`.

## Executed evidence

Nothing on the required path executes witnesses (`gunbc.rung_drop` `v1_required_lanes_withdrawn`), so these runs are the execution evidence. Receipts on head `1e8b95c9fdb2`. Each dispatch used a detached worktree with 0 dirty paths and a seed built there in a private `--target-dir`; its sha256 was identical before and after the run.

| Run | Seed sha256 | Result |
|---|---|---|
| r1 | `1f67bc00…b011` | `map_keys_without_the_declared_import_refuses_at_resolve` **true**, `surviving_sibling_contract_row_still_binds_at_resolve` **true** |
| r2 | `0a701e8f…1d19` | `declared_import_of_the_home_binds_where_ambient_refuses` **false**, `consumer_call_shapes_bind_through_the_declared_import` **false** (see the blocker below) |
| r3 | `bde71de0…a5f` | `consumer_call_shapes_refuse_without_the_declared_import` **true**, `w_algebra_map_keys_reaches_the_bridge` **true**, `w_homonym_map_keys_keeps_authored_body` **true** |
| r4 | `34e15a5b…fde3` | `--claim-run` rc 0: `map_keys_home_witness`, `primitive_identity_join_witness`, `primitive_modeled_cost_witness`, `primitive_runtime_body_witness`, `primitive_projection_authority_witness`, `value_use_dependency`, `synthetic_facts_key_collision` |
| r5 | `b1ae68e3…b3b8` | `let_binder_frame` rc 1 (the 3 FAILs pre-exist on main), `gunbc compile --entry src/v2/compiler/infer.dag --target rust` rc 0 (the `v2.compiler.infer` closure receipt) |

### Blocker on the positive: #14876

With the import, the positive refuses as `resolve_reason_declarer_refused`, not as unbound. This is not specific to this declaration:
- In the same harness, `import std.algebra { map_insert }` (the delegate form) and `{ map_lookup }` (an ordinary fn) refuse identically, with reasons `resolve_reason_unbound_symbol, resolve_reason_declarer_refused`.
- The cause is that `std.algebra` has no binding for `Map` under v2. `std.types` imports `std.algebra`, so the reverse import would be a cycle, and every Map-typed `std.algebra` declaration is refused there.
- #14876 retypes that surface to `FinitelySupportedFunction`.

The positive and `consumer_call_shapes_bind_through_the_declared_import` therefore stay red until #14876 lands. The RED (unbound without the import) and the `map_values` control discriminate today.

### `v2-bootstrap`: E0308 in emitted `v2_compiler_occurrence_binding_census.rs`, blocked on the by-ref lowering

- **The failing line.** Every Map seam is lowered at its call site to its bridge. `map_keys`'s row is `passes_by_ref: true`, so line 440 (`map_keys(m: fold_list(..., empty: empty_map(), ...))`) emits `Rc::new(v1_rt::map_keys(&crate::std_algebra::fold_list(..., v1_rt::rc_empty_map::<_, _>(), ...)))`.
- **Why it fails.** rustc does not deref-coerce `&Rc<HashMap<_,_>>` to `&HashMap<K,V>` while those generics are still open. On main the call went through the typed `map_support_keys` fn.
- **Why the delegate pair would not help.** `map_insert` is lowered the same way, to `v1_rt::rc_map_insert(...)` on the same line. It compiles only because its bridge is by-value.
- **Ruling (relayed by wise-moth-707): B, not A.**
  - `v1.compiler.emit_rust` generalizes the by-ref Map bridge lowering, which also deletes the `rc_list_push` by-value leaf. That fixes every by-ref Map bridge at once: `map_keys`, `map_values`, `sorted_map_keys`, `lookup`, `map_get` and `map_contains_key`.
  - It is clever-crane-830's lane (Manager 2), which has this receipt and mechanism.
  - This PR adds no Rust bridge.

## Status: HOLD (draft)

This PR lands only after both blockers are in:
1. **The emit_rust by-ref lowering (B, clever-crane-830).** It clears the `v2-bootstrap` E0308.
2. **#14876, the Map binding in v2.** It turns the positive and `consumer_call_shapes_bind_through_the_declared_import` green.

After both land: merge main, re-run the receipts above on the new head, and confirm `v2-bootstrap` is green.

## Consumer (§3c)

The gate tip's instrument call sites on `gate/namespace-tip` (owner wise-moth-707) call `map_keys` positionally with no import. The sweep above gives them the import, and the tip imports the home.

## Compute route

body:
Serves the v2 self-host program on the N7 critical path: the seed must resolve a Map<..> annotation through its import to the declaration it names, so that std.algebra's FinitelySupportedFunction can be the one Map concept without the seed emitting a kernel-Map-vs-FSF crossing at every consumer (operator Map ruling A). This is the atomic cutover: seed fix and std.algebra retype land together because neither half is green alone.

## What the diff actually does, keyed on what each part decides (DESIGN §4b)
- **std.algebra retype (the crossing).** `dag/std/algebra.dag`'s Map-spelled surface is retyped to `FinitelySupportedFunction`, the declaration it means. No `import std.types { Map }` is possible (`std.types` imports `std.algebra`; DESIGN §3 makes import-graph acyclicity the only structural law), so the crossing is made by spelling the target declaration, not by importing the alias.
- **Seed: the kernel keyed-container admission is UNCHANGED in what it decides.** Where a `Map<K, V>` annotation is admitted as the kernel keyed container, the predicate asked is `node_is_keyed_algebra_spelling` (main's, from PR #14880) and it compares `container_template_algebra` on the **last segment of the authored name** — a leaf-spelling check. This PR does not key that decision on a declaration, and does not claim to: `gunbc.recurring_failure_mode.emitter_keyed_container_lowering_is_keyed_by_leaf_spelling` names the declaration-keyed hardening as its next rung. An alias settling to that declaration is what makes an imported `Map` and a directly spelled `FinitelySupportedFunction` meet at a join as one type (witness `a_map_aliasing_the_keyed_algebra_joins_its_declaration_as_one_type`).
- **Seed: the added refusal is a VISIBILITY refusal, not a declaration lookup.** `unimported_map_diagnostics` (`src/v1/04_resolve.dag`) refuses a built-in container spelling the module does not have in its own visible names, judged through the existing `import_visible_name` predicate the unlisted-import check already reads (one fact, one place). It is deliberately able to fire where the spelling resolves somewhere in the corpus — `global_bare_lookup` can still bind an unimported name — which is why it is NOT named as an unbound/declaration predicate. Its harm direction is refuse-only: it concatenates one error node and can never render a look-alike as the built-in. The spelling roster it consults is `map_builtin_spelling`.
- **Carriers.** `gunbc.design_ruling` row declaring kernel `Map` the host realization of `FinitelySupportedFunction` (operator default approval of the escalation, recommended by sleek-owl-397); the `gunbc.recurring_failure_mode` row above with its leaf-spelling census as an identity join over a named population; the `AmbientNameHome` row for `Map` (home `std.types`, `ExistingDeclaration`).
- **Witnesses.** `test.claim.map_annotation_resolves_by_declaration_witness`: positive control (an imported `Map` is inhabited by the declaration's own target type), discriminating RED (the same bytes minus the import edge refuse), join-as-one-type, and the look-alike-record refusal. Plus the element-type join REDs in `test.claim.parameterized_alias_settles_by_declaration_witness` (`Map<String, Int>` beside `FinitelySupportedFunction<String, Bool>` must refuse at the join), which is also the check that a regeneration took.

## Status
The Map import wave has landed on main, so the corpus this branch is merged against already imports `Map` where it uses it; the draft-blocked-on-the-wave note is obsolete. Remaining red is bootstrap-only and known: heal's round 1 builds the regenerator from the head's checked-in `stage0` mirrors rather than the base commit's whole crate (fix in #15339, crisp-bee-97), so the retyped `std.algebra` mirror fails to compile with E0308/E0282 until a regen with a buildable regenerator lands. Mirrors are regenerated, never hand-edited (DESIGN §3, §5).

## Follow-up, named and NOT widened here (DESIGN §6b breadth fork)
"A name that global-bare lookup reaches but the module never imported must be named in the module's import list" is, in today's seed, enforced **per spelling**. Fork census, derived by reading the two predicates that gate it: `bare_free_call_requires_listed_import` (a free-call spelling, one leaf: `trim`) and `map_builtin_spelling` (a built-in container spelling, one leaf: `Map`, added by this PR). Both then ask the same visibility predicate, `import_visible_name`. Two sibling `"trim"` / `"Map"` comparisons exist elsewhere and are NOT part of this fork: `rust_host_string_op_fn_emit` (v1.compiler.emit_rust) selects a host string-op body by spelling, and `expected_type_is_keyed_collection` (v1.compiler.infer) admits a keyed-collection expected type. Neither asks whether a name was imported.

Why `map_builtin_spelling` is not simply deleted in favour of `import_visible_name` alone (§6b "should be generalized, but not now"): `import_visible_name` is the shared predicate for *all* bare names, so dropping the spelling test from the refusal would refuse **every** unimported global-bare name corpus-wide. That is a different behavior change with its own census (which corpus modules currently rely on global-bare reach, per name), and it is not this PR's subject -- the Map crossing does not need it. Why it is not keyed on the resolved declaration either: measured, the refusal is a visibility judgment and an unimported name still binds through `global_bare_lookup`; keying it on a declaration would invert it, because the case it exists to catch is a declaration reachable globally that this module never named in its import list.

The general rule does not belong in either leaf: it belongs at **`global_bare_lookup`'s own visibility** -- one judgment about whether a bare name may bind at all from outside the module's declared imports, with no per-spelling roster anywhere. Growing this PR to cover more spellings would mean adding leaves to the same fork, which is the wrong direction, so it stays at two. Routed to tidy-ant-251's lane as a follow-up (owner of the general visibility rule at `global_bare_lookup`): the namespace cut retires import-list visibility anyway, which dissolves the fork rather than completing it. The `gunbc.recurring_failure_mode` row counts `map_builtin_spelling` among its six open leaf-spelling probes **on purpose** -- declaring it solved while it still decides on spelling would be rung inflation (DESIGN §4b), and its harm is bounded honestly: the roster's only effect is to concatenate one error node, so it can refuse a spelling but can never render a look-alike as the built-in.

## Motivating RED, measured on main (current)
The refusal this PR's retype clears is live on main, not historical. Measured by silent-raven-360 (run `raven-ctl-1`, srv1) at main `586fea37d8d0` and corroborated byte-wise at `586fea37d8d0` and `30bd214ede45`: both control claims (`test.claim.infer_optional_at_required_witness`, `test.claim.free_monoid_structure_bound`) exit 2 — `refused at prepare cause=resolve_reason_declarer_refused`, chain `resolve_reason_unbound_symbol` @ `dag/std/algebra.dag` on the occurrence `Map` → `unbound_symbol` → `declarer_refused` at `module_roots_from_source_root_ingest` / `fmi_assemble`. The unbound occurrence is the **return annotation** of `fn empty_map<K, V>() -> Map<K, V>`, i.e. the emitted compiler's own prepare resolving `std.algebra` during claim adjudication — the declared-return-type render path, which this branch routes through the existing keyed-collection arm of the emitter so the retyped spelling lowers to the same host table as its callers. Run logs: srv1 `~/raven1b.out`. The alias settlement that briefly suggested this premise was obsolete did **not** clear it; the controls still refuse (manager-3 correction, measured).

Cycle constraint on the fix: `import std.types { Map }` into `std.algebra` is impossible (`std.types` imports `std.algebra`), and DESIGN §3 makes acyclicity the import graph's only structural law — so the crossing is cleared by retyping the `Map`-spelled surface in `std.algebra` to the declaration it names, `FinitelySupportedFunction`, which is what this branch does.



## `map_support_values` dissolution
`std.algebra` `map_support_values` (review 88909) reads the ambient `std.primitives` `map_values_contract`, a dying root; retired when `map_values` is homed in `std.algebra` as a HostRealizedSeam and its contract retired by the generated import sweep (the #15164 shape), after #15164 lands; `map_support_values` then reads that home.



## Heal state at 6e3a53f55df6 (inference, not a measurement)
Heal run 41438208510 fails required-regen with 1447 hard diagnostics, 449 of them `unresolved type 'Map'` across about 40 files: this PR's unimported-Map refusal firing where the Map import wave has not applied. The wave lands first.
The `'Required' undefined` (src/v1/04_types.dag, 05_emit.dag) and `'Text' unresolved` (05_emit.dag) lines are INFERRED to be cascade from that refusal (a hard-refused module leaves no registry rows or imports), not red on main: src/v1/05_emit.dag is byte-identical to main here, and heal passed on #15638 and #15641 with the same file and the same required-regen step. Expected to clear when the wave lands; not yet confirmed by a run.
